description: The no-till seeder machinery has been developed to support Morocco's national plan of having one million hectares of farming land under Conservation Agriculture practices by 2030 (Generation Green 2020-2030). Developed from a local prototype by an ICARDA, INRA and local manufacturer team, using technology imported from dryland farming machinery in Australia, the no-till (zero tillage) seeder allows smallholder farmers in Morocco to sow seeds directly into the soil (direct seed) without causing any mechanical modification of the soil structure. No-till practices are expected to improve the resilience of dryland smallholder farmers by reducing soil erosion and increasing the amount of carbon dioxide, water, and organic matter retained in the soil.
title: No-till seeder adapted in public-private partnership to Moroccan crops and soil types for Moroccan smallholder farmers to practice zero tillage Conservation Agriculture

description: The on-farm Water, Energy, Food, and Carbon footprint (WEFC) nexus index has been developed to enable the quantitative assessment of on-farm integrated resources management in wheat and faba bean farming systems in Egypt. The WEFC index is computed as the weighted arithmetic average of the four pillars of (1) water: on-farm saved water consumption/national maximum water consumption; (2) energy: on-farm saved energy consumption/national maximum energy consumption; (3) food: on-farm agricultural yield/national maximum yield; and (4) carbon dioxide (CO2): on-farm saved CO2 emissions/national maximum CO2 emissions. The WEFC nexus index values are, therefore, indicative of resource consumption (inputs) and agricultural production and CO2 emissions (outputs). The index can be used to quantitatively assess the nexus performance of site-specific packages of practices under certain conditions and quantify the impact of new interventions on the nexus status to drive transformative actions at the farm level.

description: The Agroecology initiative aims to contribute to achieving agroecological transition through developing and scaling a range of innovations in 8 countries across three continents. It proposes to do so by using a participatory action-research approach involving the key stakeholders of the Agroecological Living Landscapes (ALLs), multi-stakeholder territorial spaces in each country on which the Initiative targets its transformation and innovation efforts. A major pillar of such an approach consists in codesigning the required innovations and corresponding processes as well as effecting the required changes in behavior/practices by the concerned actors. At the heart of the initiative’s ambition and approach lies the ability to mobilize and support ALL stakeholders in co-designing and implementing the diverse activities required to develop the innovations needed in each context. Hence, the initiative has designed a tool to support this process.
title: Integration of research and innovation processes that facilitate the co-design and testing of context-specific agroecological innovations:  A process for stakeholder engagement in Agroecological Living Landscapes ​

description: The RVF tool is a collaborative effort between the One Health Initiative and the Digital Innovation Initiative, designed to analyze climate-epidemic interactions and support decision-making for Rift Valley Fever (RVF) outbreak prevention and control in the Greater Horn of Africa. It includes a decision-support system for managing RVF epizootics, enabling timely and effective responses, and integrates a disease information management system for efficient data compilation and dissemination. The tool enhances disease surveillance in high-risk areas by combining trapping systems with community reports and supports cost-effectiveness studies on RVF prevention strategies, informing contingency planning. It provides meteorological data, including rainfall and precipitation at county and sub-county levels, and incorporates RVF modeling for risk assessment. Additionally, it serves as a key resource for prevention and control efforts, featuring an online news bulletin that enables users to generate customized scientific advisories with geospatial visualizations and professional reports.

description: Climate adaptation processes can be uneven and reinforce inequitable power relations and outcomes. In dairy households of Nandi and Bomet counties in Kenya, despite women’s significant labor contributions, gender norms limit women’s access to resources and decision-making agency. Rather than top-down, one-size-fits-all solutions, adaptation must prioritize flexible, locally led approaches tailored to diverse capacities of households and groups with differential access to resources and opportunities. Our innovation combines two inclusive approaches, scaling with households and champions in groups to enhance women's capacities to learn, lead and scale adaptation. The first approach works with households as part of the Pioneer Positive Deviance (P-PD) approach to scale farmer-led solutions developed by “adaptation pioneer households” (APHs). The second approach works with local champions and grassroots women-led groups to support women's peer learning in collectives and strengthen their leadership capacities. Synergies between these two piloted approaches support equitable scaling of locally led adaptation.
title: Scaling with households and groups: socially inclusive approaches supporting equitable scaling of locally led adaptation in Kenya's dairy sector

description: This innovation is a new/adapted technology for conservation of Suidae (pig) genetic resources in-vitro based on a stem cell approach.The technology relies of harvesting of somatic cells (such as from an animal’s body), which are then bought back to undifferentiated stem cells, also called induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), in the laboratory. The iPSCs can be stored in-vitro (under liquid nitrogen) and later used to produce any cell type (undifferentiated stem cells are characterized by their ability to produce any cell type in the body). To date we have successfully demonstrated stable lines of local pig somatic cells in culture. The steps in progress include inducing pluripotency, characterizing and demonstrating their differentiation potential, and later using them in assisted reproductive technologies to revive the pig which cells were stored in liquid nitrogen. This technology will be used to conserve tropical pig genetic resources in Uganda, Vietnam, and potentially elsewhere.
title: Conservation of tropical indigenous pig Suidae genetic resources using the induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) derived from somatic cells

description: The Climate Security Programming Dashboard for Climate Finance (CSPDxCF) is a comprehensive tool designed for initial conflict sensitive assessments and guidance for projects funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) along with other climate funds and financial institutions. In the project design phase, CSPD assists Accredited Entities (AEs) and Direct Entities (DEs) in identifying operational risks and entry points for peace-informed action, providing tailored guidance on integrating climate strategies with security programming. Additionally, CSPD enhances AEs and DEs due diligence and risk management, optimizing project design in fragile and conflict-affected settings.

description: The methodology is applicable to measures that reduce anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in rice-cropping soils. Such measures include changing the water regime during the cultivation period from continuously to intermittently flooded conditions and/or a shortened period of flooded conditions, using the alternate wetting and drying method, adopting aerobic rice cultivation methods, and switching from transplanted to direct-seeded rice (DSR). description: In response to  rangeland degradation, conventional practices involving exotic species like Acacia saligna and Atriplex nummularia have exacerbated ecological imbalances by endangering local flora and fauna and diminishing biodiversity. While developing the Tunisian National Strategy for Advancing Feed and Forage Resources in Tunisia, ICARDA proposed innovative solutions centered on the reintroduction of indigenous species. These were carefully selected to thrive in specific agroecological zones addressing key constraints, and which will be implemented by the Office of Livestock and Pastures and other national institutions. Drivers of loss of indigenous species planting include limited seed availability, lack of awareness, and entrenched institutional behavior. Therefore, our strategies involve genetic source scanning to match indigenous species with environmental conditions, raising awareness about indigenous species' benefits, and efforts to change institutional behavior. Additionally, we are exploring ways to enhance seed collection and multiplication. This approach revitalizes degraded rangelands, contributing significantly to climate change mitigation.
title: Unlocking indigenous plants as innovative solutions for restoring agro-ecological zones under changing climate in the dry areas

description:
Targeting Tools is a web-based Geospatial Information System (GIS) platform that houses a wide range of spatial datasets, both global and country-specific. It provides Land Similarity, Land Suitability, and Land Statistics tools for use on both desktop and web platforms._x000D_
The platform not only facilitates the visualization of datasets stored in its geodatabase but also supports user-uploaded raster format datasets. It enables various types of suitability or risk mapping analyses by combining different datasets._x000D_
Users are given the flexibility to establish their own criteria and thresholds to identify suitable areas. Moreover, these tools can be used to characterise the identified areas through the calculation of zonal statistics.  _x000D_
The tool allows for the integration of multi-dimensional datasets, including bio-physical (e.g. climate, soils, agro-ecology) as well as socio-economic (e.g. poverty, nutritional status, access to markets) data and thus for analyses along the different CGIAR impact areas.

description: The Climate Security Observatory (CSO) is an online decision-making support tool providing robust, localized, and policy-relevant evidence on	how	exactly climate security risks	may	emerge across different geographic contexts. It aims to answer several	research	questions on how the  climate security nexus operates at the subnational level. To achieve this , the CSO performs a series of mixed-methods analyses (data-driven literature review, pathway analysis, social media issue mapping, governance coherence analysis, network analysis, spatial analysis, econometric analysis), before synthesizing outputs into an open-access online dashboard. Within the CSO, a module for decision making on displacement-related is being developed.

description: Pig and beef cattle keepers in Son La province of NorthWest Vietnam rarely engage in best practice in pig and beef cattle production and marketing.  There are numerous reasons for this, a key one being lack of access to information.  To address this, we are developing a social behaviour change communication (SBCC) campaign that will share best practice messages on herd health, breeding, animal nutrition and marketing.  The campaign will be designed to reach livestock keepers of different genders (women and men) as well as ethnicities (primarily Thai and H'mong).  Currently the strategy for the campaign is being developed in conjunction with behaviour change specialists.

description: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is designed for Excellence in Agronomy (EiA) Use Case teams with an interest in developing gender- and youth-responsive agronomic solutions. The SOP is a guide to help Use Case teams move from each step in their workflows when designing, validating, and piloting their Minimum Viable Products (MVPs) to ensure they can develop gender- and youth-responsive agronomic solutions by the end of their Use Case. This stepwise procedure first entails carrying out a diagnostic assessment of gender and generational differences in agricultural management practices and technology adoption and the factors contributing to these differences. These steps (6 total) to developing gender- and youth-responsive agronomic solutions are described with some detail in this SOP. The SOP has been used during the implementation of the integrated survey to ground the Use Cases. Reports from 3 Use cases are shown in the evidence.

description: Accurate measurement of crop cultivated area is essential for assessing various agronomic gain key performance indicators (KPIs) including yield, profitability, and resource use efficiency. Previous household surveys heavily relied on farmer-reported plot area. However, it has been reported frequently that farmer-reported plot area is often biased due to various reasons. Here, we describe procedure for a GPS-based field area measurement. Module 1 introduces the use of GPS devices as first option, whereas module 2 describes the use of application software on smartphones and tablets as second option. Here, we describe UTM Area Measure, an android application downloadable for free from Google Play Store, as an example. This module describes the procedures for downloading and performing the measurements with this application. There are many other applications, that have functions similar to those of UTM Area Measure. They can also be used to measure field/plot area

description: We develop a novel approach for spatial analysis based on databases characterizing sub-national units in various countries using Uber H3 level-6 hexagons—a spatial grid system. Uber's H3 system optimizes spatial data exploration, enhancing geographic information analysis across various data types: crops, livestock, population, and climate. Unique identifiers in H3 hexagons aid data aggregation, outperforming square pixels for broad spatial coverage. Note: Hexagon size may differ from actual pixels like SPAM; values vary by location and underlying pixels. Interpret as important indicators, not absolute values. Our database serves researchers, policymakers, and organizations keen on foresight analysis. We actively promote H3 system integration into existing models, offering documentation, tutorials, and support. Preliminary appraisals ensure system accuracy and reliability. This innovation provides invaluable insights using efficient spatial data analysis for foresight purposes, benefiting stakeholders.

description: The Climate Smart Governance (CSG) Dashboard provides accurate data on climate-related hazards, population vulnerability, forecast climate scenarios, sector-relevant data (water, health, agriculture, ecosystem), infrastructure and climate-related projects to support coordinated mid- to long-term adaptation planning aligned to global development goals. description: Climate variability and its impacts on natural and human systems are increasingly visible across the globe. Despite international attention towards this so-called climate security nexus, understanding of how climate, conflict, and resilience interact is sparse. This is partly due to a lack of sources that combine relevant data. The aim of this concept is to develop a Climate Security Index (CSI) that will allow academics and policymakers to conduct evidence-based research into an imperative global challenge. The CSI would be able to produce an aggregate, comparable, subnational dataset that provides relevant information for academics and policymakers to analyze indicators across the nexus.

The FRESH initiative is developing an end-to-end approach to increase fruit and vegetable intake and in turn improve diet quality, nutrition and health outcomes while also improving livelihoods, empowering women and youth and mitigating negative environmental impacts. _x000D_
_x000D_
Worldwide intake of fruit and vegetables is too low contributing to poor quality diets and in turn, high prevalence of malnutrition and diet-related non-communicable diseases.​ Key barriers to increasing intake exist include the availability, accessibility, affordability and desirability of fruit and vegetables. The integrated end-to-end approach will address each key barriers by implementing co-located approaches that simultaneously address constraints to increasing the desirability, availability, affordability and accessibility of sustainable, safe and healthy produce and ultimately intake of fruits and vegetables, evaluating these approaches to help build evidence on what works and inform policy and program design.

description: Carbon credits can potentially be used in various ways to improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers. They may incentivize farmers to switch to crop management practices that reduce the carbon footprint and improve soil health and productivity in the long run. The compensation could be disbursed directly to farmers or be used to improve advisory or community services and cover the cost of inputs. Since their parcels and total land area are relatively small, the monetary value of carbon credits for a farm household is also small. Hence, it is essential for the Measurement, Reporting, and Verification tools to be cost-effective. To address the challenge, we designed a satellite remote sensing-based carbon offset estimation system to help smallholder farmers estimate carbon offsets from conservation agriculture practices using freely available datasets. We tested the proof-of-concept system in Bajío, Mexico. This report describes the data and approaches developed as an early-stage innovation.
title: ECOSat: A satellite remote sensing-based carbon offset estimation system to help smallholder farmers estimate carbon offset potentials using freely available datasets

description: Modern breeding is a data rich process, and requires data management software designed for the task of generating, tracking, storing and using the information produced by breeding programs for breeding decisions.  Many programs are currently not using a formal data management system; others are using older legacy systems.  With the Enterprise Breeding System becoming available, these programs can now adopt the new software.  Data migration into a new database is a complex process with many idiosyncrasies depending on how a breeding programs has been managing its data before adopting a new system, hence a clear and transparent strategy was needed.  Scope, process, and timelines will be defined so new adopters can quickly get value of the system. An important point of agreement for scope was the definition of a minimal set of operational data that would allow breeders to use the system within a year of beginning adoption.
title: A data migration strategy for future Enterprise Breeding System users is formalised and allows for quick, efficient adoption of EBS

description: A package of good agricultural practices (GAP)  developed by FRESH Initiative partner World Vegetable Center was developed for okra and chili pepper production to help smallholder farmers safely intensify production. The GAP package includes training on how to improve vegetable nursery health, the use of organic farm inputs and reduced chemical use, improved irrigation methods, and best practices for insect or pest management. This package of good agricultural practices, when implemented, may increase vegetable farmers' yields while reducing overall input costs and minimize health risks due to pesticide exposure.

description: Food safety practices in traditional markets are often very poor, due to lack of infrastructure, low knowledge levels, and the absence of incentives. This innovation addresses these gaps by providing food safety training to vendors and offering an opportunity for enrollment in a voluntary food safety grading program. Consumers will be made aware of the program through posters advertising the grading program and signs indicating the food safety grade of participating vendors.

description: This innovation assesses the impact of incentives for good hygiene behavior at upstream value chain nodes by integrating a slaughterhouse hygiene inspection into the regular duties of meat inspectors, who assess hygiene standards. Slaughterhouse workers receive performance-based bonuses linked to these inspections, encouraging compliance. Slaughterhouse owners and regulatory authorities oversee implementation, ensuring alignment with food safety regulations and public health goals.

description: This framework helps to assess the potential of innovations and technologies to contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions from food systems. It considers (1) the technological,  institutional/political, social and biophysical context; (2) the local or country-specific barriers  to adoption; (3) value chain-specific barriers to scalability; (4) context-specific carbon benefits, sustainable development co-benefits and undesired social and biophysical effects that may result from broad adoption once barriers are overcome. The framework also helps in identifying scaling bottlenecks and designing a cost-effective scaling strategy for the prioritized innovations/strategies.

description: This DSS will use watershed modelling and monitoring to analyse loads, fate, transport and human exposure to microbiological pollutants (including zoonotic pathogens) via water flow pathways. Such DSS will allow policy makers to assess risks from microbial pollution in watersheds, and to test ex-ante the cost-effectiveness of solutions (e.g. improved treatment of livestock waste) to manage and mitigate health risks. So far the watersheds monitoring plans have been formulated for Hindon (India) and Akaki (Ethiopia) and first water samples collected. Modelling conceptualization has started.

description: We previously developed and assessed the validity and feasibility of using innovative AI mobile technology that provides offline real-time diagnostics and tailored "nudging" on dietary intake as a strategy to improve diets and nutrition of adolescents living in urban settings in Ghana and Viet Nam. The innovative AI app FRANI (Food Recognition and Nudging Insights) was developed and tested in younger female adolescent girls aged 15-17 years with promising results. This study aims at further developing the app and evaluating it’s use in older adolescent females aged 18-24 years. Our hypothesis is that by addressing knowledge-related barriers to healthy food choices using information tailored to existing circumstances, adolescents will improve behaviors related to food consumption and diets, and potentially improving behaviors of their peers.
title: Validation and feasibility of AI-assisted dietary assessment mobile app (FRANI) for nutrient intake and personalized nudging to improve diets in female youth in Urban Ghana

description: The Digital AgroClimate Advisory (HingaSmart) is designed to support agricultural value chain actors with bundled agro-climate advisory services. HingaSmart has been customized to generate context-specific agro-climate advisories for Ghana and other countries. To contextualize the HingaSmart app for Ghana, key crops from the three major Agro-Ecological Zones (AEZs) were mapped using the Ghana land use map. The highest-ranked major crops per AEZ were then subjected to a detailed analysis to determine key descriptors, including region, district, altitude, maximum and minimum temperature, fertilizer recommendations, crop water requirements, crop coefficient (KC) per crop stage, and the seasonal average KC for each crop. In the second year, additional location-specific data on crops and fertilizer recommendations were collected. This information was integrated with climate data to digitally deliver context-specific, location-based, and actionable recommendations along agricultural value chains in Ghana.

description:
The rare bean species Phaseolus hygrophilus, collected in the Costa Rican rainforest and preserved in CIAT’s gene bank, has proven difficult to conserve due to its inability to produce seeds. To address this, a tissue culture method has been optimized, and the species is now maintained both in tissue culture and as a living collection in specialized growth chambers. These plants are propagated using grafting techniques and cuttings. For Phaseolus albicarminus, a separate grafting and layering protocol has been developed for vegetative propagation. However, this species has not been successfully preserved through tissue culture and is instead maintained as a living collection in growth chambers._x000D_
The conservation methods are being used to conserve and produce seeds of wild bean species in the field by genebank staff working on the regeneration of the bean collection.
title: Conservation methods developed for rare wild bean species

description: The diamondback moth, Plutella xylostella (Lepidoptera: Plutellidae) is the major insect pest attacking cabbage crops in West Africa. As commonly practiced control measures, farmers very often resort to spray chemical insecticides at high dose and application frequency. Over the years, this indiscriminate use of chemical pesticides has led to the resurgence of pesticide resistance in the pest, hence demanding more frequent applications with all the unintended harmful effects of human and environmental health. In the attempt to break the vicious circle of pesticide resistance, bio-pesticides such as the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana have been identified as very efficient alternative control options in managing the pest and hence are the target of our intervention.
title: Farmer participatory validation and adaptation trials for selected biopesticides against the diamondback moth on cabbage

description: In order to improve farmer-managed seed systems in NATURE+ five countries, it's essential to understand the current existing seed (related) policies and laws in the implementing countries to address and remove potential obstacles for effective support to farmer-managed seed systems. In several countries, right now seed policies and laws are hindering or preventing farmers from fully benefiting from minor crops and local varieties. This report highlights the policy and legal elements required to fully promote farmer-managed based seed systems as a critical innovation to develop a NATURE+ production system. The Initiative already developed a number of innovations related to seed system development, which can only be implemented at scale when a supportive policy and legal context exists.

Our innovation provides them with a non-chemical pest control alternative which is safe and sustainable, based on the introduction and releases of the specific predatory mite Phytoseiulus longipes (Acari: Phytoseiidae).

description:
Mechanized direct seeded rice (DSR) introduces innovations in both the design and sourcing of specialized seeding machines, as well as in developing business models to facilitate access to these machines. This method involves sowing rice seeds directly into the soil using mechanical seeders that precisely plant seeds in rows, covering them efficiently, whether in dry or wet conditions. The innovation lies in the mechanization process, which incorporates advanced seeding machinery designed or sourced specifically to optimize seed placement and soil contact, leading to reduced seed rates and decreased water requirements._x000D_
_x000D_
Additionally, this approach not only addresses the challenges of labor and cost reduction but also promotes water conservation and faster planting times. By integrating these technological and entrepreneurial innovations, mechanized DSR aims to overcome the limitations of traditional and broadcast seeding methods, such as low yields and high operational costs, while also contributing to environmental sustainability by reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
title: Mechanized direct-seeding for sustainable, economically-viable and climate resilient rice production in the Mekong sub-region

description:
A data-to-analytics infrastructure roadmap was developed for EiA in 2022. A critical part of this infrastructure is a global datapool or database that allows search within standardized datasets largely collected across _x000D_
CGIAR (i.e., beyond traditional metadata search) to return aggregated datasets for analyses. A proof-of-concept was developed in Q4 of 2022, built on state-of-the-art graph database technology. Further development in 2023 has generated an alpha version, populated by a public, legacy datasets (about 200) standardized using the Carob (R script) workflow. Users can search the database for gender-disaggregated data, to assess gender-based differences in crop yields or fertilizer application. Aggregated data from such searches is pre-formatted for easier use in analytics (aligned with R scripts used in ML and the Carob model) and for commonly-used AgMIP crop simulation models (as a first step toward data-to-model capability). Users can also upload data directly to private data pools.
title: Global agronomy database v. alpha to enable search of standardized data and retrieval of aggregated datasets by researchers

description: AfricaRice developed a protocol under the guidance of Aarhus University to break the dormancy of Oryza glaberrima seeds. In 2022, the protocol was tested among a range of alternative methods and validated with seeds from 300 accessions constituting the core collection. The protocol involves heating the seeds at 50C for 28 days. Results exhibited a very high germination rate for all accessions tested (average 97%). The protocol has been adopted as standard procedure for seed dormancy breaking of this species and shared with IRRI and will allow more efficient viability testing and regeneration of accessions in both collections. In 2024, the innovation was used to test the germination of new Oryza glaberrima collections.
title: Successful protocol to break dormancy of Oryza glaberrima seeds incorporated into standard procedure after testing on 300 accessions.

description: In 2024, 90 standard genebank operating procedures (SOPs) were drafted or updated to incorporate new improved protocols, procedures or technologies at AfricaRice, CIAT, CIMMYT, CIP, ICRISAT, IITA, ILRI, IRRI. In 2023, 21 Standard operating procedures (SOPs) were drafted, 96 were updated and 76 were audited in ten genebanks.  In 2022, 49 SOPs have been newly drafted or modified with improved methods in all nine CGIAR genebanks. The new SOPs are the result of trialing new techniques and piloting of new technologies that have been found to improve existing seed germination, conservation, disease testing or other genebank procedures that are documented and implemented in CGIAR genebanks and germplasm health units. In 2022, examples of new SOPs include a protocol for high-throughput DNA extraction and a procedure for analysing genotypic data developed by CIAT and a dormancy-breaking protocol for African rice species in AfricaRice. Genebanks and GHUs are continuously attempting to improve genebank and phytosanitary procedures as a means to become more efficient.

description:
In Aquatic Food Systems, the adage "we don't know what we don't know" is particularly relevant. To truly understand the potential for aquatic foods system transformation, we must know where the largest data gaps are, and the effort vs impact trade-offs that exist in filling them._x000D_
This is a method to identify gaps in data and knowledge using the FishBase databases of aquatic biodiversity and traits for 11 countries of interest according to 4 key areas: topic, time, taxonomy, and territory.

description: Seed, grain, and food businesses in Indonesia rarely use any form of traceability, with some limited use of paper-based records or digitized business management systems. This makes protecting the value of biofortified zinc rice difficult to protect throughout the supply chain. This innovation aims to bring together private-sector businesses that offer digital traceability systems to seed businesses that supply zinc-fortified rice in Indonesia. In 2023, we collaborated with a local innovation partner to design and develop a digital tool to monitor full supply chain activities of zinc wheat in two regions: Jakarta and Yogyakarta. In 2024, users will also participate in the research pilot. The final tool will be presented to users in 10 districts with proportion of the users selected for questionnaires on likeability and usability of the tool.
title: Digital Traceability: A biofortified rice traceability system for seed businesses in Indonesia

The ongoing expansion of groundwater resource development will undoubtedly provide a great contribution to Nepal’s irrigation sector and food security. Along this way, a digital groundwater monitoring system will be critical to help the country guide the development and management of the resource by providing decision-makers and communities with adequate spatial evidence and information about the opportunities and risks for sustainable and equitable groundwater use.

description: The innovations aim to develop improved chicken that grows fast and produces more eggs compared to the existing smallholder poultry production system. Imported commercial chicken lines lack adaptation characteristics when managed under smallholder systems. As a result the performance is usually low. They also do not meet the farmer preferences such as plumage and skin colour, mothering ability among others. This innovation entails developing various crossbred combinations that meets the needs and aspirations of smallholder farmers using improved inbred lines. It will also include evaluating the performances of the crossbreds on station and on-farm to identify best combinations using reciprocal crossing. The names of the four inbred lines are: LIL20: BIL20 Local ILRI 2020: Barred NHIL20: ILRI 2020 Brown ILRI 2020 WIL20: White ILRI 2020 The naming is subjected to change.
title: Improved dual-purpose adaptive chicken strains for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia

description: There is a lack of data on food systems greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions at the food system level. The country profiles, which will take the form of reports and briefs, will synthesize GHG emission-  and climate change-related data at the national level, provide an analysis of key drivers of and contributors to GHG emissions in food systems and explore the potential of alternative mitigation actions and associated trade-offs, taking into account environmental boundaries and transformational needs. Iterative versions of these profiles will include new data on emissions generated by the Initiative and deepen the food systems approach in order to break down entrenched sectoral categories and existing adaptation and mitigation silos while providing a means to integrate and assess emissions from multiple sources along the food value chain from production to consumption. In 2022 progress was made on draft profiles for Bangladesh, China, Colombia, Kenya and Vietnam.

description: Compressing local agro-industrial by products into nutrient dense livestock feed pellets is a worthwhile innovation to compete with expensive and imported feed pellets or concentrates. Use of such pellets also alleviates pressure on rangelands or grasslands.  This innovation consists of a small scale compressor 'pelletizer' and formulas to create qualitatively suﬃcient feed pellets with locally available inputs. In Tunisia, there are many agro-pastoralists that are dependent on expensive and imported livestock feed pellets to improve livestock quality and to supplement feed shortages. Risks of relative feed shortages are likely to increase due to climate change. Also there are many discarded by-products from local agro-food supply chains such as olive cakes, date kernels, and downgraded dates, which still contain nutrients. Feed pellet production with this small scale pelletizer producing 500 kg pellets / hour is also an interesting income generating activity for farmer organizations and creates employment.
title: Feed pellet production using a small-scale pelletizer and available agricultural products and agroindustrial by-products for agro-pastoralists, farmers and farmer organizations.

description: In Mali, vaccination campaigns against major endemic livestock diseases are conducted every year by the Direction Nationale des Services Vétérinaires (DNSV). Some of these diseases include contagious bovine pleuropneumoniae (CBPP), peste des petits ruminants (PPR) and bovine and ovine pasteurellosis. However, adequate vaccination coverage that will lead to sufficient herd immunity is often hard to achieve. Some of the challenges to vaccination are logistical, socio-economical, institutional and organisational. To address the various vaccination challenges, a multi-stakeholder approach through Innovation Platforms (IPs) was applied to create a sphere of learning, information sharing and interaction among vaccine supply chain stakeholders. The IP approach focused on three pillars: Communication and collaboration, Knowledge sharing through collective action and Capacity building. This IP approach has been successful in increasing uptake of vaccines by farmers and raising the health of livestock, which makes the livestock more productive."
title: Integrated-approach with Public Private Partnerships and community-based engagement through stakeholder platforms for vaccine delivery, monitoring and evaluation, and improved biosecurity for control of diseases in smallholder livestock systems

description: The global rangelands data platform is being established in response to a gap in rangelands data identified by the UN Environment Assembly through Resolution L17 Innovations in Sustainable Rangelands and Pastoralism 2019 and the complimentary report: A Case of Benign Neglect. Knowledge Gaps About Sustainability in Pastoralism and Rangelands. With funding from the CGIAR Big Data Platform and through a consultative process the outline of the platform was conceptualised. A global rangelands atlas was launched as a first step. It is anticipated that the global rangelands data platform will be launched in 2026. It will bring together big data on rangelands, source data including exploring crowd-sourcing and be an interactive platform for producing reports and trends for multiple users including UN Agencies monitoring rangeland and development agencies and actors developing interventions for rangelands, researchers and academics, and ultimately pastoralists themselves.

description: The WELI facilitates assessments of the impact of livestock interventions on the empowerment of women involved in the sector. By getting better at understanding what interventions work best at providing empowering opportunities, we can refine these interventions and in the long term, provide better empowering opportunities for women involved in livestock. Providing women farmers with opportunities for empowerment through livestock is important to both enhance household livelihoods and nutrition while also promoting progress on gender equity. In 2015, the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), in collaboration with Emory University developed the WELI tool based on the Women’s Empowerment in Agriculture Index (WEAI) developed earlier by IFPRI. The WELI measures women’s empowerment in livestock and crop agriculture and focuses specifically on key areas of livestock production, such as animal health, breeding and feeding; and on use of livestock products, such as animal-source-food processing and marketing.

description: The WikiPapa platform was created in 2021 to help the global community, it is an integrated system that involves farmers (guardians of the potato), consumers, students, teachers, and researchers. The WikiPapa environment connects people with the biodiversity of native potatoes through technological tools, combined with smartphones, as well as opening the world of science to students and young people to achieve learning in the exploration, observation, and discovery of the Biodiversity of native potatoes. WikiPapa’s mission is to support the in situ conservation of the biodiversity of native Andean potato varieties through citizen science, utilizing VarScout tools. This interactive platform showcases a collection of over 950 varieties from Peru, Chile, Bolivia, and Colombia and has gathered around 2,000 observations from citizen scientists and contributions from 946 farmers, representing a total of 1,481 unique varieties.
title: WikiPapa Platform: a decision support tool for monitoring the conservation status of potato landraces in space and time in diversity hotspots

description: The Environmental Flow Estimation Tools are a set of user-friendly (online and offline) software tools enabling desktop estimation of quick,  coarse-scale environmental flow requirements of rivers. The input data required are time series data of monthly “natural” river flows, either measured or estimated. The tools are meant to be used by water planners and managers in making initial planning-level estimates of environmental flows, which may then be followed by more comprehensive assessments using further data related to aquatic ecology, moving beyond river flow data. Five tools are currently available, two covering major rivers and the other three specifically for estimating environmental flow requirements in the Ganges Basin, Sri Lanka and Nepal. The tools are also useful for building capacity on environmental flow estimation, including for students and practitioners seeking to gain an initial understanding of the concept of environmental flows.

description: Breeders are forced to seek the variation they require from genetic resource collections conserved in genebanks. The challenge when searching specific traits from genebanks is that resources to search for a given trait are often such that only a relatively small subset of the available genebank can be evaluated. Thus, to be effective, a strategy is required to identify the smallest possible subset of germplasm to evaluate whilst increasing the chances of capturing the sought-after variation. Genesys currently holds more than 4 million genebank accessions from 462 institutes and is accessed by users to order germplasm. From these, around 768,576 accessions are held at CGIAR genebanks. Identifying the correct set of accessions to respond to these requests adequately can be time-consuming.The subsetting tool allows to develop and implement data mining techniques for subsetting germplasm accessions, thus helping address germplasm requests more effectively and efficiently. The sub-setting is based on indicators for historical climate information, soil information and specific per crop regarding stresses. This web tool allows users to compose the needed subsets and order them directly from genebanks in Genesys. In the tool, a user identifies a series of potential subsets using data and analytics and then selects the subset of accessions that best suits their interest. For example, amongst four potential subsets, they may select the subset with accessions grown in the driest places.
title: The sub-setting tool provides Genebank managers and users (breeders, scientists, students, NGOs) a web-tool to subset (select) genebank accessions available from genebanks based on environmental parameters

description: Breeding programs that are community-based cover a range of situations. Typically, they target low input systems with farmers within a limited geographical area who have a common interest to work together for the improvement of the genetic resources of their animals. Community-based breeding programs (CBBPs) focus on indigenous stock and consider farmers’ needs, views, decisions and active participation, from inception through to implementation. Most importantly, they provide a participatory and bottom-up approach. CBBP combines farmer training to improve selection methods, consisting of pooling community flocks to create a larger gene pool from which breeding animals can be selected, scientific support to provide farmers with information on different breeding options and data collection to monitor how well individual animals perform. The entire community flock is treated as one. Livestock keepers who choose to participate in the program are organized into sheep/goat breeding associations, many of which later evolve into formal cooperatives.
title: An innovative genetic improvement strategy for sheep and goat that involves the end users, farmers, in the design and implementation of the scheme

description:
The Circular Bioeconomy Innovation Hub (CBEIH) is one-stop-shop for training, research, advisory support, collaboration and knowledge sharing. The hub unites 17 stakeholders from the public and private sectors, research institutions, non-governmental organizations, and education to promote circular bioeconomy initiatives. Operating in the organic waste-to-resource value chain, a co-ownership model that ensures shared goals and resources for co-design and co-implementation is used for maximum collective impact. The hub aims to showcase, optimize, and promote existing circular bioeconomy innovations while fostering the development of new, accessible innovations. This is accomplished through five strategic operational areas: demand-driven capacity building; research for innovation and scaling; advisory support for policy development and implementation; monitoring, evaluation, and learning; and information sharing, collaboration, and partnerships. To promote innovation adoption, the hub also works with scaling partners._x000D_
In 2024, the hub has successfully organized and co-organized several multi-stakeholder workshops on waste valorization. It is currently piloting waste source-segregation in schools in Ghana, targeting not only students but also aiming to transfer knowledge and experience to catalyze change in their homes.
title: Circular Bioeconomy Innovation Hub in Ghana: A Multistakeholder Platform for scaling circular economy innovations to minimize urban environmental pollution

description: The optimized production and use of biogas (clean fuel) and organic fertilizer from livestock manure management improve energy efficiency and agricultural sustainability. This system processes animal waste and other organic materials to generate biogas and bio-slurry. It enables small-scale agricultural producers and livestock keepers, particularly those with minimal GHG emissions, to contribute to a low-carbon rural economy through improved agricultural practices. By promoting a circular economy on farms, it enhances productivity while supporting climate change mitigation in livestock farming. Additionally, it improves nutrition and agricultural output by using bio-slurry for food production and biogas for cooking and farm operations.

description: Water productivity constitutes one of the keyways to expand Water Energy Food Ecosystems (WEFE) benefits in water scarce contexts, yet water productivity is variable and in cases low. This innovation is focused on development of a Decision Support System (DSS) that enables planners and managers to identify solutions (e.g., resources allocations or crop mixes) that improve productivity. The DSS is a computer-based platform reveals the productivity associated with alternative investment choices, which can support investment decisions that optimize water productivity and WEFE benefits in different geographies. Key users of the DSS platform are water planners and managers, as well as those in related sectors (i.e. Energy, Food and Ecosystems).

description: Achieving durable resistance to wheat rust disease and effectively managing it requires continuous monitoring of pathogen movement and analyzing their pathogenic variations. Despite the severe drought in wheat-growing areas across CWANA in 2024, the Regional Cereal Rust Research Center in Turkey, along with national rust surveillance teams, conducted rust monitoring in Morocco, and the rust surveys in Lebanon and Tunisia were conducted by the national rust survey teams, adhering to BGRI surveillance guidelines. Surveillance data were collected from 35, 64, and 27 locations in Lebanon, Morocco, and Tunisia, respectively. The ODK rust survey mobile application was use during the rust survey in Morocco, Lebanese and Tunisia that carried out rust surveys in wheat-producing regions. They recorded GPS coordinates, rust disease status, and crop phenology, then shared this data with the online Global Cereal Rust Surveillance and Monitoring System in accordance with BGRI's standard protocol

description: Alfalfa mosaic virus (AMV) is a significant plant pathogen affecting a wide range of legume crops across various regions of the world including WANA countries. AMV is transmitted by aphids in a non-persistent manner and via seeds of several hosts (including faba bean, chickpea, and lentil). Seed transmission makes managing AMV more challenging, as infected seeds can introduce the virus into new areas and lead to infections in the next growing season, even before aphid vectors are active. Accordingly, seed testing and the use of certified seeds are key strategies to mitigate the spread of AMV as a seed-borne virus. Early detection and accurate diagnosis of viral diseases is critical for the application of appropriate control measures. However, the accuracy and reliability of molecular methods is a fact beyond dispute. This report describes a validated molecular tool for AMV detection and characterization applied by ICARDA’s Seed Health and Virology Laboratory.
title: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay for detection and characterization of Alfalfa mosaic virus (AMV) in legume crops applied by ICARDA’s Seed Health and Virology Laboratory

description: This early innovation presents a novel approach to assessing Rice Blast (Pyricularia oryzae) severity in rice plants through machine learning and remote sensing. Using a visual scale from 0 to 9 to gauge infection severity, the research collected data from nine trials conducted between 2022 and 2024 at CIAT in Palmira, Colombia. These trials included various rice genotypes and control varieties to benchmark resistance levels. Drones equipped with RGB and multispectral cameras gathered data, later processed with Agisoft Metashape and Phenoi software to extract vegetation indices. Machine learning models were then developed using PyCaret and Scikit-learn, with datasets balanced through oversampling and undersampling techniques. The Random Forest classifier performed best, achieving up to 0.98 accuracy for binary classification (resistant vs. susceptible) and 0.91 accuracy for multiclass classification. This innovation underscores the potential of integrating machine learning and remote sensing for accurate disease monitoring in agriculture focusing on rice diseases.

description: The miniSASS is a tool for citizen scientists to investigate the health of rivers. The miniSASS mobile app uses machine learning to facilitate the identification of the invertebrates living on the stream bottom.  The app then uses the identifications to calculate the river health score based on the tolerance of each invertebrate type and then submits this data to a global mapping platform

description: Integrated Agriculture-Aquaculture (IAA) systems are diversified farming systems where aquatic and terrestrial foods are grown together on the same plot using the resources from one to benefit the other. In Egypt, for example, the production of fish such as Nile tilapia, mullet, and African catfish creates nutrient-rich water that can then be used to irrigate crops such as date palm, olives, figs, pomegranates, guava, onions, sugar beets, and tomato. IAA includes a range of technologies and methods that can be put together and adapted to each farming situation as needed. IAA is one of the most promising and fastest-growing food production systems in Egypt since it enhances production diversity, land productivity, water efficiency and nutrient cycling on farms.

Citizens' Juries (CJs) are a form of deliberative democracy fostering public participation in decision-making. In each CJ, a randomly selected group of 25 people are selected to act as jurors. By involving citizens directly, CJs empower communities to have a direct impact on decision-making processes._x000D_
The jurors learn about and discuss the following topic: "The future of our food systems: Measures to reduce the adverse ecological impacts of agricultural production in the Caquetá region considering socioecological tradeoffs.“ They deliberate and make policy recommendations that are disseminated to policy makers and stakeholders.

description:
Begomovirus is a genus of plant virus that can infect okra. It is transmitted primarily by whiteflies and can cause diseases such as okra leaf curl disease or okra yellow vein mosaic disease. This virus poses a significant problem for agriculture as it induces symptoms like leaf distortion, yellowing, and reduced yield, impacting the productivity and quality of infected crops._x000D_
New genetic resources with resistance to key diseases are needed to strengthen seed systems. West Africa, specifically Nigeria, is a secondary center of diversity of okra, and begomovirus resistance is likely to be present in some genetic resources from this region. 256 accessions of various Abelmoschus species (okra) were collected by the National Horticultural Research Institute in Nigeria and shared with the World Vegetable Center. The accessions were tested as possible resistance sources against Begomovirus diseases and preliminary experiments showed some resistant candidates.
title: Identification of Begomovirus Resistant Okra Accessions for Improved Variety Development

description: Solar-powered irrigation is rapidly increasing in Africa and South Asia. This innovation addresses the urgent need for sustainable solar irrigation recognizing its intricate connections within the Water-Energy-Food-Environment (WEFE) nexus. It brings together a set of innovative solutions and approaches to the design, operation and implementation of solar irrigation that maximizes positive and minimizes negative outcomes. Components include (i) tools for optimal water pumping to prevent groundwater depletion, (ii) new approaches for evidence-based decision-making for assessing the financial feasibility of solar irrigation, (ii) capacity building programs for enhancing the understanding of the WEFE environment in which solar irrigation takes place, (iv) water-efficient irrigation practices (v) gender-responsive finance and business models; (vi) and evidence-based policy guidance promoting sustainable solar irrigation for multiple outcomes, including job creation, gender equality, climate action and improved nutrition.

description: Implementation of e-flows or environmental flows is a requirement of water resource managers but is seldom adequately done. The Digital Innovation Initiative is researching application of digital tools to enable better management of rivers and implementation of e-flows. These tools include drone (UAV) mounted Lidar, Sonar, Ground Penetrating Radar and other sensors that deliver high resolution 3D data describing a river channel and allowing calculation of the river hydraulics. Generated data can be used not only to assess the discharge required to implement e-flows, but can also be used to monitor changes in river morphology over time.
title: A suite of digital tools to map the morphology of rivers to enable monitoring of changes due to river flow management

description: This innovation offers near real-time monitoring of irrigated areas across an entire transboundary river basin. The first version of the system utilized high-resolution Sentinel-2 (optical) satellite imagery data to identify these areas on a monthly basis. It makes use of both expert decision trees and machine learning techniques to identify irrigated regions. Until now, most mapping activities have focused on an annual timescale rather than a near real-time one. This represents a substantial improvement in irrigated area metrics, which directly impacts water availability.
title: A satellite remote sensing-based near real-time monitoring of irrigated areas in the Limpopo River Basin

description: The Water-Energy-Food-Environment (WEFE) Nexus Capacity Scorecard (NCS) is part of a toolkit developed to support organizations to assess their institutional processes, readiness, and capacities in understanding and implementing integrated approaches across the water, energy, food, and environmental sectors. It helps to identify opportunities, possible gaps, and inform the planning of tailored nexus capacity-building efforts, programs and interventions, and/or their monitoring over time. The tool can be used by any organization (public, non-governmental, civic, private, research, etc.) and in multiple contexts. It is adaptable to different program need and can also serve as a launchpad for discussions, within and across organizations and sectors, for improving WEFE nexus practice and collaboration.

description: This report presents the findings from the validation of a Decision Support Tool (DST) developed to optimize late blight management in potato farming. The DST, available as physical discs or an interactive mobile application, integrates host resistance, environmental conditions, and management practices to provide fungicide spray recommendations. Color-coded discs (red, yellow, and green) display spray guidelines that adjust based on potato variety and weather conditions, as informed by research or expert input. The objective of this study was to evaluate the technical efficiency of the tool, assess its efficacy in reducing chemical inputs, and identify potential areas for improvement. The evaluation was conducted on a sample of 61 farms from Kenya's mid- and high-altitude agroecologies, which represent the primary potato-growing regions in the country.
title: Validation trials for a hand-held decision support system for late blight management in Kenya

description: The original PROBFLO was developed as a holistic environmental flow (e-flow) assessment tool. PROBFLO evaluates the socio-ecological consequences of various water resource scenarios and generates e-flow requirements on a regional spatial scale. It follows the ecological risk assessment exposure and effects approach, with multiple stressors, habitats, and ranked ecological impact relationships. Due to the complexity, PROBFLO is currently only used by skilled scientists. As a response to the demand partner in the Limpopo River basin, we are developing a new version of PROBFLO in collaboration with the World Modeler program. The new version will be equipped with a user-friendly interface and streamlined workflow to make the tool more accessible to stakeholders.
title: PROBFLO v2: A user-friendly environmental flow assessment tool for evaluating socio-ecological consequences of basin-level water management scenarios for transboundary natural resource management authorities

description:
The Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning, and Impact Assessment component of the Market Intelligence Initiative is developing a methodology for rating varieties in terms of how well they match the market intelligence developed through the initiative; as a proxy for how impactful they might be for farmers and consumers, if adopted. We plan to develop a system to score varieties in terms of their market intelligence. We plan to develop this scoring system in much greater depth in 2023, in collaboration with MELIA focal points from other initiatives in the Genetic Innovation action area. This system will compare the chosen varieties to the Target Product Profiles (TPPs) developed under MI Work Package 2, on various dimensions._x000D_
_x000D_
MELIA is also collaborating with MI WP3. Randomly selected farmers will receive nudges to encourage them to adopt varieties promoted by WP3. We will exploit this random variation to establish causal relationship between adoption and impact.

description: Understanding how fish respond to stressors, such as water pollution and altered flows, is important to monitor aquatic ecosystem health. Fish’s behavioral responses are shown to be up to 100 times more sensitive to environmental stressors than any other established line of evidence, and they are used in various environmental monitoring, conservation, and research programs. Recent advancements in sensor-based telemetry studies showed fish behavior could be observed remotely in real-time, providing prospects for enhanced natural resource management activities. In the Limpopo River Basin, we support the University of Mpumalanga in developing FISHTRAC, a real-time water quality monitoring system using fish-attached sensors, and testing its functionality. In 2022, based on FISHTRAC’s prototype, we improved the system’s real-time monitoring capabilities. The improved FISHTRAC was deployed to a school of Tigerfish in the Crocodile River. In 2023, we collected more data to establish relationships between fish behaviors and environmental variables.
title: FISHTRAC: Real-time monitoring of water quality dynamics using fish-attached sensors

description: Tracking the movement of the wheat rust pathogens and monitoring their pathogenic variabilities are the main pillars in successful breeding for durable rust resistance and disease management programs. Despite the severe drought conditions in wheat growing areas in CWANA in 2022, the rust surveillance was coordinated by the Regional Cereal Rust Research Center-Turkey in Lebanon, Morocco, and Tunisia, following the BGRI rust surveillance protocols. The national rust surveillance teams at the Lebanese Agricultural Research Institute, Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique (Morocco), and INSTITUT NATIONAL DES GRANDES CULTURES-TUNISIA (Tunisia) conducted the rust surveys in target countries. The GPS coordinates of survey sites, the status of rust diseases, and crop phenology were collected and shared with the online Global Cereal Rust Surveillance and Monitoring System (https://rusttracker.cimmyt.org) following the BGRI standard rust surveillance protocol (https://rusttracker.cimmyt.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/2013-Updated-BGRI-protocols-v2-web.pdf).
title: Surveillance and monitoring the cereal rust diseases in Lebanon, Morocco, and Tunisia in 2022

description: The innovation provides experimental tools to examine how access to market intelligence (MI) information impacts breeding investment decisions and potential heterogeneities in decision making by various characteristics (e.g., breeder and institutional characteristics). The tool also allows to examine breeders’ willingness to pay for market intelligence. The tool can be implemented by means of an online lab-in-the-field experiment. This method will allow to analyze the impacts of different types of market intelligence, investigate underlying behavioral mechanisms, and elicit demand for market intelligence in a more controlled setting, allowing us to estimate causal effects of market intelligence and variations in the way the intelligence is presented.

description: South Asia Drought Monitoring System (SADMS) is a powerful platform that helps farmers, authorities, and extension workers to monitor and effectively manage droughts. It combines real-time weather updates and satellite data to provide (1) forecast droughts and monitor their severity at district-level, (2) trigger contingency plans when drought strikes, protecting smallholder farmers, and (3) analyze national and regional data from satellites and other sources. SADMS was developed successfully in South Asia and was now transferred to Africa. It inspired similar platforms in Zambia and Pakistan, proving its adaptability and effectiveness. SADMS is a data-driven approach empowers communities, safeguards vulnerable populations, and builds regional resilience against a shared climatic challenge. SADMS stands as a testament to innovation in the face of environmental adversity.

description: This effort seeks to leverage significant advances in distance learning technologies and techniques to deliver a step change in the capabilities of countries to utilize simulation models in pursuit of their development goals, notably food security in a context of climate change. It has been designed with a focus on scaling economic simulation modeling capacities for meeting the climate challenge in low- and middle-income countries, targeting four sets of key institutions: central decision-making units within governments; research institutes with formal linkages to policymaking; central banks; and large research networks. Central to this innovation is an online economic modeling program. Alongside in-person trainings, communities of practices, and a website portal, the program targets different audiences: people who i) want to know what insights can be gained and generated using economic modeling tools b) run the models for decision making, and iii)  design scenarios or models of their own.

description: Climate change and anthropogenic activities have negatively impacted agro-silvo-pastoral ecosystems across the planet. The global agenda to achieve ecosystem restoration targets has resulted in an increased demand for plant materials that current production systems are unable to satisfy. Under open field cultivation, several species show a low rate of seed germination or need special climatic conditions to germinate or take a long time to establish. Consequently, there is an urgency to preserve and propagate selected genotypes by improving efficient mass propagation techniques. It is necessary to resort to innovation tools, such as in vitro tissue culture technology. Plant tissue culture is used for producing high-quality, disease-free, and true-to-type plants at a fast rate. In vitro propagation can help meet the increasing demand for planting materials aimed at large scale restoration and afforestation programs. Incorporating organic growth additives can stimulate tissue growth and increase the number of shoots, leaves, and roots.
title: Incorporation of organic growth additives to enhance in vitro propagation of selected shrub/tree species for large scale restoration and for supporting local communities dependent on agrosilvopastoral systems in building resilience.

description: This web-app has been developed to ease the weather data acquisition process. This web-app allows the user to extract long-term monthly scale temperature and precipitation data for selected countries in the CWANA region. Users are required to indicate the country of interest and the desired time period. Consequently, the web-app presents annual weather information and time-series precipitation and temperature data as well as meteorological drought indices such as Standard Precipitation Index (SPI) and Standard Temperature Index (STI). Additionally, the platform allows users to generate spatial maps for weather parameters and to export data in the form of maps, tables and figures. This web-app automatically retrieves up-to-date weather data from the ERA5-Land archive.

description: The potato production through zero-tillage using rice straw as mulch (PZTM) is an innovative technique to sustainably intensify agricultural production with potato uses few inputs and residues from the previous crop without disturbing the soil. It has the potential to address issues being exacerbated by climate change like excessive input use leading to detrimental environmental effects, water scarcity, and worsening air quality due to rice straw burning and, as such, significantly contribute to a sustainable agroecological transformation in India. Key to this practice is the efficiency principle, by increasing resource-use efficiencies of major inputs. It recycles straw as mulch, creating value for a residue that would have been burned otherwise. As this technique is associated with economic gains as well as women’s empowerment, it improves rural livelihoods and promotes gender equity, and as such adheres to the principle of human and social values.
title: Production of saline tolerant potato variety under zero tillage using rice straws during the fallow winter season for farmers in rice-based ecosystems in West Bengal, India

description: The project multiplied  clean sweet potato planting material in greenhouses and through Ukama Ustawi trained Decentralised vine multipliers (DVMs).  Farmers therefore accessed orange fleshed sweet potato (OFSP) seed from the research stations and from  DVMs. Public extension workers were responsible for beneficiary registration and provided short training to sweet potato seed beneficiaries.  This innovation is relevant  because it is high in beta carotene a precursor for vitamin A which  contributes to a reduction in Vitamin A deficiency and provides  income to smallholder farmers through its commercialization.  In addition, this innovation is drought tolerant, can be grown throughout the year, even in marginal soils  and hence can provide reasonable yield hance  contributing to food security under drought  conditions or in relatively poor soils .

description: Rice Crop Manager Indonesia, known locally as Layanan Konsultasi Padi (LKP), was developed and introduced to address the key challenges for rice production and productivity in Indonesia through site-specific recommendations leading to a proven increase in yields and incomes. LKP is a digital agriculture decision support tool developed by the International Rice Research Institute to identify the best nutrient management practices for specific rice fields using site-specific nutrient management principles. LKP is designed for use by extension workers, crop advisors, input providers, and providers of services who interview a farmer using a computer or smartphone. Collected information is used to calculate recommendations and transformed into a crop management guideline for the farmer in a one-page printout. Each guideline provides an actionable recommendation, which matches the location-specific cropping practices and needs of a farmer.
title: Layanan Konsultasi Padi (Rice Crop Manager Indonesia): A digital advisory service for rice farmers in Indonesia

description: Current adaptation interventions tend to have a top-down governance approach with limited cross-sector coordination. To achieve systemic change, innovative governance arrangements are necessary to enhance coordination and collaboration across sectors and stakeholders. The multiscale polycentric governance framework promotes coordination across multiple decision centers at different scales with mechanisms for conflict resolution. The framework consists of standard operating procedures to support practitioners and policymakers to collaboratively design and implement transformative adaptation options and governance structures to enhance climate resilience and improve rural welfare.

description: Feed resources are scarce and expensive in the Initiative intervention area of Bonga and Doyogena in Ethiopia. Two youth and women groups in these regions have been supported through research and development activities in the last number of years to improve their small ruminant production. The lack of nutritious and inexpensive suitable feed resources has now solved through the introduction of a complete feed processing unit composed of a grinder, conveyor belt and feed mixer. Each farmer group has received a feed processing unit which is produced by a local manufacturer. International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas and its partners have developed suitable feed ratios taking into account the availability of local ingredients. The co-designed business plans show the potential of this local feed production. This innovation will improve access to inexpensive quality feed and generate income for groups through feed commercialization and feed grinding services.

description: Currently no single strategy has been successful in the control of Fusarium wilt of banana caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc). We observed spent waste of an edible mushroom species to suppress Foc in vitro and under screenhouse conditions. As a follow-up to this, trials to evaluate its potential to suppress Foc under field conditions were set up in 2023. Preliminary results show a single application of mushroom waste over a one-year period to be in adequate for lowering disease pressure on farm., while repeated close applications look to potentially reduce Foc on farm. More bio-active cultures need to still be explored with more regular applications following bio-priming at planting.
title: Spent waste of the edible mushroom Pleurotus ostreatus has potential as a bio-control agent to suppress Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense.

description: In 2023, farmer preferences for silvopastoral sustainable intensification interventions involving both private and public good benefits assessed through mixed mode surveys based on Best-Worst Scaling (BWS) workshops, a Choice Experiment (CE) and a payments for ecosystem services conservation tender approach in two districts of Northern Laos. In 2024, the PES conservation tender approach was implemented and 534 farmer bid offers (involving ≈320 individual farmers) across 7 interventions in 17 communities in 2 Provinces were received. Of these xx bids were selected for implementation, considering cost-benefit ratio (e.g. cost per tree planted), conservation value (e.g. native species), and equity considerations (e.g. household's land size, gender, number of households that could be supported). Selected bids included (1) 135 households participating in forage trials, (2) 118 households establishing living fences with over 40 tree species, (3) 62 households protecting trees on pastures, and (4) 17 households producing tree seedlings for inclusion in silvopastures

description: In Zimbabwe, three million smallholder farmers are currently practicing Conservation Agriculture (CA) under the Climate-Proofed Presidential Input Scheme (Pfumvudza/Intwasa). It is also popular practice in Zambia and Malawi. The crops covered are maize, sorghum and legumes. Under this practice, that follows the principles of CA, farmers dig planting basins, apply lime, manure, fertilizer, and seeds in the basin. Such practice has resulted in yield boost due to the benefits of precision input use in addition to CA. However, it is limited to small plots due to drudgery that limits its wider adoption outside of the small plots. It is done mainly by women who are sometimes accompanied by children.  CIMMYT has developed an innovative low-cost mechanized solution called “Basin Digger” that can be used to save time and reduce drudgery, saving up to 85% labour compared to the current practice of manual digging using hand hoes.
title: Basin digger under minimum soil disturbance for smallholder Conservation Agriculture (Pfumvudza) in Southern Africa

description: IFPRI researchers developed the curriculum, ‘Planning for Voice,’ to equip women with key knowledge and skills to help them navigate the process of demanding assets through the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005 (MGNREGA). It addresses both informational and skills gaps, designed to work with women in small groups within their existing social networks, so that each woman receives intensive focus and opportunities for practicing skills during a condensed time period. By the end of the course, participants should be able to: • Understand the basic process for requesting a MGNREGA asset and the key local stakeholders involved • Describe a  MGNREGA asset that could improve their individual lives or livelihoods or improve the community more broadly • Articulate different ways to play a role in influencing what their community decides to build • Develop a strategy to overcome foreseen barriers to exercising their voice and agency.
title: Planning for voice: A novel approach to help women develop the skills they need to exercise voice and agency in their communities

description: The Initiative on Asian Mega Deltas (AMD) pursues establishment of rice-fodder production systems in the coastal zones of Bangladesh to enhance feed availability that is crucial not only for the well-being of livestock but also for improving the nutrition of the coastal communities in Bangladesh through milk and meat production. The performance of six fodder crops was evaluated under rainfed environment during 2022-23 and 2023-24 dry seasons to document productivity in the coastal zone and palatability by the livestock. The crops were: Barley, Proso Millet, Foxtail Millet, Maize, Sorghum, and Triticale. Among them, maize produced the highest green biomass, followed by sorghum and foxtail millet, while barley and triticale produced the lowest biomass. The consumption rate of cross-breed cows was significantly higher than that of local cows. The palatability findings suggest that sorghum, maize, foxtail and proso millets have the most potential as fodder crops in the coastal polder zone.
title: Diversified and intensified farming through rice-fodder production systems in the coastal zones of Bangladesh
input_text: The Initiative on Asian Mega Deltas (AMD) pursues establishment of rice-fodder production systems in the coastal zones of Bangladesh to enhance feed availability that is crucial not only for the well-being of livestock but also for improving the nutrition of the coastal communities in Bangladesh through milk and meat production. The performance of six fodder crops was evaluated under rainfed environment during 2022-23 and 2023-24 dry seasons to document productivity in the coastal zone and palatability by the livestock. The crops were: Barley, Proso Millet, Foxtail Millet, Maize, Sorghum, and Triticale. Among them, maize produced the highest green biomass, followed by sorghum and foxtail millet, while barley and triticale produced the lowest biomass. The consumption rate of cross-breed cows was significantly higher than that of local cows. The palatability findings suggest that sorghum, maize, foxtail and proso millets have the most potential as fodder crops in the coastal polder zone. Diversified and intensified farming through rice-fodder production systems in the coastal zones of Bangladesh

description: The project strategically selected mini-watersheds called “Learning Hubs (LHs)”, where the sluice gates are operated by water management groups of coastal polder zones to create favorable water environment for scaling improved cropping round the year by cultivation of high-value rabi crops (maize, sunflower, mungbean, okra and chili) and HYV rice in a contiguous area in dry and wet seasons. The LH farmers harvested 4.5-6.8 t/ha paddy that almost doubled the wet season productivity over traditional rice varieties. In 2023 and 2024 dry seasons, a total of 905 men and 310 women cultivated rabi crops on 160 ha in 15 LHs of the coastal zone, in which 26% farmers cultivated chilli, mungbean and okra under conventional method. The mean yield of chilli, mungbean and okra was 457 kg/ha, 687 kg/ha and 7205 kg/ha, respectively and most farmers used these crops for home consumption that reduced family expenditure and improved household nutrition.
title: Diversified and intensified farming through rice-vegetables (mungbean, okra, chili) production systems in the coastal zones of Bangladesh
