description: Vegetable adaptation trials play a pivotal role in assessing diverse varieties under specific growing conditions, aiding farmers in selecting the most suitable options for their region. In Benin, where farmers encounter challenges in accessing improved vegetable varieties, the FRESH core partner World Vegetable Center has identified 23 improved, locally adapted varieties (1 okra, 11 tomato, 7 chili pepper, and 4 habanero). Through iterative workshops and consultations with key stakeholders, these varieties will undergo the World Vegetable Center's variety release process. This basket of new, improved vegetable varieties empowers local seed companies offer and distribute desirable seed to farmers, offering substantial potential to enhance vegetable supply and address challenges faced by farmers in Benin.

description: This platform provides raw (anonymized) data of over 14062 milk samples submitted by milk collection centers in Mbarabra, Kirihura, Kazoo, and Ntungamo in Uganda. The data was recorded through 75 milk analyzers installed by the Ugandan Dairy Development Authority in randomly selected local milk collection centers. The platform allows one to select a custom date range (e.g., the last 30 days) and obtain the average butter fat (%), average SNF (%), average protein (%), and average added water (%) of samples taken for each milk collection center. The platform also reports the total number of samples submitted to each Milk Collection Centre (MCC) during the selected period. In addition to averages by MCCs, the platform also provides the evolution of overall averages over the chosen time frame (using moving averages).

description: The Global Biotic Stress Monitoring and Screening Network (Global BioNET) was established, aiming to enhance the surveillance and monitoring of rice diseases and pests, crucial for early detection and effective management. In 2023, substantial progress was made in setting up national and regional surveillance networks in Bangladesh, India, and Vietnam. BioNET-Bangladesh was launched after identifying major rice diseases and experts through a survey. In India, global BioNET was launched in agreement with the "All India Coordinated Research Project on Rice" (AICRPR), a well-established system for monitoring rice diseases and pests. In Vietnam, the BioNET-Vietnam network was marked by a scientific workshop that focused on enhancing cooperation among research institutions, improving the evaluation of rice varieties, and enhancing research on resistance genes. In 2024, BioNET was introduced to African rice pathologists. These activities represent major steps in addressing rice diseases and pests at both national and global levels.

description: This study evaluated Participatory Adaptive Trials of early bulking potato varieties in two locations of Bangladeshi over two years. Among ten varieties assessed, BARI ALU 79 emerged as the highest yielder with superior tuber size, adaptability, and potential for improving food security and livelihoods. Gender-sensitive farmer preferences showed that male farmers prioritized yield, while female farmers valued color and culinary traits, emphasizing the need for integrating diverse farmer insights into variety selection. By capitalizing on the early bulking traits of BARI ALU 79, this variety has the potential to significantly improve farmers' livelihoods and boost food security in Bangladesh. Future collaboration with seed companies and ongoing farmers engagement is crucial for successful adoption and market alignment.

The goal of the Local Indicator Selection Process (LISP) is to co-develop a set of performance indicators with stakeholders in each Agroecology Living Landscape (ALL) that are relevant for and customized to their farming systems and respond to the vision and interventions that will be implemented in the ALL. description:
HOLPA consists of two parts to permit both context specificity and global comparison of results: (1) a set of global performance indicators (2) the Local Indicator Selection Process (LISP), in which food system actors co-design metrics of agroecological performance in a given context. Together, they constitute a framework for holistic localized performance assessment, or HOLPA, which can be applied across diverse farming contexts and agroecological activities. The evidence will enable communities to see the impact of agroecology on things that matter to them, while also giving investors and other decision-makers a clear picture of agroecology’s performance under a wide variety of conditions._x000D_
In 2024, Local performance indicators have been selected in 15 communities across eight countries and incorporated into the HOLPA tool. Data has been collected from more than 1,600 households and has been analyzed. Country reports are under production.
title: Holistic Localized Agroecology Performance Assessment (HOLPA) tool for assessing the performance of fields, farms and landscapes transitioning to agroecology

HOLPA consists of two parts to permit both context specificity and global comparison of results: (1) a set of global performance indicators (2) the Local Indicator Selection Process (LISP), in which food system actors co-design metrics of agroecological performance in a given context. Together, they constitute a framework for holistic localized performance assessment, or HOLPA, which can be applied across diverse farming contexts and agroecological activities. The evidence will enable communities to see the impact of agroecology on things that matter to them, while also giving investors and other decision-makers a clear picture of agroecology’s performance under a wide variety of conditions._x000D_
In 2024, Local performance indicators have been selected in 15 communities across eight countries and incorporated into the HOLPA tool. Data has been collected from more than 1,600 households and has been analyzed. Country reports are under production. Holistic Localized Agroecology Performance Assessment (HOLPA) tool for assessing the performance of fields, farms and landscapes transitioning to agroecology

description: Food system transformation require reforms at global, national, and local levels to address prevailing structural weaknesses exacerbated by multiple crisis. As context matters, the question of what works where, why, and how for scaling innovations for achieving impact requires the application of political economy and policy analysis. Evidence-based from political economy analysis are critical to understanding the [dis-]enabling policy, institutional and governance conditions contributing to the success or failure of development interventions and innovations. This Political Economy and Policy Analysis (PEPA) Sourcebook for food systems transformations is a unique collection of frameworks and analytical tools for unraveling the interaction between policies and economic processes to unpack the power relationships, ideas, policy risks and decision making. This spans across food and nutrition; land and water; and climate and ecology systems to design politically feasible and technically sound development programs for achieving greater impact at the national and local levels.

description: The proposed innovation involves making quality visible at milk aggregation points by installing simple quality monitoring equipment. Installing milk analyzers at milk collection centers will enable quick and easy testing of milk delivered by smallholder farmers on compositional quality of the milk, such as butter fat and Solid Non-Fat (protein, carbohydrates, and minerals). The milk analyzer will be paired with a custom application that runs on a tablet computer that can be used to keep track of milk samples. This will enable milk collection centers to increase the quality of their aggregate milk and negotiate a quality premium to processors demanding high-quality milk. (Part of) this premium can be passed on to farmers to encourage them to supply better-quality milk.

description: This Guide is intended for researchers and practitioners who wish to better understand and transform gender norms as the root cause of gender inequalities and women’s disempowerment in agrifood systems (AFSs). Understanding the impact of gender transformative interventions, as well as the links between gender norms and other AFS outcomes, requires high-quality data and measurement tools designed to measure changes in gender norms. Yet, prior to the development of this Guide, there was no existing, ready-to-use tool to measure and track gender norms specific to AFSs. To address this gap, the CGIAR Gender Equality Initiative developed this Guide, which contains step-by-step guidelines and templates to aid users in the participatory development of measures of gender norms in AFS and, where applicable, draws on empirical examples based on piloting of the Guide in Nigeria and Tanzania.

description: In Work Package 3, which focuses on behavioral intelligence, we seek to pinpoint interventions that induce faster uptake of new varieties. Specifically, we consider varieties which we believe will have effects in the 5 CGIAR impact areas. We run parallel experiments in Ethiopia, India, Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda to allow us to generate externally applicable knowledge about the general constraints, as well as unique local barriers or opportunities, to adoption of new varieties that farmers face. By coordinating closely on what interventions to implement, and implementing joint survey modules, we will be able to pool the data and conduct a meta-analysis to study what interventions effectively increase adoption of varieties, and the extent to which their effectiveness depends on the traits of the promoted varieties. The evidence attached to this innovation provides an overview of registered trials and design for meta-analysis research, which will evaluate common intervention across different contexts.

description: The Paris Agreement encourages countries to track and report on their progress in adapting to climate change. But there are no suitable frameworks and tools are not suited for tracking adaptation for international reporting, more so for the livestock sector. TAiLS tool is designed to enable governments to track if adaptation is taking place across space and time and its outcomes. The tool has been co-produced in consultation with livestock keepers and government officials in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda. It integrates a set of indicators related to three dimensions, i.e., climatic hazards, impacts, and adaptive capacity and actions. The tool is also customized to leverage on the existing dataflows at national and subnational levels of government.

description: This institutional innovation provides tools and approaches for partner assessments and characterization to identify current strengths, partners' own change ambitions, capacity development priorities, and define partner roles and responsibilities in regional networks. Also, NARES are assisted in defining their own improvement plans, informed by reviewers insights. Since 2019, 128 in-depths assessments have been conducted in Africa and Asia. Critical developments in 2024 include: 1. Assessment of a 36 NARES programs; 2. Piloting of Scaling Breeding Operations (SBO) grants with three NARES in Africa (NRCRI, NARO and ZARI) to support their crop programs to implement improvement plans and 3. Support to cost 41 breeding pipelines in order to build accurate budgets and optimize resource allocation.  Many networks are now reaching the point where most Level 1 partners have been assessed. It is becoming feasible to develop a regional breeding strategy with responsibilities attributed within networks based on network member capacity.

description: Product Design Teams (PDT) were introduced and further scaled in 2023 among NARES partners. In 2024, 31 PDT meetings were held, bringing the total number of PDTs conducted since 2022 to 95, covering 15 crops in 24 countries. Approximately 400 national Target Product Profiles (TPPs) have been developed through these meetings. They are currently being uploaded to the Breeding Portal which makes the information publicly accessible through GloMIP (https://glomip.cgiar.org). PDTs are NARES-led with participation and support from CGIAR through ABI-TRANSFORM. NARES leadership of PDTs and the involvement of multistakeholder national participants has been key to ensuring client-driven prioritization, national ownership and alignment of CGIAR breeding efforts with national priorities as requested by various NARES consultations.  National TPPs are aggregated in regional network meetings to define regional market segments and regional TPPs that are pursued by CGIAR breeding programs to ensure they are aligned with national needs.

description: Bananas and plantains are crucial for food security and smallholder livelihoods in Africa. Diseases like Xanthomonas wilt of banana (BXW) threaten production. Traditional disease surveillance methods lack accuracy. We developed a deep-learning system to detect BXW-affected stems in mixed landscapes in Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo using Red, Green, Blue (RGB) and multispectral (MS) images from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), improved through pansharpening algorithms. Two deep-learning models, Yolo-V8 and Faster R-CNN, were compared. Our system achieved precision, recall, and F1 scores between 75% and 99% for detecting healthy and BXW-infected stems. RGB and panchromatic (PAN) images performed well, while multispectral images struggled due to lower resolution, though certain vegetation indexes showed potential for larger-area detection. This research highlights the promise of UAV imagery and deep learning for crop health assessment, offering a novel approach to BXW detection, revolutionizing agricultural practices, and enhancing food security and early disease management in Africa.

description: Pigeonpea and chickpea crop improvement networks for ESA were established through a series of meetings at regional and country levels (Product Design Teams- PDTs) duly involving stakeholders along the whole teams and identified country specific MSs and TPPs, that led to develop 3 and 4 regional market segments (MSs) and target product profiles (TPPs), respectively in pigeonpea and chickpea. Based on the strengths of the NARS and country priorities, agreed on regional breeding pipelines to be led by network NARS member countries. CIMMYT leads over all coordination, trialling, product advancement and on-farm testing strategies. Identified 5 regional priority and 3 pre-breeding priority traits to be included in breeding pipelines that are well designed to capture breeding program optimization plans. Also noticed upcoming niche markets like green vegetable types for MSs refinement. In Tanzania conducted a market survey with VC actors in 7 chickpea potential areas.

description: ICARDA’s Germplasm Health unit (GHU) is responsible for the monitoring, clearance and documentation of safe germplasm movement at the Center's locations in Lebanon and Morocco. All incoming and outgoing genetic resources and breeding germplasm must go through a strict quarantine monitoring system, including seed health testing. To confirm the health status of seed samples, the GHU conducts different types of tests based on the nature of the pest to be identified. In this manual, we listed and described the procedures of diagnostic tools validated by ICARDA’s GHU for detection of cereal seed-borne pests.

description: The synergy of pathogen diagnostics, epidemiology, and advanced digital disease detection systems holds immense potential for elevating continuous monitoring, rapid diagnosis, and real-time tracking of crop diseases in resource-constrained southern regions. AfricaRice and the John Innes Centre (JIC) collaborate on the Plant Health Initiative, developing TIDIS—a portable, scalable point-of-care management system for disease identification. TIDIS employs sequencing and analysis of blast-infected rice leaf samples, enabling virulence genomic profiling and polymorphic gene definition through bioinformatics and Wet-lab PCR pooling techniques. Currently, TIDIS implementation highlights the diversity of Ugandan isolates compared to those from Cote d’Ivoire, prompting further sample collection for result validation in hotspot areas. Ongoing analysis of newly sequenced datasets aims to enhance tree informativeness and pooling efficiency, marking significant progress in combating crop diseases.

description: In collaboration with the World Modelers program, CGIAR Initiative on Digital Innovation soft-launched the Digital Dojo online platform that enables system dynamics modeling researchers in CGIAR and partner institutions to test what-if scenarios and facilitates informed policy and investment decisions at multiple scales (from a location-specific local-level to national and regional-scale). Built on an open-source modeling framework, Dojo, the Digital Dojo provides a suite of features for digital twin and system modeling researchers to register and transform datasets and operate containerized modeling tools. Additionally, its artificial intelligence-based AI Assistant tool allows users to conduct literature search and review  in natural languages, leveraging Large Language Models. As of December 2023, the platform hosts 27 models and 264 datasets, all of which have been contributed by partners throughout the development process. The platform is at the beta stage for the public testing.

description: Southern rice black-streaked dwarf disease virus (SRBSDV) emerged in China in 2001 and has since spread to Vietnam, Japan, Korea, and most recently, Northern India in 2022. In response, IRRI's pathologists, with support from PHI, organized an online workshop in November 2022 involving experts from China, India, and Vietnam. Discussions addressed SRBSDV's situation in India, sharing outbreak experiences, and proposing plans for surveillance and diagnostics. An SRBSDV-BioNet was established for standardized detection, collaboration, and research. In 2023, the network achieved two major milestones: (i) a follow-up hybrid webinar on SRBSDV management occurred on July 5, in collaboration with Punjab Agricultural University, and (ii) the development of standardized detection protocols and guidelines for preventive measures for SRBSDV. Coordinated by IRRI, the network aimed to develop an interim management strategy for SRBSDV in India, providing guidance to local farmers to protect their rice fields from this disease.

description: In 2023, data collection continued to determine the activity range of soap and botanical product formulations, alone and in mixtures (soap and botanical products) to control banana aphids. A dose dependent relationship was found for a pyrethrin preparation and a neem-based formulation (crude and commercial). However, mortalities were low, except when mixed with soap. These tests will continue in 2024 and will be used to determine potential formulations to test in the field. Field tests of soap and botanicals initiated in 2022/2023 were suspended due to the prolonged rainy season between March and December 2023. These tests will be resumed in 2024. 10 candidate generalist potential aphid predators have been indentified and will be studied in the field in 2024. Two potential parasitoid species are under functional study on banana aphid and have been sent for molecular sequence evaluation using barcoding gene sequences. These data will be available in 2024.

description:
Better Management Practices (BMPs) for farming genetically improved farmed tilapia (GIFT) were developed to support the development and scaling of tilapia farming in Northeast Africa. The BMPs manual was published to provide guidelines for sustainable tilapia production systems in and to serve as a handbook for aquaculture technicians/practitioners from different stakeholders such as I/NGOs and private sectors._x000D_
BMPs emphasize the optimal use of production inputs such as good broodstock and appropriate feeds for each specific stage. They also underscore the proper management necessary for rearing broodstock and collecting eggs and for better nursing approaches for fry after the eggs hatch, with a focus on nutrition. Attending carefully to these BMPs ensures that the available resources and operation elements are used properly, without compromising the protection of the environment.
title: Best management practices for commercial tilapia reproduction in Northeast Africa

description: The CGIAR Ontologies Community of Practice harnesses international expertise in knowledge representation and ontology development to produce missing ontologies, identifies best practices, and guides data labelling by teams managing multidisciplinary information platforms to release the FAIR data underpinning the evidence of research impact (Arnaud et al, 2020). Ontologies CoP is instrumental for advancing semantic interoperability across the CGIAR’s diverse and ever-growing agricultural research datasets The CoP stimulates exchanges between domain experts and experts in ontology design, knowledge modeling, ontology-driven applications, and semantic web technologies. The role of agrisemantics in FAIR principles, a role that grows now thanks to rapid advances in natural language (NLP) processing, likely needs to extend to innovative AI-driven digital tools. AI technologies often rely on extensive data encapsulated in large language models (LLMs), potentially lacking precision in specialist areas such as agri-food research. The CoP has already initiated dialogues around this extended roles through webinars.

description: The IITA's yam breeding currently operates with two functional breeding pipelines, white yam, and water yam, that serve three product profiles defined for the market segments (https://cimmyt-eibp-prd.azurewebsites.net/bpdc/my-page). The white yam breeding pipeline serves two market segments: early maturing bushy/semi-dwarf white yam with less tendency to climb and intermediate or late maturing white yam. Each pipeline, based on market demand and consumer preferences, is at a different stage of modernization. In line with germplasm development, and during 2023, the yam breeding has simultaneous work with its NARES and advanced research partners. The NARES including UAC in Benin Republic, SARI/CRI in Ghana, CNRA, Bouake/Côte d’Ivoire, NRCRI/Umudike in Nigeria, Ethiopia, Uganda, and DR Congo. The breeding program has developed and shared progenies originating from high-performing crosses in the NARSE network.

description: This innovation aims to control insect pest, rodents and mycotoxin in stored cereals. Storage of crops in a non-hermetic system in the tropics not only favors mycotoxin contamination but also leads to insect infestation, rodent attack, and loss in quality. These results in both quantitative and qualitative losses which negatively affects incomes and livelihoods. Smallholder women farmers and processors who store their harvest and market weekly to sustain their lives are the most affected. The objective of the reported innovation was to test an auto-generated CO2-anti-rodent-hermetic storage cocoons equipped with solar powered Ecowise® monitoring system for small scale farmers and processors.
title: Mycotoxin control: Auto CO2-generated anti-rodent hermetic storage cocoons equipped with solar powered Ecowise® monitoring system for small scale farmers and processors.

description: This innovation is about the validation and performance of rust resistance genes. The development of rust-resistant varieties depends on the presence of efficient rust-resistance genes, and the utilization of these genes in breeding programs relies on their effectiveness. Field assessments conducted under natural infection conditions provide valuable information regarding the efficacy of seedling resistance genes against various rust pathogens. Alongside assessing seedling resistance genes, evaluating sources containing adult-plant resistance genes can be considered during the adult-plant stage. The three wheat rust trap nurseries comprising the yellow, stem, and leaf rust resistance genes were planted in several locations in Morocco and Lebanon under natural conditions. The yellow and leaf rust trap nurseries were planted at Tel Amara in Lebanon and Allal Tazi in Morocco, respectively.
title: Field-based assessment of the effectiveness of rust resistance genes under field conditions in Morocco and Lebanon

description: Five neem-based formulations were developed to promote the Biopesticide-based Integrated Pest Management (IPM) of cowpea (Maruca vitratta, Aphis craccivora, Megalurothrips sjostedti, and Clavigralla tomentosicollis) and maize pests, including African armyworm and the invasive fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda). The formulations include (i) Neem oil Concentrate, (ii) Neem grain cake, (iii) Neem oil concentrate fortified with Eucalyptus leaf powder, (iv) Neem oil concentrate fortified with Hyptis leaf powder, and (v) Neem oil concentrate fortified with Lantana leaf powder. Procedures were established for manufacturing concentrates including packing and storage, and working solutions for field application using knap snack sprayers. The formulations were validated under researcher-managed trials and compared with synthetic pesticide applications. Training was organized for farmers and extension officials on manufacturing and applications of biopesticides. It also included the determination of pest incidence and decisions on IPM application. These formulations are ready for scaling, which will be pursued as the next steps.

description: In Africa, lowland rice is severely impacted by the African rice gall midge (AfRGM), Orseolia oryzivora. It has become a significant problem in Nigeria in recent years, with reports of its increased pest status. The larvae of AfRGM infect rice tillers during the vegetative growth stage and produce tubular galls called onion leaves or silver shoots, which causes crop damage. Infestation causes irreversible damage to the tillers, which inhibits their capacity to produce more leaves or a panicle. Recent interest in IPM has focused renewed attention on other approaches among which is the use of habitat manipulation for the conservation of natural enemies. Paspalum gall midge, O. bonzii infests Paspalum scrobiculatum, a common weed in rice fields. Paspalum gall midge cannot attack rice but is an alternative host for the two main parasitoids of AfRGM (Platygaster diplosisae – larval parasitoid and Aprostocetus procerae – pupal parasitoid).
title: Promotion of natural biological control of African rice gall midge (AfRGM) through habitat manipulation in Nigeria

description: Selection of meritorious parents and their matings that maximize genetic gain are key action steps to in yam breeding.  To optimize parent selection and identify their best cross combinations complementary to their genetic characteristics, a Genomic Prediction Cross-Performance pipeline  was developed and integrated into yambase analytical functions. The pipeline utilizes both phenotypic and molecular marker data to compute total genetic and breeding values of the progenies for all potential matings between the potential parents.

description: The classical approach to developing improved yam varieties is challenging and time-consuming. In 2023, IITA achieved significant progress in modernizing the yam breeding program through the development and deployment of molecular tools. Utilizing the yam product profile, 14 key agronomic and tuber quality traits were identified, leading to marker-trait association studies using various genetic models. Numerous markers across yam genomes were identified and documented. Promising SNP (Single Nucleotide Polymorphism) markers for nine traits and validated SNP markers for seven traits were identified, employing haplotype/allele segregation analysis and investigating putative genes. In marker-assisted selection, over 3,000 genotypes from early-generation trials were selected, and validated markers were tested for product advancement. To uncover genomic regions related to tuber quality traits, additional analyses were conducted, considering five mapping populations for a food quality index based on instrument and sensory assays, leading to the identification of several markers linked to the index.
title: Marker-trait association identified, developed and deployed for key traits in yam breeding to mainstream best practices in breeding pipelines

description: Feminisation of agriculture’ is generally utilized to indicate an expansion of women’s engagement in agricultural production, as labourers or decision-makers. Feminization of agriculture is often reported as a global trend. While literature on feminization of agriculture (FoA) has seen a steady rise in the last decade, there is little consensus on defining feminization of agriculture and consistent approaches that provide comparative quantitative data on FoA are lacking. This innovation is a methodological approach to assessing the extent of FoA, deployed on DHS data from South and South-East Asia.
title: A methodological approach to the assessment of feminization of agricultural labour through demographic and health survey data

description: This innovation aims to support Voluntary Sustainability Systems (VSS) supporting the development of agrifood value chains and markets to enhance gender equality and social inclusion in value chains. description: Since 2018, the European Union and several other countries have decided to ban the sale and use of many pesticides containing thiram and thiamethoxam molecules, affecting shipments of seeds treated with these chemicals from entering these countries. Accordingly, a new fungicide formulation should be sought as an alternative to Celest Top (thiamethoxam 262.5 g/l; fludioxonil 25 g/l; difenoconazole 25 g/l) and Vitavax (carboxin 200 g/l; thiram 200 g/l), which are the chemicals most used as seed dressing to treat the wheat seed-borne diseases. The research was conducted using varieties of bread wheat (Faiza and Najia) and durum wheat (Faraj and Jabal). The results revealed that the newly tested formulation (fludioxonil 25g/l; sedaxane 25g/l) was effective against common bunt (100% success rate). The new fungicide formulation outperformed Celest Top in all evaluated parameters related to  production. Further validation with large quantities of seed is due.
title: A new seed-dressing fungicide formulation for wheat

description: Directly sourcing from smallholder farmers can significantly improve their livelihoods and productivity. Input credit systems have also been proven to effectively enhance productivity and livelihoods of smallholders, reduce rural poverty, and promote sustainable agricultural practices. These initiatives bridge seed supply gaps, and establish risk management strategies, collaboration with seed enterprises, and in-house seed production units are some options that can be used. To support this, it's essential to establish training guidelines for agronomic and post-harvest skills, fertilizer recommendations, and seed quality support for producer cooperatives, especially for women, along with financial literacy and agribusiness skills training. Financing is also crucial to enhance the commercialization of high-demand diversified produce and products for farmers, and training and working capital to grow and establish new crops are essential. To overcome supply chain constraints and increase efficiency, digital registration and payment processes for producers are being explored.

description: A prototype surveillance platform was developed and validated that allows the visualization of the areas under surveillance for tropical race 4, unifying the internal Agrocalidad system (GIA) with the Tumaini mapping platform. This prototype platform collects, integrates, and analyzes data on suspicious cases and Foc TR4. Users in general, especially the producing sector, will have the opportunity to know in real time the coverage of the national TR4 Phytosanitary Surveillance System in all the banana producing areas of Ecuador, directly on the website of the NPPO (Agrocaliad). This tool process maximizes data analyses and speeds up decision making processes in cases of suspicious TR4 cases. As a complement, drone-based surveillance is in the pipeline, with 2 acquired drones and 30 technical officers trained.

description: We created a virtual food policy expert using a customized AI chatbot system to understand the benefits and limitations of chatbots in supporting food policy research. A comparative assessment was made of the results obtained from asking the same food policy-related questions to different AI sources, including the customized AI virtual food policy expert. Chatbots proved useful for summarizing research and providing initial information. However, their usefulness depends on the volume of information uploaded and their ability to draw from various sources. While they can answer a specific set of questions, for detailed and country-specific information, human experts are still needed.

description: In Nigeria, the cassava seed system is successfully integrating newly released varieties into the value chain. The breeding program continues SAH plantlets propagation for late-stage multilocation trials, producing 14 varieties for various product profiles. A total of 123,567 plantlets were multiplied at the SAH facility, contributing to breeder seed production. Modifications to SAH technology, such as nodal procedures and innovative screen house systems, were well-received. While poundable and fine face varieties were downscaled due to low demand, poundable will be promoted in the Northern part of Nigeria. Additionally, 386 plantlets were produced for a potential candidate line in the RTB breeding program, showing superiority in trials. The IITA breeding program ensured nucleus seed stock materials for EGS companies, delivering pencil stems of high-demand and new varieties for breeder seed production. IITA-GoSeed established 60 ha breeder seed fields with varieties like game changer and baba 70 leading production.
title: Rapid multiplication technologies (semi-autotrophic hydroponics) to produce quality planting material of cassava improved varieties for early generation seed production by seed companies/producers

description: Five improved rice varieties, released in countries of the Economic Community of West African States, were introduced to members of women’s cooperatives in Sipilou and Bouaké, Côte d’Ivoire, and the Ahafo Ano North and South-West districts of Ghana for their assessment. The introduced varieties were NERICA L-A9 Sub1 and WITA 4 Sub1 (high-yielding and resistant to lodging; released in Nigeria), ARICA 3 (high-yielding and tolerant to disease and insect; released in Mali), ARICA 2 (high-yielding and tolerant to disease and insect; released in Guinea Conakry), and Orylux 6 (highly aromatic and long grain rice; released in multiple countries). The farmers were trained in improved agronomic practices using demonstration field plots and in assessing postharvest characteristics. description:
Biodiversity management is a design of a sustainable ecosystem for the benefit of the human and natural environment. Rice cultivation is mostly grown as monoculture and often linked to high pesticide use impacting human and environmental health. In the rice system, biodiversity management aims to find optimal combinations of rice and other crops considering space and time for improvement of ecosystem services, human health and economic benefit for rice farmers.       _x000D_
In this innovation development, farmer’s survey guided the selection of non-rice crops to diversify the rice system. Rice with mung bean grown on the bunds cultivated in wet season and watermelon cultivated in dry season are evaluated for its impact on ecosystem services and yield. Initial data analysis has shown that the rice-mung bean-watermelon system positively resulted in increasing cost-benefit ratio, lowering thrips damage and GHG emission compared to the non-diversified system, whereas grain yield is comparable in both systems.

description: The effectiveness of (Fawligen®) (Spodoptera frugiperda multiple nucleopolyhedrovirus) against FAW in maize was studied in Zambia in 2023 over five weeks. Threshold-based Fawligen sprays applied to plots established from seed treated with FortenzaTM Duo or Fortenza® were compared to calendar-based sprays of Fawligen applied to plots established from untreated seed, untreated control, and Ampligo®/Denim Fit® sprays on plots established from untreated seed. In plots established from untreated maize seed, calendar-based Fawligen sprays (7 in total) effectively reduced plant damage relative to the untreated control at 7, 21, 28, and 35 days after crop emergence (DAE). In contrast, threshold-based sprays (5 in total) reduced FAW damage only at 28 and 35 DAE. When threshold-based Fawligen sprays were applied in Fortenza Duo or Fortenza plots, plant damage was significantly lower than the control throughout the five weeks of assessment only in the former.

description: The highlands of North Shoa in Amhara region are dominated by cereals (wheat, barley and tef) followed by food legumes. The productivity of cereals and food legumes is due to biotic and abiotic factors as well as insufficient input supplies like planting materials and other inputs. Farmers are trying to add vegetatively propagated horticultural crops (tubers, bulbs and fruit trees) into the framing systems. Horticultural crops are very important to diversify diet, incomes and reduce risks of cereal and legume crops. There are many temperate fruits (apple, peach, pear, plum etc), potato and garlic varieties developed by the research system but most of them are not demonstrated to the farming communities. Horticultural crops are becoming important due to increased small scale irrigation in the highlands as opposed to cereal and legume crops and promotion and awareness programs on nutrition.

description: Entomopathogenic fungi (EPFs) provide a unique opportunity to efficiently control fall armyworm (FAW) in small-scale farming systems. Surveys were conducted in the five agroecological zones of Cameroon for collection, isolation, and identification of EPFs associated with FAW in maize fields. Cameroon’s EPF isolates were used, which have also proven effective on other pests. Pathogenicity and dose-response tests were conducted on the immature stages of FAW under laboratory conditions. TEPFs of the genera Beauveria, Metarhizium, Aspergillus, and Fusarium were found to effectively kill FAW larvae in the field; however, the best results were registered in the laboratory for EPF isolates collected, which were effective on eggs, larvae, and pupae. Metarhizium anisopliae’s isolate MIITAC 11.3.4 caused significantly higher mortality rates and mycosis, followed by Beauveria bassiana’s isolate BIITAC 6.2.2 varying between 84 to 96% and 83 to 90%, respectively. Results show these strains' potential for developing biopesticide formulations against FAW.

description: Entomopathogenic fungi-based formulations using two Beauveria bassiana ( BIITAC10.3.3, BIITAC6.2.2) and one Metharizium anisopliae (MIITAC6.2.2) isolates were formulated. The efficacy of these formulations, i.e., virulence against banana aphid, Pentalonia nigronervosa, the vector of the banana bunchy top virus (BBTV), was tested based on preservation conditions under screenhouse and field conditions. Results showed that conidia viability in formulations decreased with temperature, storage time, and increased exposure time under UV rays. High conidia viability was obtained at 4°C compared to ambient temperatures (25°C & 35°C) at 2 and 5 months, BIITAC10.3.3 and MIITAC6.2.2. High UV protection was revealed for formulated MIITAC6.2.2 and BIITAC6.2.2. Formulations preserved for six months caused up to 60% mortality of aphids in the laboratory and greenhouse. In the field, microbial formulations were less effective compared to synthetic insecticide (imidacloprid) treatment. Overall, the microbial pesticides effectively reduce the banana aphid populations and minimize BBTV spread in the endemic areas.
title: Effective microbial biopesticide against the aphid vector (Pentalonia nigronervosa) of the banana bunchy top virus

description: The collaborative effort between the IITA yam breeding program and NRCRI established on-farm trials at 18 locations across nine Nigerian states to evaluate two candidate clones, TDr1302042 and TDr1302100, alongside benchmark cultivars Asiedu (TDr8902665) and local checks. Twenty stands of each genotype were planted on mounds, and the trials employed a participatory variety selection (PVS) model involving various end-users and stakeholders. Through structured questionnaires, 500 respondents, including farmers, processors, marketers, and consumers, provided feedback on candidate clone performance. Data collected covered tuber fresh yield, tuber browning, flour yield, peel loss, and proximate analysis. Both test clones demonstrated favorable attributes over the checks, with TDr1302100 exhibiting high food quality in boiled and pounded consumption. Overall, the agronomic, nutritional, and food quality assessment supports the official release of candidate TDr1302100, which has shown remarkable yield potential and adaptation across diverse Nigerian regions. TDr1302100 was officially released in Nigeria on January 11, 2024.

description: Experiments with different management tactics were established in two plots of APBOSMAM Cooperative in Northern Peru. These experiments evaluate the effectiveness of different IDM strategies. To identify and manage predisposition factors, soil samples were collected and analyzed in 5 plots. Nematode genera (phytopathogenic and free-living nematodes) present in the field were identified. It was also possible to characterize affected plots for physicochemical parameters. Preliminary analyses indicated that pH and CIC might be related to high disease incidence. Three experiments were established within two plots of APBOSMAM. These look to evaluate strategies for: preventive management and the rehabilitation of affected areas., For example, cover crops have been established, and effect on inoculum level is being evaluated. Training activities have been developed such as the International Forum on TR4 and the workshop on the use of digital tools; massive participation indicates the level and concern and the need to increase training mechanisms.

description: The Fusarium wilt IDM work in India focusses on: Development and evaluation of consortia of bioagents possessing multiple functions for the management of Foc TR4. Elucidating the mechanism of action (Transcriptomics, microbiome, LC-MS-MS analyses, SEM analysis etc) of these biocontrol consortia. Studying the effectiveness of flooding, crop rotation (with paddy rice), growing resistant banana cultivars/mutants (with or without biopriming), application of organic amendments (e.g., cakes, FYM, Vermicompost) on reducing incidence and symptom expression of Foc TR4. Field evaluations of integrated approaches for the effective management of Foc TR4 in Grand Nain will be established in early 2024 at a disease hot spot area in Northern India.

description: Lentil and chickpea are the most important legume crops grown in the mid highlands of central Ethiopia. Productivity of both crops is affected by several biotic factors such as pod borers, aphids, wilt/root rot, foliar diseases, and viruses. Most of the plant viruses are transmitted by many aphid species and thus management of insect vectors is one of the main options for controlling viral diseases. On-farm trials were conducted at Enewary, North Shewa in 2022/23 main cropping season to identify best options for the management of emerging lentil and chickpea virus diseases and their aphid vectors. Spraying insecticides significantly minimized aphid populations and reduced the incidence of virus symptoms. The highest lentil biomass and grain yield was recorded for the early sowing date combined with insecticide sprays. The results obtained indicated that management of viruses and aphid vectors can be achieved through adjusting sowing date combined with limited insecticide sprays.
title: Integrated management of chickpea and lentil viruses and their vectors in North Shewa, Ethiopia

description: Stable Foods offers irrigation as service based on the biophysical and socio-ecoenomic setup of the farmer. The technological interventions are not one size fits all, instead they are geared towards developing interventions that match the end user. For example, a ground truthing exercise identifies the terrain, water source, the  farmers prevailing conditions such as affordability, land to labor ratio, irrigation potential, and distance to markets. Thereafter, the information is aggregated to develop a mechanization niche that describes the level of intensification, labor issues and market demands. This approach goes beyond conventional irrigation design/development approach by capturing the whole irrigation development value chain.

description: The Agricultural Credit Index (AgCx) is an initiative to redesign Indian smallholders' creditworthiness based on their cashflows. More than 50% of Indian farmers struggle to access institutional finance, primarily due to inaccurate land records or status as tenant farmers without alternate collateral. Despite this, lenders have limited information for credit risk assessment. To address this, AgCx leverages digital assessments to help all farmers, particularly smallholders, tenants, and women, secure loans. The project enables farmers to obtain loans without needing to visit a bank, thus saving their time and wages, and facilitates prompt loan sanctioning. Furthermore, it allows banks and other lenders to lower their lending costs, extend their reach to farmers in remote locations, and minimize non-performing assets (NPAs).

description: Leveraging recent developments in Large Language Models (LLMs), a new Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based data query tool was developed to enable user-friendly access to scientific data collected and managed by the African Dairy Genetic Gains (ADGG) program. Currently intended users are extension workers who visit the farm to collect data for ADGG program and progressive farmers who wish to query the data collected about their farms and animals using Natural Language Inputs. The natural language inputs given by the users automatically generate Structured Query Language (SQL) queries and return responses in a user-friendly format. This approach bypasses the need for technical knowledge, allowing non-specialist users like farmers to interact with complex databases. Importantly, the system maintains context, allowing for intuitive exchanges. Additionally, it stores queries, SQL, and responses, aiding researchers to refine the process. Standard security protocols protect the database since the AI doesn't directly interact with it.
title: An Artificial Intelligence-based scientific data query tool for user-friendly access and analysis of the African Dairy Genetic Gains (ADGG) database

description: IITA's yam breeding program achieved significant success, releasing 25 varieties in West Africa over the last five years. description: Licensing agreements are an important tool that public research institutions can use to increase dissemination of publicly-bred varieties. Licensing can formalize the relationship between public and private actors in the seed sector, increase the availability and affordability of quality seed, and improve adoption of technology and, ultimately, farmers’ access to seed. While some NARES have not yet implemented licensing programs, others have, with varied licensing strategies across NARES in Africa. This Guide is designed as a tool for public research institutions and their partners, including CGIAR Centers, to guide the transfer of rights and authorization at the national level in order to use developed material and registered varieties for commercial purposes, in exchange for a predetermined payment (e.g., royalties), or performance of particular conditions. New Markets Lab, a NGO specializing in legal and regulatory analysis, has been responsible for this work which is in collaboration with Seed Equal WP5.

description: The fall armyworm (FAW) is the most important insect pest of maize crop worldwide, and it has recently become a harmful and invasive pest of summer planted maize in Lebanon. To save maize crop, a field trial was carried out during the summer of 2023 in the farmers’ field at Qob Elisa village to study the effect of pheromone traps and spraying with environmentally safe and low-risk insecticides. The results obtained showed that the peak of FAW population in the maize field was during the period of August 22 to September 15. The management of FAW before reaching this date is very important to avoid the high FAW infestation in the field. FAW damage on maize production in the field that used pheromone traps and recommended insecticides was almost unobservable compared to neighboring farmers, who followed their own practices.

description: Faba bean viruses are the major problem for Lebanese farmers, which has led to decline in faba bean productivity. In addition, aphids are the most serious insect which attack faba bean and transmit devastating virus diseases. To salvage the crop and to restore farmers’ confidence in growing faba bean, a field trial was conducted in farmers’ field to evaluate IPDM options (sowing dates, varieties, seed-treatment) to control viruses and their aphid vectors during the 2022/2023 season. The results obtained showed that the number of infected plants by viruses and aphids were higher at the 2nd sowing date than at the 1st sowing date. In addition, viruses and aphids incidence was lower in the plots planted with treated seeds compared to the untreated plots and for both sowing dates. Moreover, no aphids were recorded in the plots planted with treated seeds on all faba bean varieties sown in November.
title: On-farm validation of Integrated virus and vector management innovations on faba bean in Lebanon

description: The overall area covered by exclosures is currently increasing by 2%/year and could reach 5-7 million ha by the early 2030s. Similar rehabilitation of degraded rangelands has been fostered by establishing exclosures in different parts of Africa and Asia. This trend in exclosure expansion is attributable to their many benefits: restoring degraded landscapes, increasing carbon sequestration, and improving other ecosystem services. This can provide opportunities for livelihood diversification, and thus enhancement, decrease soil erosion and seed loss in farmlands located downslope of exclosures, thereby helping boost agricultural productivity over the medium to long term.The major agroecological transition fostered by setting up exclosures in degraded ecosystems is the shift from a free grazing system (i.e. natural) to a cut-and-carry system (i.e. knowledge/labour intensive agroecological system). The initiatives are built on previous IWMI activities. In the project areas, we developed a participatory freshwater conservation plan where exclosure is an important intervention. We will pilot and train partners, and show business models.

description: The introduction and promotion of vermicompost in the Central Rift Valley (CRV) intervention area to address the impacts of challenges of soil organic matter depletion and soil nutrient mining. This innovation can be an important input to sustainable intensification innovation bundles.  The vermicompost technology has not been widely adopted in the CRV of Ethiopia although the area is characterized by low soil fertility, high application of chemical fertilizer, and pollution of water bodies such as Ziway, Langano, Abiyata, and Shala lakes. In CRV, 268 farmers were involved in the preparation and application of vermicompost including means to earn money. Vermicompost can be made using different organic materials and adding the worms into it to do the job. Currently, in some parts of the country, it is an important organic fertilizer production process but the scientific underpinning and business model development need some focus.

description: Bean yellow mosaic virus (BYMV) is reported to occur on several legumes worldwide and caused up to 50% yield loss or more. Early detection and accurate diagnosis of viral diseases is critical for the application of appropriate control measures. The development of PCR has greatly improved the sensitivity and utility of hybridization and other nucleic acid-based assays. Immunocapture-RT-PCR (IC-RT-PCR) is another alternative where virus particles are detected without isolating RNA. This hybrid diagnostic technique is more sensitive than ELISA and RT-PCR alone. In addition, Immunocapture of virus particles step provides a simple method to isolate virus particles from plant tissue, particularly when inhibitory substances are present, and thus enables subsequent use of RT-PCR amplification. The validated molecular tool (RT-PCR and IC-RT-PCR) for detection and characterization of BYMV in legumes was developed and shared with the partners participated in the diagnostic network.
title: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay for detection and characterization of Bean yellow mosaic virus (BYMV) in legumes applied by ICARDA’s GHU

description: The Infrared-hot air drier is an eco-friendly hybrid drier used to dehydrate fruits and vegetables. Itis suited for companies and researchers. The prototype combines two methods of infrared and hot air drying, and also incorporates the Arduino open source platform to continuously monitor the temperature, humidity, time and weight of the product. The implementation of the hybrid dryer allows the dehydration of the food for its microbiological preservation and in turn delays many undesirable reactions. Dehydration reduces packaging, handling, storage and transportation costs, since the weight of the food is reduced, and in some cases the volume. The hybrid dryer can generally dehydrate fruits and vegetables.

description:
Cavendish [AAA] production landscapes along the Red River in northern Vietnam are heavily affected by Fusarium wilt TR4._x000D_
Although susceptible to Fusarium Race 1, Pisang Awak [ABB type] plants are rarely affected by TR4. Farmers have started replacing their Cavendish mats with Pisang Awak._x000D_
In the framework of the PHI, 'Formosana' [a Cavendish somaclone that is moderately resistent to TR4] has been imported in 2023 into Vietnam, from TBRI-Taiwan. These 'Formosana' plants will now be evaluated in affected production landscapes around Hanoi._x000D_
The current IPM approach to revive these Fusarium-affected Cavendish production zones comprises the use of Pisang Awak and Formosana._x000D_
In 2024, it is envisaged to add a biocontrol dimension. A consortium of biocontrol agents [mainly Trichoderma and Bacillus] developed at ICAR-NRCB, India and highly effective in the control of TR4, will be transferred to Vietnam and evaluated at project field sites.
title: IDM approach for reviving Fusarium wilt affected banana production landscapes in Northern Vietnam

description: Common bean breeding in Central America, by local programs, the Panamerican School (Zamorano) in Honduras and CIAT, pursue small-sized black beans demanded by smallholders and consumers in Guatemala and Costa Rica; and small-sized red beans demanded by smallholders and consumers in El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Costa Rica. Even though variety releases are taking place, correlation analyses between testing sites show a wide diversity of growing environments. With small investments by each national breeding program, local breeding programs are challenged to implement an effective variety identification program. Also, farmers conditions are very different to those on station. Establishing regional trials among the five Central American countries, jointly evaluating varieties from all partners, would better replicate production regions. This could be followed by in-country, large-scale on-farm trials, using the cost-effective TRICOT methodology. Such collaborative approaches are already successfully used in Africa where new bean varieties have invigorated the bean sector.

description: The African Union launched the Food Safety Strategy for Africa 2022–2036 (FSSAI), which recognises the importance of the informal food sector in African food systems. Framed as principles of engagement, these elements are meant to guide policymakers in the successful inclusion of informal food markets in national food safety systems. The development of this document, Draft Guidelines for Informal Food Sector Engagement, has benefited from conversations involving ILRI researchers, other stakeholders in the food safety space (in and outside of Africa), and the African Union Commission (AUC) Secretariat.

description: The highlands of North Shoa in Amhara region  are dominated by cereals (wheat, barley and tef) followed by food legumes. The productivity of cereals and food legumes is due to biotic and abiotic factors as well as insufficient input supplies like certified seeds, planting materials, inoculants and other inputs. Because of diseases and insect pests, acid acidity and water logging problems, farmers are reducing areas of  food legumes and growing more cereals leading to low crop diversity that can reduce soil fertility, incomes, food diversity and increase disease threats. Many cereals, food legume  and potato varieties are released by many centers and did not reach farmers due to limited demonstration and shortage of quality early generation seeds and planting materials. Poor access to quality seeds contributes to low crop productivity and limited technology scaling in north Shoa.

description: Sustainable Healthy Diets researchers from Wageningen University and Research are designing an online interactive tool ("dashboard") for policymakers in Viet Nam. When complete, the online tool will allow users to dive deeper into the results of trade-off modelling and scenario analyses. It will be organized by the desirable outcome areas of food systems transformation: (1) Health and Food Security, (2) Economy and Inclusivity, and (3) Environment and will provide details on selected indicators for each outcome area. One of the first steps in the development of this innovation was an in-country workshop held with stakeholders in November 2023. Workshop participants suggested indicators to include in the trade-off modelling, which, subsequently will appear in the online tool. This is part of this Initiative's work to promote the use of decision-support tools that stakeholders can use to navigate trade-offs in a fairer, more inclusive and more equitable way.

description: Simple-to-administer and low-priced indicators are essential tools for monitoring fruit and vegetable intake at the population level. A promising tool is the fruit and vegetable component of the Global Dietary Recommendation score (FV-GDR). The score is based on data collected using the Diet Quality Questionnaire (DQQ). Researchers from Sustainable Healthy Diets investigated the relative validity of FV-GDR in comparison to the 24-hour recall method to measure fruit and vegetable intake among 620 Vietnamese and 630 Nigerian adults. The researchers concluded that the DQQ is a promising low-burden, low-cost and simple way to calculate FV-GDR and to monitor fruit and vegetable consumption at the population level. This provides the possibility of evaluating an important aspect of diet quality in low-resource settings.

description: The country coordination units in the Sustainable Healthy Diets target countries are a central part of our strategy to strengthen the connections between CGIAR researchers and national partners in food systems policy processes. The Units are comprised of researchers from all work packages (WPs) plus Wageningen University and Research (WUR) and representatives from specific national partners. This institutional innovation is the primary pathway we will use to engage with in-country multi-stakeholder processes that improve the design and implementation of the national roadmaps towards food systems transformation for sustainable healthy diets. In addition, the Units ensure research coherence and efficiency by formalizing information sharing between WPs and with other CGIAR Initiatives working in the country. Sustainable Healthy Diets established the Units in Vietnam in 2022, in Ethiopia in 2023, and plans to establish one in Bangladesh in early 2024.

description: People routinely get exposed to multiple  zoonotic infections  as they interract with livestock or wildlife, or consume their products. These infections are  caused by  bacterial, viral or parasitic agents that may end up causing  epidemics. Public health care facilities  however do not usually have adequate facilities for detecting many of these infections to enable the implementation of  interventions in good time. This  challenge  needs to be addressed so as to develop capacity for stopping zoonotic spillover. The Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) sequencing method provides a high-resolution, real-time analysis of bacterial diversity in clinical samples, uncovering both known and novel pathogens. it uses 16S rRNA sequencing for a comprehensive characterization of bacteria but its application has been limitted to lab settings. We have assessed ONT's effectiveness in identifying bacterial communities in febrile patients’ samples from northern Kenya. We are currently refining the analysis pipelines and assessing the practicality of using portable ONT sequencers for sequencing in remote healthcare settings. Further, we intend to employ this technology for concurrent pathogen detection in humans, animals, and wildlife samples. This will transform zoonotic bacterial pathogen identification, illuminating cross-species infections and co-infections at human-livestock-wildlife interfaces, leading to precise prevention and management strategies in a one-health approach.
title: Assessing the feasibility of Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) for 16S rRNA sequencing as a diagnostic tool in detecting bacterial infections in febrile patients within a pastoral setting

description: The Farmer Interface App FIA is a digital advisory running on Android. It integrates a scouting algorithm guiding the farmer with simple symbols on how to move randomly in the field, check several crop plants, inspect them for pests (or damage symptoms), and press the right symbol to record the presence/absence of the pest. The App updated with the phenology data collected at eight constant temperatures using maize and onion as host plants, and models describing the life history of FAW were developed. These include the development time model, the development rate model, the mortality model, female fecundity, and adult (male and female) senescence. These models were therefore validated by comparing laboratory life table data with data collected at ambient temperature. FIA and VIPS were integrated by extending the FIA-cloud service to communicate with the VIPS platform.

description: Recent interest in IPM/organic farming has focused renewed attention on other approaches among which is the use of habitat manipulation for the conservation of natural enemies. Habitat manipulation is using agricultural areas/surrounding environments with the aim of conserving the population of natural enemies. Paspalum gall midge (PGM), O. bonzii infests Paspalum scrobiculatum, a common weed in rice agroecosystems. Paspalum gall midge cannot attack rice but is an alternative host for the two main parasitoids of AfRGM (Platygaster diplosisae – larval parasitoid and Aprostocetus procerae – pupal parasitoid). However, the parasitoid populations build up too late to prevent heavy AfRGM infestation.

description: Insect pests such as the rice stem borers (African rice gall midge (AfRGM) Orseolia oryzivora, and the stalk-eyed flies – Diopsis spp. are among the economically most important pests of rainfed upland/lowland and irrigated rice in West Africa. The larvae of stem borers cause significantly yield loss during the vegetative (seedlings to panicle initiation) and reproductive stages by producing silver shoots/deadhearts and whiteheads, respectively, which prevent panicle development. The extensive use of synthetic insecticides to control these pests has raised concerns regarding environmental and human health. Consequently, this has necessitated the need for alternative control measures such as the use of biopesticides: Entomopathogenic fungi and botanicals. In the present study, two Entomopathogenic fungi (Metarhizium anisopliae(MET 31); Beauveria bassiana (Bb11) and two botanical biopesticides (Azadirachta indica (Raktin); Eucalyptus sp. (Lyptol)) were assessed against (AfRGM) and Diopsis species in Nigeria.
title: Efficacy of eco-friendly biopesticides for control of African Rice Gall Midge and rice stem borers

description: Chickpea and lentil are the major legume crops grown in Ethiopia, providing people with balanced nutrition of proteins, minerals, fibers, and carbohydrates. Since 2019, farmers in the highlands of Ethiopia are losing their crops because of virus epidemics, and lentil production area in Ethiopia was reduced due to the virus infection. Knowing genetic variation and the exact identity of viruses affecting crops is essential for breeding for resistance and crop management purposes. Serological tests for more than 2000 samples showed that the most important viruses are Chickpea chlorotic stunt virus (CpCSV) on both crops, and Pea seed-borne mosaic virus (PSbMV) on lentil. Representative samples were selected and further analyzed with RT-PCR and sequenced to identify the isolates at molecular level. Phylogenetic analysis showed that the Ethiopian PSbMV isolates (5 lentil & 1 chickpea) are clustered with pathotype 2, and CpCSV isolates (3 chickpea & 2 lentil) are clustered with Serogroup-I.
title: Genetic diversity of two viruses affecting lentil and chickpea crops in the highlands of Ethiopia
input_text: Chickpea and lentil are the major legume crops grown in Ethiopia, providing people with balanced nutrition of proteins, minerals, fibers, and carbohydrates. Knowing genetic variation and the exact identity of viruses affecting crops is essential for breeding for resistance and crop management purposes. Serological tests for more than 2000 samples showed that the most important viruses are Chickpea chlorotic stunt virus (CpCSV) on both crops, and Pea seed-borne mosaic virus (PSbMV) on lentil. Representative samples were selected and further analyzed with RT-PCR and sequenced to identify the isolates at molecular level. Phylogenetic analysis showed that the Ethiopian PSbMV isolates (5 lentil & 1 chickpea) are clustered with pathotype 2, and CpCSV isolates (3 chickpea & 2 lentil) are clustered with Serogroup-I. Genetic diversity of two viruses affecting lentil and chickpea crops in the highlands of Ethiopia

description: Semiochemicals from cowpea plant parts have been found to attract Maruca vitrata and its parasitoids Liragathis javana. Few host plant volatiles identified from cowpea have been shown to attract M. vitrata, including butyl butyrate, limonene, 4-ethylpropiophenone, 1H-indol-4-ol, octyl butanoate, and 2-methyl-3-phenylpropanal. However, these attractants have limited applications and have not been demonstrated as semiochemicals in multi-site situations and different legume cropping systems. The GC-MS analysis performed presented some specifics compounds of the attracted cowpea organs. Those specific compounds are the potential attractants for M. vitrata and its parasitoid L. javana. The validation of those chemical compounds for their use in biocontrol strategy for Maruca species is ongoing.

description: Management of maize lethal necrosis (MLN) by the smallholders needs an integrated approach, as the disease is caused by a combination of viruses, especially Maize Chlorotic Mottle Virus (MCMV) and Sugarcane Mosaic Virus (SCMV). An experiment was undertaken in 2022 at the MLN Screening Facility at Naivasha, Kenya, under controlled conditions, using biopesticides for the control of thrips and aphids that act as vectors for MLN-causing viruses, in combination with MLN-resistant hybrids. Preliminary results showed significant effect of biopesticides in combination with native genetic resistance to MLN. These results need to be further validated in farmers' fields.
title: Integrated management of maize lethal necrosis (MLN), including native genetic resistance and biopesticides, for supporting smallholder farmers

description: We developed a gender inclusion checklist specifically for breeders and management of farm operations to improve inclusion of women in the workplace. The document includes an action scale assessment system to ensure gender inclusion initiatives are implemented on the organizational and farm station levels.  This checklist will help managers and breeders acknowledge the strengths and weaknesses of their organization’s gender inclusion initiatives and measures. It will also help guide and encourage the discussion of gender-related issues within within the organization.  We suggest improvements to increase women staff in five key Action Areas: work organization, Improvement of work equipment, making facilities inclusive, capacity development, and compliance.

description: Under the project 'Consortium for Improving Agriculture-based Livelihoods in Central Africa', the Centre of Nuclear Nuclear Techniques in Food and Agriculture coordinated research towards development of isotope techniques to make cassava and banana production systems more climate change resilient. Using precipitation data from local measuring stations and 'Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data' satellite imagery data for Rwanda, Burundi, and DR Congo, variability and trend analysis has been executed to understand the change in water availability and frequency in dry spells. In collaboration with the Alliance Bioversity & CIAT, a field experiment was conducted to validate and up-scale the use of stable carbon isotope techniques for assessing the intrinsic water use efficiency of cassava under field conditions. This research facilitates understanding of the plant’s behavior under drought in the field at an early bulking stage. This and other indicators will be included as parameters for breeding drought-tolerant cassava.
title: Isotope techniques for the introduction of climate-resilient varieties in cassava and banana production system

description: The pathology team at IRRI developed 40 single nucleotide polymorphism markers that can distinguish 12 Asian Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) (a rice bacteria) populations and used them to monitor the bacteria (Xoo) population in Asia. The distribution of 12 Xoo populations was mapped out and the effectiveness of Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) resistance genes in different countries was predicted. The data is currently uploaded on PathoTracer app.

description: Research Protocol describing the Participatory Socio-Agronomic Research carried out in Northern Bangladesh, which includes on-farm agronomic trials and trainings but also nutrition and marketing trainings. In the agronomic trials  different cropping patterns are compared. These cropping patterns are more diverse and include crops with higher nutritional value that the conventional ones, which often are based 100% on cereal and/or carbohydrate rich cops. Agronomic data as well as parameters to assess production costs and benefits is collected. Agronomic trainings and marketing trainings are linked to these agronomic trials and further in some location farmer HH are given nutrition trainings. This will allow assessing the contribution of improved access to knowledge about nutrition on diversification in crop production.
title: Research Protocol for linking farm diversification, markets and nutrition through on-farm agronomic trials and trainings.

description: Traditional systems of yam seed production are slow and inefficient. Leaf-bud cuttings have been tested to determine if they can be used to quickly establish large quantities of yam planting material of improved high-yielding varieties. Techniques for evaluating the performance of leaf bud cuttings (LBCs) were developed and comparisons were made between transplanted and direct planted LBC. Direct planted LBCs gave yields that were more than double those of transplanted LBCs. There were no significant differences in results for the two varieties that were tested. Further research is required to determine the most appropriate situation within the yam seed system in which to use LBCs. Pilot testing of using LBCs in farmers' small seed plots was done during the 2023 cropping season in Bwari, Abuja, Nigeria, and the results was encouraging with farmers excited about the technique.
title: Leaf bud cuttings: a novel method for quicker and more efficient production of yam seeds by farmers in Nigeria and Ghana

description: The Tumaini app is an AI-powered banana disease detection tool that can identify symptoms on any part of the crop, including the leaf, pseudostem, fruit, bunch, or entire plant. The Tumaini app helps agricultural extension workers and banana farmers to correctly identify banana diseases and improve disease surveillance and management. Once a pest or disease location is identified and can be reported using the GPS uploading option and then it can be displayed in the global map database. Once a pest or disease affecting a crop is identified, quick and targeted action can reduce the extent of outbreaks and potentially save entire crops. Tumaini is available in English, Spanish, French, Tamil, and Swahili.

description: These are a series of tools/survey instruments which are designed to characterize seed demand for vegetatively propagated crops (VPCs) in two southern states of Nigeria (Oyo and Cross River). The tools aim to collect information for major target VPCs, including cassava, banana, sweetpotato, potato and yam and to serve as instruments that could potentially be used on a wider scale to assess seed demand characteristics more broadly at country level. The pilot level intruments developed during 2022 were for: 1. Characterizing the VPC seed demand and sales of traders in major markets in the target states; 2. Assessing the production capabilities and institutional characteristics of seed production units in a range of national partners; and 3. Determining the seed needs of product profiled varieties of VPC crops at selected sites in the targeted regions of southern Nigeria.

description: In the integrated rice-cucumber and rice-tomato systems, cucumber or tomato is cultivated during the dry season (March–May), and rice serves as the rotation crop during the wet season (June – October). The residue of cucumber or tomato is incorporated into the soil before rice cultivation. These integrated cropping systems prove to be well-suited for lowlands with water availability either through surface water (river or dam) or shallow wells during the dry season. As compared to existing farming practices where rice is solely cultivated in the wet season, these systems substantially increased farmers' net income by 13,651 to 22,357 USD/ha in an on-farm participatory experiment at two rainfed lowland sites, Mbe and Lokapkli, in the Bouake region of Cote d’Ivoire. This suggests that these systems could be promoted in rainfed lowland systems to increase farmers’ income and provide opportunities for raising household dietary diversity through the consumption of nutritious vegetables.
title: Appropriate and promising diversification options in rice-based systems with vegetable and legume in farmers’ fields in Cote d’Ivoire

description: A willingness to pay (WTP) auction experiment was conducted to measure farmers demand for climate-resilient improved maize varieties in Nigeria. The maize seed auction experiments were conducted with about 1,100 maize farmers across two States of Nigeria. To examine how gender roles in seed purchasing and planting decision may shape demand for improved maize varieties, the WTP experiments were conducted with both male and female farmers. Additional seed and fertilizer bunding and deferred payment treatments were also included to investigate how demand for high-quality seed can be enhanced through a bundle of product/services that agrodealers may use to improve their value proposition to farmers. Results from this study are expected to better inform policymakers about inclusive seed marketing strategies to accelerate varietal turnover and deepen demand for quality seeds in Nigeria.

description:
Experiments were conducted at the station of AfricaRice at Mbe in Cote d’Ivoire to evaluate the agronomic and economic performances of diversification options with mungbean and fish of rice-based systems. The preliminary results show that the total yield of the system in terms of rice plus the yield of non-rice crops converted into equivalent rice yield on a price basis was lower in the system that includes one crop (rice) than in the double cropping system. The results also suggested that the introduction of mungbean in rice-based systems can enhance the efficiency of the system. The efficiency of water use and the economic performance of the systems are being assessed and will be presented in the following report.   _x000D_
A second experiment was established at the Mbe station to evaluate the agronomic and economic performances of the integrated rice-fish systems.

description: Pea seed-borne mosaic virus (PSbMV, genus Potyvirus, family Potyviridae) is the most important virus infecting lentil both in terms of economic importance and geographical distribution. It was reported that PSbMV can even lead up to 61% yield loss. Therefore, developing and implementing effective management strategies for PSbMV is very important to reduce yield and quality loss. However, accurate detection of virus disease is the first essential step for effective management strategies for control of this disease. Molecular is efficient tool to accurately detect and monitor the occurrence and development of crop diseases. This report describes a validated reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay for laboratory detection and characterization of PSbMV applied by ICARDA’s GHU.

description: Wheat plays a crucial role in global food security, sustaining millions of smallholder farmers. Bacterial leaf blight or leaf necrosis disease, caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. syringae (Pss), poses a threat to wheat crops, affecting yield and quality. Accurate disease detection is vital for effective management strategies. A validated molecular tool, a standardized conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay for Pss, has been developed by ICARDA’s Germplasm Health Unit. This innovation enables precise monitoring of leaf necrosis disease occurrence and development. The PCR assay is now available for National Plant Protection Organizations, contributing to enhanced disease control measures. Given wheat's significance, these advancements promise to fortify food security and safeguard the livelihoods of smallholder farmers globally.
