description:
A series of Better Management Practices (BMPs) for smallholder fish farming in pond-based systems has been developed, drawing from field experiences and empirical evidence. These BMPs cover biosecurity, sex-reversed fingerlings for uniform growth, pond construction, species selection, stocking, feeding, harvesting, and marketing._x000D_
To enhance accessibility, the BMPs have been compiled into a manual, translated into local languages, and tailored to smallholders, particularly women. The manual serves as a guide for sustainable fish production, such as tilapia, benefiting aquaculture technicians, NGOs, and private sector stakeholders._x000D_
Adopting BMPs can significantly improve aquaculture in Africa, where smallholder fish farming has high growth potential, contributing to poverty reduction and food security. By supporting small and medium-sized aquaculture enterprises, BMPs help increase fish production, strengthen local economies, and enhance the availability of fish products in the region.
title: Best Management Practices (BMPs) to strengthen the smallholder's aquaculture sector in Zambia and Malawi

description: A refrigeration-equipped truck transports fruits and vegetables in standardized plastic crates. The efficient operation of cool transportation also needs a logistical support system. Cool transportation can preserve the quality of fruits and vegetables when transporting them in distance from production sites, typically in the northern regions, to large demand centers in the southern regions. Post-harvest losses in quality and quantity are reduced to a minimum to benefit producers and consumers, often spatially distanced. Preserving product quality is expected to increase incentives to enhance product quality.

description: Women’s and Men’s Political Participation Trainings are curricula co-designed by ActionAid Nigeria and CGIAR researchers to strengthen women’s sense of collective efficacy and leadership skills, and to increase men’s support for women’s voice and agency. Women's exclusion from civic spaces often leads to policies that inadequately address issues vital to their well-being, such as provision of public services (e.g., healthcare, education, agricultural extension, etc) and infrastructure. Women's political participation remains low for several reasons, including lack of resources, time and information; social norms that discourage women's involvement in politics; and psychological barriers that make women doubtful of their ability to influence change. The women's curriculum is designed to counteract the psychological and social barriers to women's political participation. Meanwhile, the men's curriculum is designed to enhance the support that women receive from their husbands to participate politically by training men on the benefits of women's political participation for their families and communities, as well as how to operationalize this support for women’s benefit.

description: Processed enriched straw is a new processing technique to improve low quality rice straw, which forms 70% of the daily diet of large ruminants in Nepal. In this process the straw is shredded using a shredding machine and fortified with 8% molasses, 1% urea and 1% mineral mixture. It is then compressed and bagged as mash or block. Feed industries procure rice straw from farmers in the harvest season, which will then be processed and sold to dairy keepers through their cooperatives in the lean season when there is acute nutrient stress for dairy animals.

description: A Fall Armyworm (FAW) Innovation Platform was established by CIMMYT in 2022 at Kiboko, Kenya, in partnership with Kenya Agriculture & Livestock Research Organization (KALRO), International Center for Insect Physiology & Ecology (icipe), and Centre for Agriculture and Bioscience International (CABI). FAW management technologies from partner institutions were integrated into 16 different integrated pest management (IPM) packages (including native genetic resistance, biological control, biopesticides, intercropping, push-pull, and synthetic pesticides). All the blocks were artificially infested with egg masses of FAW. A field day was organized on November 8, 2022, where 89 farmers (20 female) and extension personnel from six counties in Kenya individually evaluated the IPM packages and provided their ratings/observations. Another round of evaluation will be done at the harvest stage by the same group on February 8, 2023, and the results will be used for identification and scaling of highly effective IPM packages against FAW.

description: The miniSASS (Stream Assessment Scoring System) was developed as a citizen science tool for monitoring the health of river systems and reflecting the water quality by assessing macroinvertebrates communities. The miniSASS samples the macroinvertebrate community in a river reach and compares the community present to the expected community under ideal natural conditions. The information garnered during a survey relies heavily on the accurate identification of macroinvertebrates by low-skilled citizen scientists. This leaves a potential for errors in identification which may impact the accuracy of results and, ultimately, of the river health assessment. In response, we initiated the development of the new version of miniSASS, the MiniSASS v2, a smartphone application with built-in artificial intelligence and machine-learning algorithms for the automatic, real-time identification of macroinvertebrates.
title: MiniSASS v2: An Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based water quality monitoring system

description:
Improvements in technology, reduction in costs and significant policy support has driven expansion of solar irrigation in Asia and Africa. In India - which is the early leader in solar irrigation adoption, the number of solar pumps is estimated to have grown from a handful in 2010 to more than 350,000 by 2020. The Government of India has announced an ambitious campaign to support the deployment of more than 3.5 million solar pumps over the coming years. Given the significant public and private investments in solar pumps, it is critical that these pumps be 'right-sized' - over-sizing can lead to wasteful expenditure and poor utilization while under-sizing can seriously limit the pumps' benefits. With support from GIZ, IWMI partnered with ICAR and BISA to develop the Beta version of the SIP Sizing Tool for MNRE, Government of India. The tool estimates irrigation and pumping requirement, analyzes future scenarios and recommends the right size for installation of a solar pump. _x000D_
In 2023, IWMI and GIZ expanded their collaboration in promoting this innovation in Nepal. An Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness (IPSR) workshops was conducted in Kathmandu to identify challenges towards solar irrigation in Nepal and co-create solutions for promoting the Decision Support Tool for Right Sizing of Solar-powered Irrigation Pumps. In 2024, the project team has developed a Beta version of an excel based ‘Solar Water Pump Planning Tool for Nepal’.  The tool is officially launched for use by the AEPC and Provincial governments in Nepal. The simple and user-friendly tool will help local government and other stakeholders to quickly estimate the system costs for budget planning. The team will continue its work with further engagement for scaling the tool in India, Nepal and elsewhere.
title: Decision Support Tool for Right Sizing of Solar-powered Irrigation Pumps in Africa and South Asia

description: Groundwater is especially challenging resources to govern, because it is mobile and difficult to observe. Externally imposed rules often fail to work, but examples of community governance of groundwater are also scarce. This toolbox offers examples of innovative procedures, policy instruments, and institutional tools. Stakeholders engaged in enhancing groundwater governance can utilize these examples to comprehend their issues and opportunities. Additionally, they can deliberate on and potentially reach consensus on norms or rules aimed at preventing aquifer depletion. Furthermore, the toolbox facilitates the creation of shared gains that enhance water productivity. Institutional tools for groundwater governance could help deal with complex nexus linkages such as transitions to solar-powered pumping, aquifer recharge and storage to buffer against drought, and regenerating ecosystems. This groundwater governance toolbox offers government agencies and communities resources for thinking about the variety of instruments available and how they might be chosen, combined, and adapted to create customized toolkits to solve problems and achieve gains in specific contexts.
title: Groundwater governance toolbox: Guidance on how to identify, adapt, and combine tools to improve groundwater governance in a participatory and locally-appropriate manner for government agencies and communities

description: Water productivity constitutes one of the key ways to expand Water Energy Food Ecosystems (WEFE) benefits in water scarce contexts, yet water productivity is variable and in cases low. This innovation is focused on development of a Decision Support System (DSS) that enables planners and managers to identify solutions (e.g., resources allocations or crop mixes) that improve productivity. The DSS is a computer-based platform reveals the productivity associated with alternative investment choices, which can support investment decisions that optimize water productivity and WEFE benefits in different geographies. Key users of the DSS platform are water planners and managers, as well as those in related sectors (i.e. Energy, Food and Ecosystems).
title: Water Productivity Atlas that enables planners and managers to identify solutions to improve water productivity

The Smart Nkunganire System (SNS) was created in response to the Rwandan Ministry of Agriculture's (MINAGRI) request for enhanced digital extension services and precise, site-specific fertilizer recommendations for essential crops. The project aims to develop a digital advisory tool integrated within the existing SNS platform, managed by BKTechouse. This tool is designed to provide customized fertilizer recommendations for six priority crops in Rwanda: cassava, maize, wheat, potato, rice, and beans, making these recommendations accessible to both extension agents and farmers through the SNS platform._x000D_
_x000D_
This initiative is further supported by making these tools and methodologies available to the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), aiming to enhance the innovation's development. This strategic approach ensures that the digital advisory tool effectively meets the specific needs of Rwanda's agriculture sector, providing tailored support to improve productivity and sustainability.

description: Since 2022, ABI-Transform has organized an annual leadership consultations between Genetic Innovation and NARES in Sub-Saharan Africa to assess partnership health and identify priority areas to further improve collaboration. Key decisions and outputs from these meetings have been captured in Aide Memoires which have been endorsed by leaders from CGIAR, NARES and SROs. Resolutions and actions are tracked and pursued by the Core Technical Team that meets quarterly and is composed of representatives from the CGIAR, NARES and SROs. These meetings have highlighted 8 key areas: 1. need for co-creation and increased alignment with national and regional priorities; 2. Increased role for partners in regional breeding networks; 3. Better attribution; 4. Increased funding transparency; 5. Joint ownership and decision making; 6. Need for an annual partnership health check through a representative survey; 7. Need to incorporate Universities and SMEs in regional breeding networks; 8. Need to institutionalize human capacity development.
title: High level engagement for co-creation of collaborative breeding networks: building more equitable partnerships that more effectively address regional priorities, and collectively increase genetic gain and farmer variety adoption

description: Gender inclusive activities to promote newly released climate smart legume varieties (less than 10 years), use of quality legume seed and integrated crop management technologies in SeedEqual countries were organized. To build synergies and utilize existing networks, events were organized in collaboration with public and private sector (private seed companies, NGOs, CBOs, Schools, agro dealers, Extension agents, traders) actors, with national partners taking the lead. These events included: demonstrations, participatory variety selection, exhibitions, Barraza’s, sensitizations, trainings, and field days. The ultimate goal was to accelerate adoption of new varieties to lower the Area Weighted Age of the Variety (AWAVA). Some of the varieties promoted are high in iron and zinc to ensure supply of these important nutrients in nutritionally vulnerable communities especially targeting women and girls. All promotional events were organized to ensure inclusivity and that women, men, boys and girls participated.
title: Collaborative Promotional Events to Promote Improved Varieties, Use of Quality Legume Seed and Integrated Crop Management Technologies in Eastern, Southern and Western Africa

description: This report pertains to Work Package Five of TAFSSA. In the reported period, the Cereal Systems Initiative in South Asia (CSISA), in conjunction with Transforming Agrifood Systems in South Asia (TAFSSA) and the Asian Mega Deltas Iniative, enhanced an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system for mung bean farmers in Bangladesh's coastal regions, focusing on Patuakhali and Barguna districts. Building on previous efforts, M-World (a private company) has been selected to manage the IVR system sustainably from 2024. The CSISA team is supporting M-World in mastering the mung bean IVR system and executing IVR calls. A total of 328,752 IVR calls were made to 10,472 mung bean farmers, including 668 women and 9,804 men, 72 Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) officers, and three mung bean millers across 17 selected locations in coastal Bangladesh during the harvest period from March 29 to June 06, 2023.
title: Mung bean farmers benefit at scale from interactive voice response (IVR) calls on rainfall forecasts during the 2023 mung bean harvesting period.

description: The CGIAR Research Initiative on Livestock and Climate is supporting pastoral communities in Tanzania to secure their land rights and strengthen governance and management of rangeland resources. This is achieved by supporting policy-serving innovations, engaging in joint village land use planning (JVLUP) and facilitating participatory rangeland management (PRM). These efforts have resulted in a notable enhancement of pastoralists’ land tenure security and encouraging investments that enhance land productivity and where degraded, facilitating restoration in the four rangeland units being supported. In  2023, in response to the community's rangeland management plan, the community from the ALOLLE shared grazing land requested assistance to clear thorny bush from 112 hectares of land, that would then allow for grasses to regrow. ILRI and local NGO partner KINNAPA provided technical and minimal financial assistance to the community to undertake the clearance in October, with a larger area to be cleared in 2024.
title: Tanzanian pastoralist communities commence restoration of degraded rangelands through participatory rangeland management (PRM) and joint village land use planning (JVLUP)

description: The International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) and its partners have launched a forage breeding program in 1987, focused on the development of interspecific Urochloa (syn. Brachiaria) hybrids. The first hybrid was released in 2001 by Grupo Papalotla, a seed company from Mexico, and since then, hybrid adoption has happened in >70 countries. The impacts this adoption has generated over time are, however, yet largely unknown. Based on seed sales data, global databases, national statistics, grey literature, media, and expert consultations, we analyzed these impacts regarding 3 dimensions: land use, social, and economic impacts.
title: Global use of CIAT's Urochloa hybrids in cattle farming for enhancing productivity and sustainability and for improving cattle farmer livelihoods between 2001 and 2021

description: Epidemiological models are crucial in monitoring risk zones and disease outbreaks and contribute to prevention and management strategies. Plant-pathogen interactions and disease dynamics could be reproduced through mathematical models based on data on environmental factors related to disease triangles. This study standardizes a rice disease epidemiological model, EPIRICE, for predicting rice blast and rice brown spot disease occurrence risk in sub-Saharan Africa. Randomized complete block design experiments were conducted in five locations in Cote d'Ivoire, and three in Uganda in 2023, and data collected on various parameters were inputted into the model. Temperature affected the latent, incubation, and infectious periods of both diseases. The severity of diseases was significantly correlated with average and minimum relative humidity values in the shortest window length. However, the severity of both diseases was inversely correlated with wind speed. Further work will focus on fine-tuning the model by harnessing data from various rice fields.
title: An improved EPIRICE model that predicts the impact of weather factors on rice blast and rice brown spot dynamics in rice growing areas

description: Risks and occurrence prediction model frameworks of Africa armyworm developed. A system dynamics model was developed by following a structured approach that includes building causal loop diagrams and stocks and flows diagrams. The process started by thoroughly researching and understanding the system i.e. the ecology and biology of the African Armyworm, its life cycle, and the factors that influence its occurrence and population dynamics, such as temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation. The methodology combining data reconstruction techniques with rule-based systems and zero-shot learning was used to predict African armyworm infestation severity of yield losses. The model's proficiency in predicting crop loss was substantiated by an accuracy rate of 0.80, as revealed by the confusion matrix. The production of month yield losses induced by African armyworm as the real outputs of the model is still ongoing.
title: African armyworm model frameworks for predicting this pest risks and occurrence developed

description: The TUMAINI Banana Disease Surveillance Dashboard has emerged as a transformative tool, achieving seamless spatial integration across the global banana landscape. This platform bridges the Already developed Tumaini app and a recently developed online dashboard, enabling precise mapping of banana plant locations and extents. It plays a crucial role in outlining production areas and offers broad applications as a versatile resource. The resounding success of the Alliance's collaboration has paved the way for the inception of the next-generation map. So far, over 50,000 GPS points have been detailed, tracking five diseases (Fusarium wilt, Xanthomonas wilt, Banana bunchy top virus, Moko, and Leaf spot) in more than 15 countries in the global south. The database, consisting of around 50,000 mapped plants, was compiled from regional surveys, cellphone image metadata, and predominantly drone image data, which constitutes about 70% of the total database.
title: TUMAINI Banana Disease Surveillance Dashboard : a new innovation for Musaceae protection

description: This innovation encompasses the strategic integration of genomics-supported recurrent selection (GS-RSS) into cassava breeding programs within CGIAR-NARS networks. It aims to expedite the breeding cycle  (traditionally 5 to 7 years due to cassava's 12 month growth period), by incorporating genomic selection methodologies. These methods will leverage the increasingly accessible and affordable genome-wide DNA markers to predict breeding values, enabling the identification and selection of superior genotypes at early testing stages. The innovation is designed to not only enhance the efficiency and accuracy of selection for desirable traits but also to ensure that the genetic gains translate into tangible benefits in farmers' fields. By focusing on traits that address social and gender inequalities such as root quality in addition to yield, the initiative seeks to deliver varieties that are not just high-yielding but also meet the specific needs and preferences of diverse groups, thereby fostering inclusivity and equity in agricultural advancements.
title: Mainstreaming the Implementation of Genomics-Supported Recurrent Selection Schemes for Enhanced Cassava Breeding and Genetic Gain in CGIAR-NARS Networks to Empower Small-Holder Farmers

description: Knowledge of genetic variation and the exact identity of viruses affecting legume crops is essential for breeding for resistance and effective crop management.  Based on the serological results, representative chickpea and faba bean isolates of Chickpea chlorotic stunt virus (CpCSV) and Beet western yellows virus (BWYV) were selected for further molecular analysis with RT-PCR and sequencing of the partial coat protein gene. Molecular analyses recognized that Turnip yellows virus (TuYV) and Brassica yellows virus (BrYV) are newly identified viruses closely related to, but significantly different from BWYV. Phylogenetic analysis showed that Tunisian isolates of BWYV are clustered with similar isolates from Cyprus and Türkiye, where CpCSV Tunisian isolates are clustered with reference accessions under Serogroup-II. description: After launching an e-course on Food Systems Governance in 2022, key government partners of Sustainable Healthy Diets identified a need for follow-up trainings held face-to-face. A team from this Initiative and representatives from several government ministries agreed that the best way forward would be to jointly develop a new Training of Trainers (ToT) program on food systems. The ToT program will increase the pool of in-country experts that can facilitate learning processes on using food systems approaches. At the same time, the ToT program will complement the national policy processes for food systems transformation, like the Food Systems Transformation National Action Plan (FST-NAP) in Viet Nam and the National Food Systems Roadmap in Ethiopia, by filling identified gaps in awareness of how sustainable healthy diets can be achieved through food systems transformation and how to apply food systems approaches in these specific, and more general, policy processes.

description: Various fish-based products have been introduced in communities in several countries in Africa and Asia by WorldFish and partners. In particular, dried fish powder that utilizes nutrient-dense small fish can contribute to making healthy, affordable, and sustainable diets more accessible for vulnerable communities in low- and middle-income countries. In Zambia, nutrient-enhanced complementary foods for Africa and dried fish powder (ComFA+Fish) products and recipes for enhanced nutrition, particularly for mothers and infants in vulnerable households, have been developed and tested with mothers, caregivers, small-scale fishers, fish processors, fish traders, the private sector, and government representatives. These include fortified Zambian dishes such as chibwaba fisashi and kapenta chutney, fortified maize porridge, fortified bean-vegetable soup, fortified cassava bites, and fortified nutri-biscuits. The ComFA+Fish products have been widely accepted in the communities around Lake Kariba in Zambia and were recommended for scaling in communities where malnutrition is high.

description: In 2022, IWMI partnered with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Borlaug Institute for South Asia (BISA) to jointly develop the solar irrigation pump (SIP) sizing tool for India. The tool, developed with support from GIZ, was designed specifically for the Government of India, for use in the ambitious agri-solarization initiative PM-KUSUM ("Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan'). The Excel-based beta version of the tool and the user manual are available online. The tool has since been adopted by PM-KUSUM and web and mobile versions of the tool are being developed. IWMI and ICAR have committed to promote large-scale use and deployment of the tool and support future versions. As part of NEXUS Gains, the SIP sizing tool has been identified as one of the innovations to be scaled, including by extending its use beyond India. In 2023-2024, IWMI in partnership with GIZ Nepal and the Alternative Energy Promotion Center (AEPC) have developed a "Solar Pump Sizing Tool" for Nepal and launched in a Global Science-Policy Forum held in Kathmandu on 25th April 2024. The tool is developed for the use AEPC who will provide guidance to provincial government using a tool. AEPC will publish the tool along with user manual on their website.

description: Mbili Mbili intercropping system has been promoted as a crop diversification and intensification approach. Mbili-Mbili (two maize rows alternating with two legume species) exploits plant spatial configurations to increase light penetration to the legumes, otherwise often shaded by cereals. The aim is to increase legume productivity while maintaining the same productivity of the cereal and taking advantage and complementarity of the different growth habits and durations of the combined crops. It enables farmers to grow both legumes and cereals on the same land and thus harvest at different times. In the event of a loss, one crop serves as insurance. This makes the system climate-smart. Mbili Mbili system has been reported to have a higher return (up to 37% more) compared to the standard farmer intercropping practices. The technology has been promoted in maize-growing areas in east and southern Africa, and was formally released in Malawi as agronomic innovation.

description: Pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera) is still significant challenge in pulse cultivation in India. We aimed to develop regression model using weather indices for forecasting pod borer outbreaks in pigeonpea and chickpea. The historical adult trap catch data; eggs and larval data, and actual weather data of ICRISAT location from 1991 to 2023 was used.  Models predict crop stage at the first appearance of the pest (Y1), and maximum population of the pest at peak infestation time (Y2). Results showed that temperature, relative humidity, rainfall, and sunshine hours significantly influenced the population dynamics of pod borer. For pigeonpea, model accurately predicted maximum eggs population at 43rd SMW and maximum larval population at the 45th SMW. In chickpea, model predicted the maximum eggs population at 45th SMW and the maximum larval population at 46th SMW. The model's effectiveness validated in current season for pigeonpea at major growing regions of Karnataka and Telangana.

description: The ISAT platform, a collaborative effort between ICRISAT, CGIAR, Microsoft, and the India Meteorological Department, with support from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), has been at the forefront of providing farmers with vital information that can significantly enhance their decision-making processes. More than 6,000 farmers in Odisha, India, use the ISAT Climate Information Services to enhance productivity and manage climate risks. In a continued effort to empower farmers with timely and accurate farming advisories, a team from the ICRISAT recently conducted a field visit to Rayagada and Gajapati districts. The need for village-level training emerged as a top priority for maximizing the benefits of climate information services.

description: Inclusive business models are essential for ensuring small-scale fish farmers have access to quality feeds, seeds, extension services, and training. Partnering with the private sector, an accelerator grant program was co-designed to reduce risks and scale climate-smart aquaculture (CSA) innovations. Six small and medium enterprises (SMEs) received these grants to expand CSA adoption among smallholder farmers. Each SME operates within the aquaculture value chain, integrating CSA practices and Climate Information System (CIS) extension services. This approach has accelerated the uptake of innovative solutions, benefiting 45,154 farmers (36% women) who now have access to millions of high-quality fingerlings and premium-priced fish markets. Farmers have adopted modern fishpond designs resilient to flooding and drought and receive timely weather updates from the Zambia Meteorological Department via WhatsApp and radio, enabling better planning of farming activities. This approach demonstrates the impact of public-private collaboration in scaling sustainable aquaculture practices for smallholder farmers.

The innovation produces mutual benefits to both fisheries and irrigation systems through allowing fish migration, the creation of new aquatic habitats for fish species in irrigated lands and the enhancement of inland fisheries productivity through integrated systems, such as irrigated rice-fish farming systems. New generation of fish friendly irrigation innovations (sluice gates, irrigation canals, dams) to strengthen the resilience and sustainability and livelihoods of fisheries-dependent communities in Asia and Africa

description: The CGIAR Greenpass Phytosanitary Protocol (CGPP) represents the systems approach to managing the phytosanitary health of CGIAR genetic resources by the Germplasm Health Units (GHUs). In 2024, an expert consultation on enhancing phytosanitary procedures for germplasm exchange in Africa was organized. The workshop brought together Heads of Quarantine Agencies from nine African nations (Benin, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda, and Zimbabwe), representatives from the Food and Agriculture Organization Regional Office for Africa, CABI, and the African Union Inter-African Phytosanitary Council (AU-IAPSC). The discussions converged on the pressing need for a harmonized framework to facilitate safe germplasm exchange in Africa. Expert recommendations included identifying priority crops for harmonization, capacity building for officials in plant quarantine agencies, raising awareness about CGPP, and establishing a protocol for accrediting germplasm health facilities as per the ISPM-45. The workshop underscored the critical importance of regional collaboration in improving germplasm exchange systems.

description:
WorldFish has developed a digital survey approach to characterize aquaculture production systems, assess performance, and benchmark sustainability metrics across diverse geographies, economic settings, and agro-climatic conditions. Understanding how these systems function, how they are affected by diseases, management practices, and environmental factors, and how farmers make production choices requires large-scale, context-specific data collection. Tested in Bangladesh, Egypt, Kenya, Myanmar, Nigeria, and India, this approach integrates on-farm performance assessment with digital tools to generate big data on aquaculture. It supports researchers, universities, extension specialists, government agencies, and NGOs in evaluating sustainability and guiding policy and investment decisions._x000D_
The approach has been scaled into different modules and applied in bilateral investments in Myanmar, Kenya, and other countries to support baseline assessments for benchmarking aquaculture system performance. By providing a standardized yet adaptable framework, it enhances data-driven decision-making for sustainable aquaculture growth.

description:
The Community-Based Resource Management (CBRM) Training Package for coastal fisheries in the Solomon Islands was developed to provide technical support and inclusive planning for communities managing their coastal resources. Over four years, a CBRM program was implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Fisheries and Marine Resources (MFMR), Malaita Provincial Government, and WorldFish._x000D_
The program engaged 96 communities, raising awareness about CBRM and assessing existing practices. Until now, 32 communities had developed eight management plans, and 72 community facilitators from 51 communities were trained using a CBRM monitoring and evaluation tool. Recognizing the importance of customary land tenure, the Solomon Islands Government has designated CBRM as the primary coastal resource management strategy. This training package strengthens the role of Provincial Fisheries Officers (PFOs), equipping them with the knowledge and capacity to support community-led fisheries management, ensuring sustainable resource use and guiding future CBRM scaling across other provinces.

description: The Aquatic Food Ontology (AQFO) is an innovation currently used to enable efficient aggregation and analysis of aquatic food data generated by the CGIAR Initiative on Aquatic Foods and WorldFish. By structuring the meaning and relationships between terms, AQFO provides a common language for data interoperability, facilitating harmonization across datasets. The standardization of aquatic food data labels using controlled vocabularies ensures greater consistency, easier data integration, and improved analytical capabilities. AQFO is hosted on AgroPortal and is built upon FAO Agrovoc terminology and terms derived from WorldFish innovations. As the ontology continues to evolve, its application will further support seamless data sharing and interpretation across research, policy, and decision-making processes, enhancing the impact and scalability of aquatic food system innovations.

description:
Peskas, a digital catch documentation and fisheries monitoring system, combines tamper-proof, solar-powered trackers developed by Pelagic Data Systems with an open-source decision dashboard to provide real-time data on small-scale fisheries production and effort. Since its adoption as Timor-Leste’s national fisheries monitoring system in 2019, Peskas has received continuous investment from the Government of Timor-Leste (GOTL), with a second installment in 2021. By 2020, the system covered 15,690 km² of coastline in Timor-Leste, enabling evidence-based fisheries management._x000D_
By 2024, Peskas has expanded through bilateral investments and is now implemented in six countries: Timor-Leste, Malaysia, Malawi, Tanzania, Mozambique, and Kenya. The publicly available dashboard has gained global recognition, receiving >4,800 visits from 2,400 unique visitors across 65 countries in 2024. This scaling demonstrates the increasing international adoption of digital tools for sustainable and transparent fisheries governance.

description: Participatory Rangeland Management (PRM) is a defined step-by-step process for improving local level rangeland management by local pastoralist communities. It follows three stages of investigation (including participatory mapping), negotiation and implementation. It supports establishment and/or strengthening of rangelands management institutions, and supports the production of a rangeland management plan and an agreement with local government to improve access of communities to natural resources and land. M&E and capacity building are also important steps.

description: In collaboration with the FAO-ICARDA cactus network and NARS partners to promote and scale up cactus pear as a crop well-adapted to agricultural farming in the dry areas, that can be utilized by millions of poor farmers for important nutritional and income-creating purposes. Being a versatile crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM) with an extraordinary water use efficiency makes it a viable resilient important agricultural resource that enable farmers getting valuable products, including fruits for human consumption and fodder for livestock while helping to reduce the need for watering livestock due to its high-water content. This collaboration led to a substantial increase in demand for planting materials, resulting in providing improved planting materials, that can serve different agro-ecological zones. ICARDA alongside its NARS partners, has also carried out extensive awareness campaigns and capacity development activities to train farmers on promoting cactus pear as a multi-functional crop.

It combines an innovation systems perspective for impact and a rigorous evidence synthesis method, using metrics developed initially by NASA and further developed by the European Commission. It links current agricultural and food innovation systems with potential impact at scale and sheds light on which innovations, investments and partnerships should be prioritized by projects or organizations to achieve impact.

description:
Animal systems often receive less attention or are treated separately from crops in national agricultural strategies and investment plans. To address this, the Foresight Initiative developed a standardized Herd Dynamics Model (HDM) to analyze trends and investments in animal systems. Supported by a global livestock database with reconciled historical data and demographic parameters, the HDM enables integrated analysis of crop and animal system priorities when embedded in agrifood system models. Piloted in an Ethiopia case study, and in early second-phase testing in Rwanda, Tanzania and Nigeria, this system reduces the cost of modeling animal systems in national planning._x000D_
_x000D_
Building on this foundation, the Linked Economic and Animal Systems (LEAS) model now includes sheep and goats alongside cattle. Work on crop-livestock interactions in semi-subsistence economies was presented at ICAE 2024. The model has expanded to Rwanda to analyze livestock interventions, with IFPRI collaborating with ILRI to advance and align livestock modeling efforts.
title: The Herd Dynamics Model (HDM) component of the Linked Economic and Animal Systems (LEAS) model, a tool for or policy analysis on livestock management in Ethiopia

description:
Engaging with communities to employ more pragmatic land-use planning and scheduling of sluice gate operations has shown the potential to intensify and diversify cropping systems, and increasing production by 2-3 fold. This was achieved using improved rice varieties and non-rice crops, enabled by strategic management of the sluice gates to drain the lands as needed during the wet season and to facilitate timely establishment of non-rice crops after rice harvest. _x000D_
_x000D_
The sluice gate operation is being introduced and tested in multiple sites to facilitate adoption of improved cropping system (year-round), and terminal drainage to facilitate mechanized paddy harvest and early establishment of rabi crops in the coastal polder zone. Several trainings are also being provided to ensure synchronized operation of sluice gates of intended users such as water management groups and rice farmers for improved productivity and intensified production systems in the polders.

description:
The climate-smart risk maps and adaptation plans (CS-MAP) is a participatory approach involving experts from various local and national offices for (1) identifying climate-related risks; (2) delineating affected areas and risk levels; (3) proposing corresponding adaptive plans; (4) fine-tuning and verifying propose measures; and (5) developing integrated provincial and regional adaptation plans. Risk maps were developed for normal and El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) years by using technical data, infrastructures, and local observations. _x000D_
_x000D_
The CS Maps are designed to be used by policymakers and planners from regional and local offices to inform annual crop planning at province and district levels for scaling of adaptation solutions in rice production. The CS-MAP approach has been expanded to Cambodia and Bangladesh with numerous consultations, evaluations and validation with local stakeholders and farmers to develop and scale the CS-MAP approach for local planning.

It's implementation has expanded to Cambodia to establish experimental sites and engagement activities with local stakeholders were conducted.

description: WorldFish G3 Rohu was officially handed over to the Bangladesh Fisheries Research Institute at a workshop held on 8 August 2023 in Bangladesh Fisheries Research Institute, Mymensingh. In June-August 2023, 24 private hatcheries (11 of which did not previously maintain G3 rohu), 12 Department of Fisheries hatcheries, one Bangladesh Fisheries Research Institute (BFRI) hatchery and one educational institution hatchery were supplied with G3 multiplier broodstock spawned in 2023.  In addition, the BFRI hatchery was provided with 52 mature G3 multiplier fish from the 2020 spawning.  At the conclusion of 2023, 38 geographically-disparate private, 18 DoF, one BFRI and two educational institution hatcheries were known to maintain G3 rohu broodstock.

description: Within the framework of the AgriLAC initiative, biofortified rice seed was delivered to a community of small rice producers located in Letica, Cartagena, Colombia. The delivery was made through the partner in the area, which is the Canal del Dique Foundation. The biofortified rice seed Fedearroz BioZN-035 accumulates 44% more zinc under technical irrigation conditions and 63% more, under favored dryland and mechanized dryland conditions, compared to with non-biofortified rice that contains an average of 1.6 mg/100g, for this reason it contributes to the food security of the population that consumes it.

description:
WorldFish collaborates with M-World to promote an app-based innovative transportation system for the hatcheries, nurseries, and grow out farms, to enable the efficient and cost-effective carriage of fish whilst complying with all the required quality and compliance standards. The app based digital ride sharing mechanism for transporting fish from one place to another. It followed the Uber model and this is the first ever model in fish transportation in Bangladesh. To familiarize the “Maach Gari” app, MWorld conducted 60 promotional events with 1,381 participants (1,343 farmers and 348 vehicle owners). MWorld also conducted 5 market activation events with 120 fish traders in Jashore. _x000D_
As a result, 1,723 fish farmers and 25 nursery owners transported their fish using the app and its associated call center. The App generated 302 trips and delivered 172 metric tons fish worth USD 225,240 to desired destinations and markets by the registered transport service providers.
title: ‘Macher Gari’ an innovative way to increase availability and accessibility of aquaculture inputs to farmers in Bangladesh

description: The G+ approach for gender-responsive breeding, developed by CGIAR scientists since 2018, offers an integrated, systematic, and evidence-based protocol for breeding new crop varieties. The approach builds on work by the CGIAR Excellence in Breeding (EiB) Platform on the concept of a “product profile”, which describes the traits that different actors want in a new variety, giving plant breeders a target. The G+ approach complements this with two additional tools. The G+ plus customer profile characterizes client groups targeted for new varieties, considering gender differences in knowledge, assets, and decision-making which influence adoption. This makes it easier for breeders to develop the right product for the right customers.

description: The Healthy Eating Index (HEI) measures dietary quality in accordance with Vietnam's nationally-recognized food-based dietary guidelines (FBDGs). A robust HEI has the potential to reveal and monitor how well the general adult population (20 years and older) is adhering to specific, culturally appropriate and actionable recommendations for a healthy diet. The Vietnamese HEI was developed by the National Institute of Nutrition with researchers from Wageningen University and Research (WUR) involved in Sustainable Healthy Diets. Results from a CGIAR-supported doctoral dissertation applying the HEI to a nationally representative household survey dataset suggested it was effective at measuring adherence to the Vietnamese FBDGs. This innovation can a valuable tool for future research to examine associations between dietary quality and health-related outcomes and relationships between dietary quality and the environmental impacts of diets and for program implementers in government and NGOs to monitor interventions focusing on improving dietary quality.

description: This innovation aims to develop suitability maps that show the potential for rice-fish implementation across the Ayeyarwady Delta. Previous iterations of the rice-fish suitability maps showed the potential for the transformation of 15,700 km2 across the Ayeyarwady, supporting improved food security, nutritional security, incomes, and employment for the local population. The Decision Support System (DSS) includes key socio-economic variables that significantly influence suitability and consider the impact key climatic variables (e.g., temperature change and an increased frequency and severity of storm events) may have on the future viability of rice-fish. The DSS is being upscaled through a training of the trainer (ToT) approach with the Department of Agriculture (DoA), Department of Planning (DoP), and Department of Fisheries (DoF) under the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Irrigation (MOALI).

description: To facilitate further and more efficient diversification of elite backgrounds, a new strategy for augmentation has been developed.  This turns the linear process of upgrading a particular line with up to 3 new genes into a cyclical recurrent selection process, intercrossing amongst elite progeny to accumulate target genes.  The benefits of this scheme are decoupling the number of input and output lines, and a greatly increased capacity to select for a much larger number of genes with modest/tractable population sizes.  Initial founding lines and crosses are underway to establish this pipeline, initially for the medium maturity program and from there to direct-seeded material as resources permit. The scheme prioritized traits for disease resistance, abiotic stress resistance (e.g. drought) and improving grain quality. These traits aimed to produced breeding lines that would help combat impacts of climate change and increasing consumption of healthier rice without penalizing yield.

description: On-farm Genomic Selection (GS) using a Sparse Testing design has been implemented  in rainfed upland rice breeding pipeline covering six countries in Africa. A total of 898 (896 tests and 2 checks) upland breeding lines evaluated in six diverse target population environments (TPE) in Côte d’Ivoire, Mali, Nigeria, DRC, Guinea Conakry, and Sierra Leone using a P-Rep design. Thirty percent of the test lines (282 genotypes) were tested twice and distributed across farms and remaining 616 test lines were identically distributed into six countries . Two checks: 1 regional check (NERICA 4) and 1 local check were used, and each check was replicated twice within a country. The trial is being conducted using a modified  tricot design. Five sites/location have been  chosen, and 10 farmers are involved  on each site/village.

description:
Microsite (Krishi Kund) offers a resource-efficient alternative for restoring degraded lands by concentrating natural amendments within specific areas for improving agricultural diversity, soil health, and overall ecosystem services. It also helps alleviate the pressure of intensive farming on other lands. Moreover, this practice holds promise for reversing migration among tribal communities._x000D_
This practice focuses on improving micro-sites rather than entire parcels of land using organic amendments. In this method, small cylindrical pits (did: 60cm, depth 60cm) are excavated at 1.2m intervals, filled with locally available organic materials. This approach improves approximately 20% (6450 pits per hectare) of the land area, resulting in a similar yield of fully restored land._x000D_
Drought tolerant crops viz pigeon pea, caster for the poor water availability sites and other cash crops including vegetables at sites of water availability are being grown. A two-year recovery period was estimated for the cost incurred on land restoration.

description: Farming with Alternative Pollinators (FAP) is a proven ecological intensification approach that integrates marketable habitat enhancement plants (MHEP) – such as oil seeds, spices, food crops and medicinal plants - within fields. These plants provide diverse floral traits (e.g., shape, colour, flower type) and nesting support to support a high diversity and abundance of pollinators and natural enemies (e.g., Hymenoptera, Hemiptera, Aranaea). Farmers using FAP report higher fruit yields, improved quality, and increased income compared to monoculture fields. Developed as a scalable alternative to (paid) wildflower strips, FAP offers an affordable solution for low- and middle-income countries.

description: The International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI) has been implementing an open-source digital crowdsourcing tool known as KAZNET (which stands for "Kazi kwa net" translated in Swahili to mean "working within a network") to alleviate data collection constraints and monitor resilience indicators in the drylands of Kenya and Ethiopia. KAZNET includes a dissemination component, where information gathered through the platform is processed in real time and channeled back to communities, development practitioners, and governments. The KAZNET app has a dashboard through which different types of information can be visualized. The graphic presentation of the information allows for the visualization of trends while also eliminating the need for more than basic literacy to understand the information presented. The disseminated information contains indicators of markets and rangelands performance. In addition, KAZNET disseminates information about the types of food consumed by households, livestock mortality, and the strategies used for coping with drought.

description:
With fish consumption rising globally but per capita supply declining in sub-Saharan Africa, Nigeria’s reliance on single-species aquaculture limits sector growth. To address this, a decentralized GIFT (Genetically Improved Farmed Tilapia) seed supply system is being established to increase access, improve growth performance, and support species diversification. Following the successful transfer of GIFT to Premium Aquaculture Limited (PAL) in Ogun State, a breeding population was established, demonstrating a 20% higher growth rate over 60 days compared to older strains. Best management practices (BMPs) were developed, and training programs expanded to farmers. Satellite hatcheries were set up in Delta State and expanded to two more states, increasing farmer access._x000D_
This innovative scaling model fin Nigeria not only improves the availability of high-performance tilapia seed, but also creates opportunities for expanding other species value chains, fostering a more diversified and sustainable aquaculture industry in Nigeria and beyond.

description:
Aquaculture plays a vital role in food security and local economies, yet selecting sustainable and viable sites remains a challenge, particularly in developing countries. Traditional methods rely on limited ground data, often leading to inefficient resource use, environmental degradation, and logistical constraints. Without satellite-based insights, decision-making is often based on outdated or incomplete information, making it difficult to meet sustainability goals. _x000D_
Optimising AQUAculture Development and Market Connectivity (AQUADMC) leverages remote sensing technologies and geospatial datasets to provide a comprehensive decision-making platform for aquaculture site selection. By integrating environmental, socio-economic, and logistical factors, AQUADMC delivers actionable insights for policymakers, investors, and local authorities. This approach ensures ecologically responsible and economically viable aquaculture expansion, while addressing emerging challenges such as climate change and market growth. As the platform evolves, it offers a transformative solution for improving sustainable aquaculture development, guiding decision-making with data-driven precision.

description: Epidemiological models are essential for monitoring pest and disease outbreaks, aiding prevention and management. This study standardizes EPIRICE, a rice disease model predicting rice blast, a major threat in sub-Saharan Africa. Experiments using a randomized complete block design were conducted across five locations in Côte d'Ivoire and three in Uganda (2023/2024). Predictor variables were analyzed to assess infection risk. Data collection was disrupted in two locations due to brown spot infection. In Côte d’Ivoire, epidemics began between May and July annually. EPIRICE accurately predicted blast onset, with p-values above 5%, confirming reliability. Predicted versus observed field data showed strong similarities. Temperature (20-25°C) had the strongest correlation with blast risk, while wind speed had minimal impact. Ongoing analysis will determine optimal decision thresholds based on 2024 harvest data from Côte d’Ivoire and Uganda. These findings will enhance disease forecasting, supporting effective rice blast management in the region.

description: Maize Seed Field and MLN Tracker: A Check, Detect, and Reporting WebApp for maize clean seed production and prevention of maize lethal necrosis (MLN) spread. The App, known as Maize Clean Seed Production Tracker, is an Android-based Open Data Kit (ODK) software enabled through a web-based toolbox to support data management and decisions for conducting MLN surveillance in a time series and to implement Standard Operating Procedures for MLN pathogen-free commercial seed production. From the phytosanitary perspective, it is critical to follow rigorous procedures to produce and exchange MLN pathogen-free commercial maize seed within and between countries to prevent the spread and negative impact of the disease on maize production. The tool was developed and piloted for validation in Kenya. The tool helps monitor proactive MLN risk mitigation in real time. Together with the MLN surveillance data portal, it guides the establishment of seed fields in low or no-disease-pressure sites.

description: A temperature-based early warning alert system for fish farmers in Zambia has been developed. The advisory tool utilizes an air-water temperature relationship algorithm to forecast pond water temperatures, which is integrated with the data hub of the Intelligent Agricultural Systems Advisory Tool (iSAT) and an early temperature warning decision tree matrix. It also features a dashboard that uses input data and water quality parameter thresholds for critical scenarios affecting tilapia and catfish (Clarias gariepinus). When predicted temperatures approach these thresholds, a color-coded alarm is activated, triggering a specific action protocol to regulate pond temperatures. The goal is to mitigate the impact of high-risk (24°C minimum and 32°C maximum) and emergency (12°C minimum and 40°C maximum) temperature scenarios on cultured stock.

description: The drought monitoring tool for the Limpopo River Basin integrates Earth Observation (EO) datasets, meteorological indices, and hydrological modeling to track drought conditions in near real-time. Developed under the IWMI Digital Twin platform, it leverages climate data, precipitation records, and vegetation health indicators such as the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) to assess drought severity and trends. The system incorporates satellite-derived rainfall anomalies, evapotranspiration assessments, and water balance calculations, helping policymakers and researchers understand the impact of drought on water resources, agriculture, and food security. The tool identifies regions most affected by dry conditions, enabling proactive decision-making for drought mitigation and adaptation strategies. By visualizing changes in water availability and vegetation health, it supports long-term planning for irrigation, water allocation, and climate resilience efforts. This comprehensive approach enhances early warning capabilities, helping governments and stakeholders implement timely interventions to minimize the socio-economic impact of droughts.

description: The innovation titled "Multicriteria-Based Priority Mapping: Charting Agroecological Pathways in India" addresses the dual challenge of food security and environmental sustainability. Using a multi-criteria decision-making framework, it integrates diverse datasets such as net primary productivity, fertilizer consumption, rainfall patterns, groundwater levels, the aridity index, and others. Two distinct agroecological priority maps were created to reflect different stakeholder perspectives. The first focuses on food security by prioritizing rainfed, low-productivity zones, while the second emphasizes environmental restoration in high-input, degraded areas. The limited overlap in the highest priority class indicates divergent stakeholder views. These maps, developed through the Analytical Hierarchy Process, guide targeted areas for priority resource allocation and sustainable farming practices while balancing yield improvements with environmental conservation. The innovation highlights the importance of participatory decision-making, including priority zonation, dynamic policy formulation, and periodic updates to address evolving challenges. This approach offers a replicable model for scaling agroecological practices globally.

description: To overcome the challenges of high costs, outsourcing delays, and technical demands in DNA sequencing, an in-house setup was established using the portable MinION device by Oxford Nanopore Technology. This long-read sequencing technology provides a more complete understanding of a pathogen's genome and captures complex regions, unlike short-read sequencing, which relies on sequence assembly and may lose important genomic information. For bacterial diseases in rice such as bacterial blight, long-read sequencing enables the recovery of intact genome sequences without needing a reference genome. Initial sequencing runs on Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae isolates generated 855,000 reads in 22 hours, reducing turnaround time to three days. The MinION’s portability, affordability, and fast sequencing capabilities allow rapid investigation of new pathogen strains and support resistance strategies for rice breeding programs.
title: An in-house long read DNA sequencing established for rapid monitoring of pathogen populations

For bacterial diseases in rice such as bacterial blight, long-read sequencing enables the recovery of intact genome sequences without needing a reference genome. Initial sequencing runs on Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae isolates generated 855,000 reads in 22 hours, reducing turnaround time to three days. The MinION’s portability, affordability, and fast sequencing capabilities allow rapid investigation of new pathogen strains and support resistance strategies for rice breeding programs. An in-house long read DNA sequencing established for rapid monitoring of pathogen populations

description: The digital transformation of Latin America’s agricultural sector has driven innovation, yet small and medium-sized producers in Guatemala struggle to access and apply these technologies. To bridge this gap, the Bioversity-CIAT Alliance and CUNORI-USAC developed the Digital Plot, an experimental space for agricultural technologies, complemented by digital training diplomas for teachers. These initiatives aim to modernize agronomy curricula and strengthen capacity for integrating digital tools into education. However, achieving systemic change requires stronger collaboration among stakeholders to align education and research with producers' real needs. Using Human-Centered Design, this report analyzes CUNORI’s teacher training initiatives and digital curriculum integration, marking a pivotal step in transforming agricultural education and fostering networks that promote digital innovation adoption. This experience serves as a reference for institutions across the region, emphasizing the importance of co-creating localized solutions to address food system challenges effectively.
title: A Step-by-Step Plan to Integrate Knowledge Acquired from the Digital Agriculture Plot and Courses into Academic Programs

description: The Rice-Field Fisheries Pond for Enhancing Climate Resilience and Productivity integrates climate-resilient practices into traditional rice-fish systems. Key innovations include the installation of inlets and outlets to facilitate water exchange between ponds and rice fields, promoting fish migration, and improving water management. The inclusion of aquatic plants covering 30-40% of the pond area enhances biodiversity and supports ecosystem health, while strategically placed shelters protect fish and deter illegal activities. This system optimizes fish and rice production cycles, allowing farmers to achieve at least two cultivation cycles per year. In addition to boosting yields, the approach enhances climate resilience by ensuring a consistent fish supply, even during periods of water scarcity or erratic rainfall. The innovation has demonstrated significant increases in both rice and fish production—57% and 67%, respectively—while improving profitability for farmers, making it a sustainable solution for food security and income stability in rural communities.

description: This manual provides workflows for conducting spatial ex ante economic analysis of agronomic interventions. We especially leveraged the classic text by Alston et al (1995) that summarized all the methods for evaluating agricultural research and development innovations. Our task was simply to organize the different methods that spawned after Alston et al (1995) as standard operating procedures (SOPs) —i.e., analytical procedures that can be reproducible and replicated in other contexts.  In this manual, researchers will learn how to conduct spatially explicit (mostly gridded) economic evaluation of agronomic innovations with R and other programming software including Octave, and python. Our purpose for these SOPs is to standardize the spatial ex ante economic analysis process with the aim of reducing the amount of time researchers spend on coding the common building blocks of spatial ex ante workflows and improving their efficiency.

description: African Xoo, a causative agent of leaf blight in many parts of Africa, has been found to be widely different from Asian Xoo in terms of genomic characteristics. They have diverged and formed four populations based on existing genomic data from NCBI. To understand how this affects the strategy of resistant variety deployment in Africa, there is a need to monitor the distribution of African Xoo populations and what resistance genes are effective against each population. Our objective is to select and validate SNP markers that can be able to distinguish each of the populations for high-throughput and inexpensive monitoring systems. Validation results showed that the selected markers have low accuracy due to too few numbers of samples available for validation. Hence, there is a need of redesigning the markers and increase number of samples for marker validation
title: Marker development and validation for high throughput monitoring of African bacterial blight populations

description: Rice, a staple in Southeast Asia, is a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions, with climate change increasing insect pest risks. Sustainable solutions are crucial for enhancing rice the resilience of the rice sector. This study evaluates farmers’ preferred biodiversity management strategies to improve ecosystem services and profitability. Farmers identified mung bean as the preferred bund crop and watermelon as the preferred dry-season crop following wet-season rice. Between 2022 and 2024, replicated field experiments tested four treatments, varying pesticide application, bund crops, and dry-season planting. Key metrics assessed included arthropod diversity, pest damage, agronomic performance, costs, and greenhouse gas emissions. Results indicated that pesticide-free systems with diversified cropping experienced less thrips damage, maintained stable grain yields, achieved higher benefit-cost ratios, and produced lower emissions compared to conventional practices. Further analysis will focus on the role of biodiversity management in strengthening climate resilience.
title: Optimized biodiversity management of rice based ecosystem for improved ecosystem services and climate change resilience in Cambodian farming communities: progress and results

description: Land restoration can increase agricultural and ecological productivity where restoration helps producers achieve their livelihood objectives cost-effectively and sustainably. Restoration Co-Design (ReCoDe) is a structured process for fitting restoration techniques based on global and/or local knowledge into the contexts of local management systems. Producers (pastoralists, farmers), practitioners (NGO, government) and researchers (ILRI and partners) co-design restoration protocols, producers test them, and the results are scaled up in producers' restoration plans. ReCoDe is an efficient approach for designing restoration of rangelands, drylands, pastoralist and other communal grazing lands, and other challenging environments for restoration.

description: Faba bean, an essential cool-season legume in Tunisia, faces productivity challenges from viruses transmitted by aphids. A 2023/2024 study at Menzel Bourguiba and Mornag INRAT Station tested virus and aphid management strategies using two faba bean varieties (Najeh and Chourouk), two planting dates, and seed treatments with Cruiser® (Thiamethoxam) at two doses (1.00 and 1.2 cc/kg), compared to untreated seeds. Results showed no virus infection in early planting or Cruiser-treated plots during the second planting, while untreated plots during the second planting had low virus detection (0.4-0.7%). Both varieties produced significantly higher yields with Cruiser-treated seeds. Low rainfall and high temperatures reduced aphid activity, underscoring the effectiveness of adjusting planting dates and seed treatment in managing virus and aphid vectors.
title: Management of persistently aphid-transmitted faba bean viruses in Tunisia

description: Climate change in rangelands creates uncertainty that hinders the long-term direction of research, land management and agricultural production, and policy. The updated rangeland ecosystem projections under climate change use the most recent global climate forecasts (CMIP6) with evaluated model parameters for the G-Range global rangeland simulation model to project how rangeland ecosystems may change through 2050. The spatial dataset produced includes fundamental ecosystem attributes such as net primary productivity (NPP), soil carbon, cover of grass, shrubs, trees, and bare soil, and root:shoot ratio, on a decadal basis. G-Range was driven by climate inputs produced using MarkSimGCM, specifically CMIP6 from 2001 to 2050, and historical data from 2001 to 2020. These outputs are used as inputs to other models and analyses, or for national to global scale estimates of rangeland ecosystem status, structure, and function under climate change, with significant implications for research, land management and agricultural production, and policy.

description: As a proof-of-concept, new technologies in the form of heat-tolerant potential rice varieties were successfully developed by identifying the key genes with at least 0.5 tonne of yield advantage under HNT under Aus and late Boro seasons with good grain quality. Through multi-location trials, we identified superior heat-tolerant rice lines, with some yielding between 3.0 to 5.6 tons per hectare under HNT conditions in Aus season. Notably, varieties like IRRI154 and IR18C1005 showcased resilience to high temperatures (HDT+HNT) for Boro season, to enhance rice production in heat-prone regions based on participatory varietal selection. An economic surplus analysis was done to estimate the projected net economic contributions of IRRI’s heat-tolerant rice varieties (IR18C1002, IR18C1004, IR18C1005, IR18C1009) in Bangladesh from 2025 to 2034. We estimate that net present value of IRRI  and its partners’ contributions to varietal yield changes in Bangladesh for the 2025 to 2034 period is approximately USD 84.81 million.

Parasitic weeds (Orobanche spp.) severely hinder food legume production in the Mediterranean and East African highlands. To combat this issue, a multi-pronged approach was implemented in Ethiopia, Tunisia, and Morocco during the 2023/24 cropping season. This strategy involved integrating partially resistant faba bean varieties with sub-lethal herbicide application and mixed cropping techniques._x000D_
In Ethiopia, the combined application of sub-lethal herbicides and fungicide seed treatments significantly boosted faba bean productivity, with widespread adoption by both male and female farmers. In Tunisia and Morocco, Corum herbicide application effectively reduced parasitic weed infestation on faba bean crops._x000D_
To further drive innovation, the production of early-generation seeds of partially resistant varieties should be facilitated in Ethiopia and Tunisia. Additionally, exploring mixed cropping crops within the cropping system, as well as validating the use of Curum herbicide to control both parasitic and non-parasitic weeds in North Africa, are crucial steps for the 2024/25 cropping season.
title: Demonstration and Scaling of Integrated Management of Parasitic Weeds on Faba bean in Ethiopia, Morocco and Tunisia

description: "In Morocco, faba bean, kabuli chickpea and lentil are key crops in the cereal-based cropping system and provide food and incomes for small holder farmers. Pod borers and green pea aphids are key pests contributing to high yield gaps in the two crops because of weather variability. Farmers practice different cropping systems, but their ecological services are not well investigated. In this study, we investigated the roles of coriander intercropping as alternative management of pod borers in chickpea and green pea aphids on lentil.  Results showed that Coriander intercropping with lentil reduced the mean number of aphids in intercropped plots compared with sole cropping. Likewise, chickpea intercropped with coriander showed reduced mean percent pod damage. Intercropping increased the number and diversity of natural enemies that affect the two pests. This innovation will be further demonstrated under farmer field conditions in 2024/25 cropping season.
title: Management of food legume pod borer and aphids through intercropping in Morocco-24

description: The fall armyworm (FAW), *Spodoptera frugiperda*, threatens irrigated summer maize production in Lebanon and the West Asia-North Africa region, jeopardizing food security and farmer incomes. A 2024 field study in Qob Elias, Bekaa Valley, evaluated an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) approach using pheromone traps and insecticides to manage FAW in imported maize cultivars. Monitoring with pheromone traps guided timely insecticide applications, targeting peak pest activity between September 10 and 29. Early planting and pre-peak interventions were crucial. The IPM strategy significantly reduced FAW infestation to negligible levels compared to traditional methods used by neighboring farmers. Knowledge-sharing sessions, supported by ICARDA and LARI scientists, encouraged local farmers to adopt these sustainable practices. This study emphasizes the effectiveness of pheromone traps in reducing pest populations and insecticide use, offering a practical solution for controlling FAW while promoting sustainable maize production in Lebanon.

description: During the 2024 rust surveys, wheat rust samples were gathered from farmers' fields and research stations in CWANA including Lebanon, Morocco, and Tunisia using the RCRRC sampling kit. The Turkiye-ICARDA Regional Cereal Rust Research Center in Izmir received a total of 595 samples, with 88 from these three countries: 21 from Lebanon, 49 from Morocco, and 18 leaf rust samples from Tunisia. Severe drought prevented yellow rust observations in Morocco and Tunisia, but Lebanon's yellow rust samples were classified as PstS2+virYr27 and PstS17. Understanding of the prevalent races of wheat rust will enable more effective management of this major disease in the CWANA.

description: Trap nurseries comprising yellow, stem, and leaf rust resistance genes planted under natural infection in two locations in Lebanon and Morocco. Despite the availability of differential seeds, the trap nurseries were not planted in Tunisia. In Morocco, a high level of susceptibility to leaf rust was observed in several leaf rust genes, including Lr10, Lr11, Lr12, Lr13, and others across different locations. In contrast, resistance was noted in genes such as Lr2b, Lr3, Lr9, Lr19, Lr34, and others. In Lebanon, field observations indicated differences in yellow rust resistance across two locations, with various resistance genes (e.g., Yr1, Yr2+, Yr3, Yr5, Yr6+, Yr15, and others) remaining effective at Tel Amara and Kfarchakhna. In Marchouch, stem rust resistance genes like Sr21, Sr11, and Sr38 showed effectiveness, while others, including Sr5, Sr6, and Sr36, were ineffective. Details of effectiveness of Yr, Sr, and Lr genes in Morocco and Lebanon is provided.

description: Viruses such as Alfalfa mosaic virus (AMV), Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV), Bean yellow mosaic virus (BYMV), and Pea seed-borne mosaic virus (PSbMV) significantly impact legume crops in the WANA region. These RNA viruses are transmitted via aphids and seeds, threatening the productivity of crops like faba bean, lentil, and chickpea. Current detection methods, primarily ELISA and TBIA, are costly and labor-intensive, requiring separate tests for each virus. Additionally, obtaining specific antisera is challenging. To address these limitations, ICARDA’s Seed Health and Virology Laboratory developed a validated multiplex reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay. This molecular tool efficiently detects and differentiates the four viruses in a single, sensitive test, streamlining virus diagnostics and enabling high-throughput screening of samples. The approach enhances cost-effectiveness and precision in managing virus-related threats to legume crops in the region.

description: The study investigates the incidence and distribution of seed-borne viruses in faba bean and chickpea crops in Tunisia, focusing on their economic and agricultural significance. Seed samples from 20 locations across Tunisia were tested using tissue-blot immunoassay (TBIA) for six viruses: Broad Bean Mottle Virus (BBMV), Broad Bean Stain Virus (BBSV), Pea Seed-borne Mosaic Virus (PSbMV), Bean Yellow Mosaic Virus (BYMV), Alfalfa Mosaic Virus (AMV), and Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV). Among 4,587 faba bean seedlings, only BYMV was detected in two seed lots with a seed transmission rate of 1.7%. For 4,000 chickpea seedlings, AMV and PSbMV were identified in three and nine seed lots, respectively, with seed transmission rates of 1.0% and 3.2%. The highest PSbMV transmission rate (8.3%) was found in two chickpea lots. These findings underscore the need for regular monitoring, improved seed quality, and further research to mitigate virus transmission and enhance crop productivity in Tunisia.

description: Rice yellow mottle virus is a major disease limiting rice productivity across Africa and Madagascar.  Several resistance genes and alleles have been identified in previous studies, but none were available in modern elite backgrounds.  Most of these were found in Oryza glaberrima, and hence extremely difficult to introduce into Oryza sativa (common cultivated rice).  Deployment of these genes has been achieved, including those from O. glaberrima, to very high quality standards.  Elite lines have been registered and shared with AfricaRice and various national partners in ESA.  Testing of lines in Mbe (west Africa) and several sites in ESA (Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique) have shown the effectiveness of most of these genes, with the exception of rymv2.  A resistance strategy combining rymv1-5 + RYMV3 or rymv1-2 + RYMV3 has been developed.  Plans are being laid to increase the frequency of these alleles in elite material, with some populations already established.

description: The IRRI TMeLS-I (Transplanted Medium Maturity Long Grain Soft Grain - Irrigated) market segment has been benefiting nearly 6M hectares in South Asia, with 6 NARES partners in India and 3 in Bangladesh. OneRice strategy has shortened breeding cycle length from 6 to 3 years. Breeding materials tested in the 2023 wet season were generated using marker assisted selection in Rapid Generation Advance. After field evaluation in the TPE (target population of environments) sites, genomic selection was used to generate multiple-location summaries with gBLUP (genomic best linear unbiased prediction) estimates. GEBV (genomically estimated breeding value) estimates were generated for both tested and untested lines. High performing lines were selected for stage 2 testing. Comparison of average yields of current year tested materials against previous years showed positive genetic gain trend. The 1.77% rate of genetic gain was achieved through NARES engagement, strict implantation of population improvement, and predictive breeding methods.

description: The digital tool supports India's strategy in land restoration through improving outcomes of tree-based restoration and planting activities. The tool was developed for the Western Ghats, a biodiversity hotspot region, to help with choosing appropriate tree species and seed sources for tree-based restoration or other tree planting activities. Using species distribution and suitability models, the tool can choose appropriate tree species that survive current and future climatic conditions for a specified location. The tool uses a trait-based approach (based on 110 functional traits) to identify appropriate species (from 246 species) from a suitable list of species for the region based on local site conditions and restoration objectives while also accounting for current and future climatic scenarios. A list of species with seed sources based on restoration objectives and species diversity is provided to the user as a guide to select appropriate species and seed sources for restoration of specified location.
