description: A major limitation in improving the efficiency of rice breeding through utilizing major genes is the availability of those genes in elite genetic backgrounds. To enable rice breeders to gain the value of these major genes without the penalties associated with the original landrace donors, deployment of selected genes has been initiated into an elite genetic background. The deployment includes rigorous Quality Control (QC) standards for introgression, including >95% recovery of the elite background and <2cM introgression size. To date, over 60 major genes have been deployed, mostly to the IRRI 154 background.  Many of these are now validated, and lines (single genes and pyramids) have been distributed to many partners.

description: An AI-driven system for common bean disease detection was developed using advanced deep learning and object detection technologies. A comprehensive image dataset was collected from disease hotspots in Africa and Colombia, focusing on five major diseases: Angular Leaf Spot (ALS), Common Bacterial Blight (CBB), Common Bean Mosaic Virus (CBMV), Bean Rust, and Anthracnose. Pod images were available only for ALS. This innovation used data augmentation and both whole and micro-level annotations, training three YOLO architectures: YOLOv7, YOLOv8, and YOLO-NAS. YOLO-NAS achieved the highest mean average precision (mAP) of 97.9% and recall of 98.8% for whole leaf detection, while YOLOv7 and YOLOv8 performed better for pod detection. Micro annotations showed lower performance across all diseases. The YOLO-NAS models were deployed in an Android app, achieving 90% classification accuracy on unseen data. These models were integrated into the new Tumaini bean app for real-time disease detection.

description: Decisionmakers lack guidance on how to transform food systems from their current unsustainable trajectories toward more desirable, healthy, sustainable, resilient, and equitable outcomes in a comprehensive and integrated way. This conceptual framework integrates multiple perspectives and practical experiences on transition, transformation and politics to propose a holistic diagnostic and prescriptive tool for decisionmakers to navigate the process. The two-dimension framework combines domains of politics with processes of transformation, which, together, outline how temporal configurations of political actions could be  leveraged to overcome persistent unsustainable regime trajectories and drive food systems toward more normative transformative goals. The framework can be applied as a diagnostic tool to understand past transformation processes and investigate why new ideas, institutions, innovations, and narratives failed to emerge or to be scaled up. It can also be leveraged by actors across various levels to assess the nature of diverse politics that hinder current transformation actions.

description: The innovation describes how sheep use a unique amalgam of behavioral, physiological and genetic mechanisms to preserve fertility under a looming scenario of warmer climate. Management of reproduction that relies on naturally based solutions is extremely important to counter the negative perception around hormone-based interventions. In Mediterranean latitudes and wider regions of non-tropical drylands, sheep do not normally ovulate during spring but exposure to a ram can induce oestrus and ovulation. This innovation promotes the use of the response of maiden Barbarine ewes in drylands to the ‘ram effect’ during springtime for improved fertility.
title: Robust management practice ('ram effect') for enhanced reproductive performance of sheep for farmers in dryland areas.

description: The  increasing  global  temperature  due  to  climate  change  causes  an  increase  in  new  or  previously  negligible  diseases.  The  incidence  of  Burkholderia  glumae  has  been  reported  to  increase  in  recent  years  in  many  rice  growing  regions.   Burholderia  glumae  is  a  seedborne  pathogen  causing  bacterial  panicle  blight  of  rice.  It  infects  rice  at  different  growth  stages  causing  grain  rot,  sheath  rot  and  seedling  rot  symptoms  depending  on  the  rice  growth  stages. Bacterial  panicle  blight  is  difficult  to  manage  in  the  absence  of  effective  chemical  control  measures. Rapid and early disease detection  is needed to avoid severe yield losses. The development of this diagnostic method and the scaling out through the National Seed Quality Service of the Philippines enables the fast and inexpensive early detection of the agent on rice seeds across the country preventing farmers losses due to panicle blight.

description: Homestead gardening is the most complex multi-strata integrated production system that combines all farming components (crop, livestock, tree, and occasionally fish) and provides household food security, employment, and income generation opportunities. In addition, this innovation will also increase women's empowerment.

description: IFPRI’s global cropping system model – Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM) comprises the estimates of crop area, yield and production for 40+ major crops under four rainfed and irrigated production systems across a global 5 arc minute grid. This is done through a downscaling approach that accounts for spatial variation in the biophysical conditions influencing the productivity of individual crops within the cropland extent, and that uses crop prices to weigh the gross revenue potential of alternate crops when considering how to prioritize the allocation of specific crops to individual gridcells. Based on the SPAM global model, we further developed the SPAM country model, so it is more suitable for regional and country studies. The most recent global SPAM products are outdated (global: 2010, Sub-Saharan Africa: 2017). Under the ClimBeR initiative, we update the input data to 2020 to capture the recent changes of crop production to develop climate-risk profiles.
title: Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM) 2020 for country studies of crop production systems

Based on the SPAM global model, we further developed the SPAM country model, so it is more suitable for regional and country studies. The most recent global SPAM products are outdated (global: 2010, Sub-Saharan Africa: 2017). Under the ClimBeR initiative, we update the input data to 2020 to capture the recent changes of crop production to develop climate-risk profiles. Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM) 2020 for country studies of crop production systems

The model is currently being tested and applied in Myanmar aimed at improving food and nutrition security and alleviating poverty through improved and integrated aquaculture. DSM will be possibly reveal complex relationships in the interaction of the intervention with the system that cannot be captured by more traditional designs and analysis. The model results will help design and plan better interventions in the aquatic food systems space.

AquaIndex supports evidence-based decision-making to improve aquaculture governance, policy interventions, and investment strategies. It will help guide sustainable practices, ensuring that aquatic food systems contribute to food security, climate resilience, and economic stability while minimizing environmental impact.

description:
Known as the rice-fish decision support system (DSS), it is a bundle of digital and analytical tools used to inform the planning and management of rice-fish systems. Suitability maps derived from the DSS have shown the potential for the transformation of 15,700 km2 across the Ayeyarwady region, supporting improved local food security, nutritional security, incomes, and employment. As well as helping identify areas most suitable to the introduction of rice-fish polyculture, the tools help ensure that the needs of stakeholders are taken into consideration. A similar Decision Support System (DSS) for rice-fish suitability is now being developed for Cambodia following the same approach and method as the one in place for Myanmar. In addition, the DSS for Myanmar has now been refined at a lower scale to support decisions at the local level._x000D_

description:
The interrelationship between economic growth, poverty, and food security is highly complex, with relatively few studies conducted on this topic in recent years. To address this gap, the Growth, Poverty, and Undernutrition Monitoring Model (GPUMM), developed by IFPRI, serves as an economic modeling tool designed to better understand these connections holistically by employing a macro-micro modeling approach linking a macroeconomic model with micro-level household survey data. _x000D_
_x000D_
We have completed the model calibration, enabling us to provide a comprehensive and consistent view of how macroeconomic changes influence income distribution, which in turn drives poverty and hunger rates over time. _x000D_
_x000D_
Using this model, we developed projections of how economic growth will affect poverty and undernutrition rates through 2026. This projection results help countries in tracking their progress toward achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

description: This organizational innovation defines a prioritized and harmonized shortlist of indicators, featuring the most impactful indicators for measuring breeding program performance and the impact of modernization efforts.  During 2023, 26 indicators were identified that feature key components of monitoring and decision making across the product development process. During 2024, eight center teams utilized the indicators to establish Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in their respective centers and programs to track efficiency and performance throughout the product development process. At the same time, indicators that can be sourced from information systems were identified and system interoperability established to drive a dashboard and "a harmonized crop report". The dashboard and report include measures for relevance, partnerships, investment, development progress, scaling, and projected benefits. Conceptually, they are scalable across any CGIAR development pipeline. Indicators establish the success criteria of teams and processes. They provide opportunity to more precisely target improvement and generate transparency.

description: This innovation introduces a decentralized, scalable system for the mass production and distribution of four released matooke hybrids—TARIBAN1 to TARIBAN4—in Tanzania. It combines the in vitro multiplication capacities of two public research labs (TARI Arusha and Dar es Salaam) and two SMEs (Crop Bioscience Solutions and Mauri Mazuri) to ensure a reliable supply of quality planting materials. By linking production to nurseries and distributing plantlets through both public and private channels, the innovation increases farmer access to improved banana varieties. It supports faster adoption, enhances varietal reach, and strengthens the role of public–private partnerships in seed system development.
title: A scalable, multi-actor in vitro system for mass production and distribution of four released matooke hybrids, enabling timely access to improved planting material through public and private sector collaboration.

description:
Solomon Islands remains a highly agricultural society with high rates of consumption of traditional subsistence garden produce and aquatic foods. Imported foods have a role to play, but only if they are viewed as complementary to the local foods produced from gardens and seas rather than being a major component of the diet. Imagining food futures based on strengths in Indigenous food systems is important to change the course of island food systems in transition. Strengthening Indigenous food systems in Solomon Islands has been a priority by WorldFish and KastomGaden Association. A tokStori (indigenous forum format) brought together rural actors and key stakeholders to talk about traditional farming and aquatic foods under a nutrition-sensitive approach and to listen to ideas about what the Solomon Islands food systems future could look like. It has created a social movement platform for strengthening island food systems with Indigenous foods. _x000D_
Still relevant in 2024.

description: An area-based yield (ARBY) index insurance for rice based on satellite data is being developed and tested in the Philippines. ARBY provides coverage based on historical average yield of a specific geographic area, rather than individual farmers’ yields, to determine payouts in the event of crop losses. The current and historical yields are based on the Philippine Rice Information System (PRISM, https://prism.philrice.gov.ph/), an innovative satellite-based rice mapping and monitoring system. Operational since 2018, PRISM uses time series Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), a smart detection system, and crop growth simulation modeling to map rice areas and provide timely yield forecasts and end-of-season rice yields. It is more efficient than the traditional indemnity-based crop insurance which involves manual visits and verifications for each claim. By leveraging modern technologies, better crop insurance products and services can be offered to farmers to help improve their resilience to climatic risks.

description: The Rice Crop Manager (RCM) database contains 283,346 recommendations across 31 districts in Odisha, eastern India. RCM's functionality can be extended beyond fertilizer recommendations to include comprehensive crop management decision-making and the development of support systems for various stakeholders. The methodology employs advanced technologies such as machine learning to create a model that selects optimal parameters for generating these recommendations. The target yield has also been estimated using a calibration and validation ratio of 70:30, with performance evaluation primarily based on R-square, Root Mean Square Error, and Mean Absolute Error calculations. The analysis indicates that the approach is suitable for the data collected and can be automated to generate more valuable information for farmers' benefit.

description: In Africa, food legumes like cowpeas and beans are vital protein sources but suffer yield losses of up to 80% due to insect pests. Smallholder farmers rely on insecticides, contributing to resistance and food safety concerns. This study explores a sustainable alternative using semiochemicals for pest management. Using coupled gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC–MS) and coupled GC-electroantennographic detection (EAD) analyses, this study identified 2-methylbutyl 2-methylbutanoate as the aggregation pheromone of Clavigralla elongata, a key legume pest. Field trials in East and West Africa showed this pheromone and its aanalog isopentyl butanoate, attracted multiple pests, including Maruca vitrata, Megalurothrips sjostedti, Bemisia tabaci, and the natural enemy Gryon fulviventris. Optimized pheromone traps significantly reduced pests and increased natural enemy density sixfold. Legume yields in pheromone-treated fields matched insecticide-treated ones, exceeding controls by 320–590%. These findings establish coreid bug pheromones as effective, sustainable tools for legume pest management without insecticides.
title: Breakthrough discovery on plant odour sources to mimic attractant pheromones

description:
Rice and fish are the main commodities produced and consumed in Cambodia. They provide the most contribution to caloric intake, but are affected by climate change. description: Sufficient planting material is a major limitation in sweetpotato trialing. However, rapid clonal propagation methods now enable large-scale multiplication of planting materials within a few months. This approach was used to multiply breeding clones for advanced yield trials. In Uganda, the International Potato Center (CIP), in collaboration with the National Agricultural Research Organization (NARO), Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), and Tanzania Agricultural Research Institute (TARI), generated 74,450 vine cuttings for advanced yield trials conducted at 20 locations. Each trial was replicated three times, with 45 plants per plot. Additionally, CIP Mozambique produced 2,050 kg of 20 breeding clones for testing in Target Population of Environments (TPE), Multi-Environment Trials (MET), and on-farm trials. In total, 170 on-farm trials, 10 replicated TPE trials, and 7 replicated METs were established. Variety release decisions are informed by data collected from METs and on-farm trials.
title: Rapid propagation techniques significantly increased the supply of sweetpotato vine cuttings of promising clones, enabling the establishment of advanced yield trials across breeding programs in Uganda, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Rwanda.

description: Nutritional traits are important in sweet potato breeding. Iron is important to prevent anemia in pregnant mothers and children. High levels of polyphenols inhibit iron absorption and its always important to strike a balance between the two. The list provided shows genotypes that were selected for advancement due to high levels of iron and zinc. After further analysis of nutritional content, eating quality traits and agronomic data, four clones in the orange fleshed pipeline and seven clones in the white fleshed pipeline were selected, handed over to the national agriculture research program for final testing and variety release of at least one clone from each pipeline. Released varieties have a wider reach to communities that suffer most from micronutrient deficiency problems.

description: Sweetpotato product development team uses the triadic comparison of technologies approach. In 2024, CIP Mozambique tested 11 pre-released clones under on-farm for multi-stakeholder validation across five provinces (Niassa, Nampula, Zambezia, Manica and Inhambane) ensuring representation of diverse environments and farmer conditions. In each province 5 districts were selected for on-farm trialing and a total of 170 farmers successfully established the trials. The TRICOT design was the experimental design of choice.  Most agricultural actors, including farmers, extension officers and other local government representatives were involved in the setting up of trials and their assessment. Farmer and other stakeholders feedback on performance clones will be utilized and incorporated into decisions of variety release and genetic gains in farmers’ fields will be calculated. The validation system strengthened the selection and adoption of new varieties, integrating farmer needs and gender considerations into breeding advancements.

description: The project “Natural silvopastoral systems in the Colombian Orinoquia Region” is a grouped carbon project comprising a set of activities to improve grassland management in approximately 150,000 ha of Vichada and Meta, Colombia. The crediting period is 2020 to 2040 applying the Verra Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management VM0042 Version 2.0. The project primary objective is to achieve a reduction in overall emissions by focusing on carbon sequestration. This will be accomplished mainly by implementing adaptive multi-paddock grazing with improved deep-rooted grass cultivars, specifically Urochloa humidicola. An estimate of the annual average and total GHG emission reductions and removals are approximately 270,000 t CO2eq per year and 5,400,000 t CO2eq, respectively. Prior to the implementation of the project, livestock practices in the regions are characterized by annual burning of savannas and low-quality animal feed. The project was successfully listed in the pipeline of the Verra Registry in November 2023.

description: Seed-borne bacteria impact plant health and yield, and bacterial-contaminated seed is a source for the transboundary spread of pathogens. Due to a lack of effective seed-dressing agents, eliminating seed-borne bacteria involves the hot-water treatment, which is laborious, sensitive to temperature settings, and known to affect seed viability. This study evaluated mancozeb and carbendazim for their bactericidal properties by testing against eight seed-borne bacterial species (Bacillus cereus, Bacillus subtilis, Ralstonia solanecearum, Xanthomonas manihotis, Pantoea stewartii, Xanthomonas glycinea, Xanthomonas oryzae and Xanthomonas vignicola) in three crops (cowpea, maize, and soybean). Seed dressing with mancozeb resulted in 100% suppression of seed-borne bacteria and serves as the broad-spectrum reagent for seed dressing to eliminate seed-borne bacterial infection. Mancozeb is widely available, and doubles as a reagent for preventing seed-borne and bacterial contamination. To our knowledge, this is the first study to validate the effectiveness of mancozeb to control seed-borne bacterial contamination.
title: A cost-effective fungicide seed-dressing for the control of seed-borne bacterial pathogens

description: Leaf blast in rice, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, is challenging to manage due to diverse avirulence (AVR) genes. Effective resistance deployment requires detecting AVR genes specific to M. oryzae strains. The pathogen has four populations based on genomic characteristics (genome-wide SNP data), each with distinct pathogenicity patterns. We developed and validated 8 SNP markers to distinguish these populations and 39 markers targeting AVR genes, including AVR-Pizt, AVR-Pii, AVR-Pia, AVR-Pik, AVR-Pib, AVR-Pi9, and AVR-Pita. Using PACE, 26 markers showed ≥80% sensitivity, 50% specificity, or 81% accuracy for monitoring. Additional markers are under development, with successful ones integrated into the PathoTracer platform and validated with isolates from other countries.
title: Development of a high-throughput genotyping platform to monitor rice blast pathogens from field samples

description: PathoTracer, developed by IRRI, is a decision-support platform for rice disease and pathogen management. In 2023, it underwent a transformation from the PathoTracer RShiny to a more advanced QlikSense application, aiming to automate data management and improve visualization of rice pathogen data, especially for Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo). The updated PathoTracer2.0 dashboard, powered by QlikSense Enterprise and Amazon Web Services, offers dynamic visualization and analysis, enabling users to track global Xoo incidences and dominant AXoo strains. Incorporating data from 19 partner institutes, it also lists rice varieties with resistance genes, aiding informed decision-making in rice disease management. In 2024, PathoTracer was improved and reverted to using Rshiny and R visualization libraries for mapping Xoo isolate locations. The application currently houses data submitted from 22 partner institutes. List of varieties containing R-genes for specific Axoo populations was also enabled.
title: PathoTracer 2.0: Advanced Rice Disease Management through Dynamic Data Visualization and Analysis

description: This activity provides support for policy design, implementation and appraisal in the area of agriculture diversification in the Eastern and Southern African region with a specific focus on the Ukama Ustawi focus countries. The toolkit will have two components for a start namely; a) an up-to-date database of indicators relevant to diversification, and b) a policy oriented report. The policy support tool, thus, seeks to avail timely and comprehensive information on the key indicators of diversification, its benefits and challenges. These indicators will include inventories of key value chains in the region and for each country, highlighting the current and past levels of productivity, shares of intra-and extra-regional trade and opportunities enhancing, and challenges limiting sustainable diversification and value chain development. The  toolkit also tracks and highlights the status of socio-economic characteristics of the population in the Eastern and Southern Africa, and their interface with agriculture outcomes. The data generated will also be availed in interactive maps to permit quick analysis and presentation of information  for decision making. The report will present key recommendations for policy makers and practitioners to ensure regional and country resilience, and food security  for all, through sustainable agriculture diversification.

description: Diagnostic of African swine fever(ASF) includes from clinical diagnostics to identification of the agent to serological tests, according to the World Organisation of Animal Health. Clinical diagnostics is often challenging since ASF shares common clinical signs with other pig diseases in its acute form; and for the chronic forms subtle clinical signs can be overlook. Laboratory diagnostics are more accurate, including the identification of the viral particle or the presence of antibodies against the virus. However, all these laboratory test pose the same problem, they are difficult to implement in the field where infrastructures and human expertise is limited. A new generation of rapid lateral flow assays for the ASF diagnostic have been developed by various companies for both viral particle detection and anti-ASF Virus antibodies detection. We evaluated different LFA with interest for the African market. A report with the findings and a proposed way forward will be provided.
title: Penside rapid diagnostics for African swine fever for use by veterinarians and veterinary technicans in Low and Middle Income Countries.

description: The Tumaini app has undergone significant upgrades to improve banana disease detection. FasterRCNN models were replaced by more advanced YOLOv8 models, resulting in faster and more accurate detections. A step-by-step intelligent detection algorithm, developed with expert phytopathologists, guides users through symptom scanning, improving accuracy by identifying the most affected plant parts and comparing them to reference images. Region-specific AI models were also developed for different continents, increasing the total number of models from 7 to 35, further enhancing detection precision. New diseases, such as Moko in Latin America and Leaf Spot in India, were added to the detection system. Tumaini now requires user registration, ensuring data security and allowing plant detections to be linked to specific users. Additionally, users can map and georeference healthy or diseased banana plants, sharing this information in real-time through the online dashboard. Lastly, This new Tumaini version includes gender disaggregation to collect data on users.
title: Refinement of deep learning detection models to enhance a digital tool for pest and disease surveillance of banana pest and diseases

description: Many virus detection methods are mostly performed in a laboratory but also are time-consuming, and expensive. The Loop-mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) method has been adapted and/ or adopted for using on site (i.e., greenhouse, field, etc.) and it is cheaper and rapid in detecting viruses. Doctor Vida is a portable device originally developed LAMP detection of SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic and is now being adapted for testing plant pathogens as a cost-effective alternative for virus detection. Comparative tests using the same reagents and virus-infected samples showed 100% concordance and similar sensitivity between Doctor Vida and Genie (the gold standard) for detecting sweetpotato viruses (SPFMV, SPCSV, and begomoviruses). Besides, Doctor Vida operates with portable power sources like cell phone power banks, making it suitable for on-site virus detection. These findings confirm the reliability of LAMP tests on Doctor Vida device for detecting plant pathogens.
title: Use of Doctor Vida device for virus testing in sweetpotato by Loop-mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) method

description: Forage legumes such as velvet bean, lablab, and cowpea are usually of a vigorous growth habit and their integration as rotational crops in maize systems reduces the competition between the maize and the legumes. In such systems, more biomass is produced such that a part of it can be fed to livestock while another part is retained as mulch although in most cases it is not adequate. However, such diets are usually high in protein with the need to balance them off with high-energy grasses for a more balanced diet for animals. The introduction of Brachiaria grass (Brachiaria ruziziensis) as a hedgerow in the maize-forage legume rotation system is a possible solution. The maize and the legume are grown in two separate fields and rotated annually. In each phase of the rotation, Brachiaria is grown between the first two and the last two crop rows as hedgerows.
title: Brachiaria grass hedgerows in maize-forage legume rotation systems for improved crop and livestock productivity in conservation agriculture systems

description: The AADGG-Dairy mobile app, co-designed by the Africa-Asia Dairy Genetic Gains (AADGG) program and the Digital Innovation (DI) Initiative, enhances real-time data capture and validation while ensuring functionality in low-connectivity areas. Developed in collaboration with the DI and SAPLING initiatives, the app provides rapid data summaries and feedback to support livestock extension personnel. The app features an intuitive interface, guiding extension agents through a series of prompts to collect farm and animal data efficiently. Its offline data capture ensures usability in remote areas, with automatic synchronization when online. Farmers and agents can track individual animals, maintaining comprehensive records on breeding, health, and productivity. This improves farm-level productivity, ultimately leading to higher incomes. In 2024, the app was rolled out in Kenya, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, and Nepal, with training sessions conducted for users. The AADGG platform (https://portal.adgg.ilri.org/) continues to support multi-country genetic gains in smallholder livestock systems.

description: Pod borer and aphids are the most economically important insect pests in chickpea and faba bean respectively. Besides their economic damage, aphids play a role as virus vectors on food legumes. This study aimed to validate eco-friendly biopesticides (entomopathogenic fungi and essential oils) on pod borers and aphids selected in 2021/22. Laboratory results showed that two entomopathogenic fungi (Verticillium lecanii and Paecilomyces farinosus) were effective against second instar larvae of chickpea pod borer.  Similar results were found under field conditions where the two entomopathogenic fungi reduced larval population. The essential oils extracted from Ocimum basilicum and Origanum vulgare at 5000 ppm were the most effective against aphids under field conditions. Entomopathogenic fungi and essential oils can be integrated in the management of pod borers and aphids as eco-friendly alternative pest management options in Morocco. Efforts will be made to test different formulations in 2023/24 cropping season.

description: In Morocco, faba bean and kabuli chickpea are the most important legume crops for their high protein content and incomes for farmers. Farmers practice different cropping systems but their ecological services like pest management are not investigated. In this study, we investigated the roles of coriander intercropping as alternative management of pod borers in chickpea and faba bean aphids.  Results showed that Coriander intercropping with chickpea reduced the mean number of pod damage (28%) as compared with sole cropping (49%). In faba bean, the mean number of aphids was decreased in faba bean intercropped with Coriander as opposed to sole cropping.  Intercropping increased the number and diversity of natural enemies that affect the two pests. This innovation will be further demonstrated under farmer field conditions in 2023/24 cropping season.

description: The AgWise generalizable decision support framework was used to develop potato fertilizer recommendations in Rwanda. This was in response to a request from the Rwanda Agriculture Board to optimize fertilizer rates for potato, either by reducing rates and achieving the same yields, or increasing yields by 10-20% over existing average yields obtained applying the blanket recommendation. The workflow was based on machine learning and crop modeling approaches, and generated fertilizer advice that: (1) is compatible with the national fertilizer subsidy scheme complexities; (2) avoids major rework of current system for delivery; (3) tailors advice at agroecology level while providing evidence to refine factors that will capture withi-agroecology spatial variation; (4) considers commonly used fertilizer formulations; and (5) supports validation by providing fertilizer packages and treatment structures. The recommendations are being field-validated or analyzed.

description: The AgWise generalizable decision support framework was used to develop maize fertilizer recommendations for the county governments, extension, and e-voucher system in Kenya. This was in response to a request from the government and partners to increase maize yields by 30% over existing average yields. The workflow was based on machine learning and crop modeling approaches, and generated fertilizer advice that: (1) Accounts for soil nutrient deficiencies using on-farm data and digital soil maps; (2) Considers fertilizer response under smallholder management (survey data); (3) Considers multi-year data and rainfall, but permits refining based on seasonal forecasts; (4) Allows customised yield targets at (sub) county level relative to current production; and (5) Can generate recommendations for different fertilizer formulations. The recommendations will be field-validated in 2024.

description: The innovation lies in advancing methods to assess sensory traits, particularly mealiness, hardness, brownness and fibrousness in sweetpotato, thereby enhancing the selection and adoption of varieties. Sensory panels, comprising 12 individuals, were employed to evaluate 114 genotypes. Concurrently, a texture analyzer provided objective data on hardness, facilitating high-throughput phenotyping. Additionally, DIGeye photo scans were utilized to develop models for mealiness and brownness. Notably, subjective assessments of hardness correlated strongly with those obtained via the texture analyzer, validating its utility for selection purposes. While this innovation offers promising avenues for sweetpotato breeding and selection, further evidence is required to refine mealiness models developed by DIGeye. This initiative targets breeders, researchers and stakeholders in sweetpotato value chain and aims to optimize variety development by prioritizing sensory traits. Future plans involve refining and validating these methods to streamline the breeding process and meet consumer preferences effectively

description: Khotang and Surkhet lie in the mid-hills of Nepal and are drought-prone areas. Insufficient water availability in both areas has impacted agricultural productivity. During the participatory innovation selection process for various components of MFS, farmers ranked micro-irrigation as their priority innovation to increase vegetable productivity. Hence, interested farmers were given training on micro-irrigation practices, along with efficient water use practices including conservation agriculture, mulching, and multi-use water systems. 76 drip irrigation kits and 114 sprinkler heads have been distributed to the farmers for the pilot study. Farmers are selected based on inclusive criteria to ensure that women and marginalized farmers are not left behind.

description: The CGIAR Initiative on Fragility to Resilience in Central and West Asia and North Africa (F2R-CWANA) is establishing Agronomy Community of Practices (ACoP) in countries within CWANA. So far, ACoPs have been established in Sudan, Egypt, and Uzbekistan. This collaborative network aims to overcome barriers that hinder technology transfer and agricultural development by facilitating knowledge exchange among its members. The ACoP focuses on discussing scientific ideas, innovations, joint publications, local knowledge utilization, and context-specific agronomic solutions to enhance food and nutritional security in the region. Membership is open to individuals actively contributing to agricultural development through relevant practices. Online training sessions have been delivered to familiarize members with the establishment, rules, regulations, and objectives of the ACoP.

description:
The Local Technical Advisory Committee (LTAC) is a dialogue process among a diversity of local actors including scientists, technicians, representatives from the public and private sectors, and farmers, which seeks to understand the climate’s possible behavior in a locality, and to generate agro-advisories to reduce risks associated with expected climate variability. This dialogue is  used to create an agroclimatic bulletin that contains the region’s climate prediction, as well as climate smart recommendations around decision-making for each productive sector. In general, climate predictions produced by each country’s meteorological service are provided in the LTAC meeting, and the LTAC members, from various institutions, identify climate-smart agro-advisories to the climate predictions, and then the climate predictions and the agro-advisories are shared with local extension officers and farmers in the form of agroclimatic bulletins._x000D_
_x000D_
The LTAC was piloted in Battambang and Kampong Speu and is now being expanded to other Lower Mekong provinces in Cambodia.

description: The Multi-Stakeholder Agriculture Knowledge Hub (MSAKH) is an innovative platform that fosters collaboration among local and municipal stakeholders to address agricultural challenges, share experiences, and promote sustainable mixed farming systems. Its primary goals include empowering farmers—particularly women, Dalits, and marginalized groups—by improving their access to resources and advocating for policy changes. The key objectives of the platform are to enhance inclusive participation, facilitate knowledge sharing, strengthen advocacy, build capacity, support monitoring and coordination, and scale innovative agricultural practices. In March 2024, four MSAKHs were established—one each in Wards 6 and 7 of Halesi Tuwachung Municipality and Wards 12 and 14 of Gurbhakot Municipality. These hubs were formed in the presence of the research team, social mobilizers, municipal staff, and ward chairpersons. Each MSAKH comprises diverse stakeholders, including farmers, agro-entrepreneurs, local elected representatives and officials, financial institutions, community-based organizations (CBOs), and the private sector.

description: This innovation builds on  Africa RISING technology which evaluated the effect of time of NPK fertilizer application for maize production in northern Ghana and reported an increase in grain yield (22-59%), agronomic nitrogen use efficiency (26-80%), return on investment (1-9 Fold), reduction in ammonia flux emission (1-49%) with application of NPK fertilizer to maize at planting relative to the conversional practice of applying NPK fertilizer to maize at 2 weeks after planting (Irmgard 2021; unpublished data). Adoption study of the innovation by farmers showed that about 40-98% of them are not applying the innovation. Inadequate availability of labor was cited as key barrier to scaling of innovation. The objective of this innovation is to address the labor challenges associated with the planting of maize and application of NPK fertilizer on the same day using sample planters. The hand push planter sow’s maize seed and apply fertilizer in two different holes.
title: Mechanizing maize seed and basal NPK fertilizer application to improve grain yield, nutrient use efficiency and biomass availability for livestock feed

description: The development of the Human Security Index (HSI) aims to fill in the gaps on empirical research that has clearly defined the concept of human security and rendered it measurable. The Asian Mega Deltas (AMD) Initiative's research aims to create a HSI specifically tailored for rural areas,where communities are often increasingly vulnerable to impacts of climate change. Inspired from the HSI developed by Adger et al. (2020), AMD aims to better capture and assess the unique challenges and security concerns experienced by people living in rural contexts, particularly those exacerbated by climate change. We collected the data for HSI in the Ganges Delta in Bangladesh and Mekong Delta in Vietnam. This initiative seeks to provide a more accurate and context-specific tool for evaluating and understanding human security in rural environments contributing to effective strategies and policies aimed at addressing the needs of vulnerable populations in the face of climate-related challenges.

description: Sweetpotato is saline and heat tolerant in general, and considered as a climate resilient crop. To promote sweetpotato in the region for smallholder farmers, and address challenges in current sweetpotato seed systems and available varieties, the Asian Mega Deltas (AMD) Initiative through the International Potato Center (CIP) proposes to conduct a breeding pilot project with a 95-day short maturity orange fleshed sweetpotato material which comes from the CIP sweetprotato Asia short duration breeding pipeline (BP00052), and purple fleshed with high-yeilding and high dry-matter content clones. The project duration is planned to be 20 months, starting from April 2023 to December 2024. Sweetpotato true seeds from San Ramon, Peru with elite crosses (humid tropics) will be sent from Lima, Peru to Vietnam and germinated in Dalat, Central Highlands of Vietnam where the temperature is stable year around. Currently, on-farm trials in farmers' field conditions are being done in Vietnam.

description: his innovation consists of a database schema to integrate findings from multiple high-profile farm household surveys, including the World Bank's LSMS-ISA and the CGIAR's RHoMIS surveys, and others. The combined data are available for exploration and anlaysis through dashboards, which permit description of the farming practices and human welfare and livelihoods status. Additionally, there are various options for sub-setting populations according to geographic location, farming system type, asset/wealth category, standardised livelihood typologies, user defined threshold-based typologies, or user defined empirically defined typologies. This innovation akes two significant contributions: first, by providing a common means to integrate data from multiple farm household surveys; and second, by providing an accessible means to conduct farming systems analysis for the planning and prioritisation of research and development activities. It is currently in at a pilot stage, meaning that full functionality has been achieved and it is being tested by potential users.

description: This analytical framework was developed by the author to facilitate an understanding of the political economy of policies for crop diversification in Bangladesh. It seeks to unravel the intricate connections linking economic processes, political policies, and social institutions. The analytical framework presented here is a practical tool by which to analyze the political economy of agricultural policymaking.  It presents the processes, methods, tools, and techniques followed by the various actors in policymaking, to aid the reader’s understanding of, specifically, the political economy of policies pertaining to crop diversification. It will help us understand the relevant policies, programs, projects, resource use, impacts, scale, good practices, and learnings from specific initiatives. The results of such an exercise may help steer the focus of future policy and development in the agriculture sector.

description: This study sought to evaluate the resilience of intercropping (cowpea and maize) in northern Ghana, using system dynamics modelling approach. A simulation model was developed to provide insights into how this intercropping enables households to remain food secure, boost their income, and maintain natural resource capital, concurrently. The model enables quantitative evaluation of cause(s) and effect(s) of implementing an agricultural technology or new policy on different sustainable intensification domains i.e. production, economics, environment, human condition and social inclusion. The model is targeted to be used by policy makers, technology scaling experts and researchers. The model is scalable to other geographies provided that the site specific inter-linkages between different sub-systems are defined after stakeholders consultation.
title: A system dynamics approach for assessing policies for promoting resilience of maize-cowpea intercropping in Ghana

description: Soybean is an important legume and cash crop in Ghana. The grains are good source of protein  food for household consumption, it  used to make cooking oil as well as feed in the poultry industry. The fodder is also a good source of feed for livestock and it  also improves soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation. However, low soil fertility is a major constrain for soybean production in Ghana and the lack of consideration of fodder quality in the selection criteria of improve varieties by national breeding program affects its use in crop-livestock farming system. This innovation assess the effect of soil amendment and improve soybean varieties on quality of grain and fodder production in crop-livestock farming systems in northern Ghana.
title: Improve soybean variety and soil amendment for quality grain and  fodder production in northern Ghana

The fodder is also a good source of feed for livestock and it  also improves soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation. However, low soil fertility is a major constrain for soybean production in Ghana and the lack of consideration of fodder quality in the selection criteria of improve varieties by national breeding program affects its use in crop-livestock farming system. This innovation assess the effect of soil amendment and improve soybean varieties on quality of grain and fodder production in crop-livestock farming systems in northern Ghana. Improve soybean variety and soil amendment for quality grain and  fodder production in northern Ghana

description:
The Multi-Stakeholder Agriculture Knowledge Hub (MSAKH) is an innovative platform that fosters collaboration among local and municipal stakeholders to address agricultural challenges, share experiences, and promote sustainable mixed farming systems. Its primary goals include empowering farmers—particularly women, Dalits, and marginalized groups—by improving their access to resources and advocating for policy changes._x000D_
The key objectives of the platform are to enhance inclusive participation, facilitate knowledge sharing, strengthen advocacy, build capacity, support monitoring and coordination, and scale innovative agricultural practices._x000D_
In March 2024, four MSAKHs were established—one each in Wards 6 and 7 of Halesi Tuwachung Municipality and Wards 12 and 14 of Gurbhakot Municipality. These hubs were formed in the presence of the research team, social mobilizers, municipal staff, and ward chairpersons. Each MSAKH comprises diverse stakeholders, including farmers, agro-entrepreneurs, local elected representatives and officials, financial institutions, community-based organizations (CBOs), and the private sector.
title: Inclusive multi-stakeholder knowledge sharing platform on mixed farming system for farmers, and relevant stakeholders in Halesi Tuwachung Municipality, Khotang district and Gurbhakot Municipality, Surkhet district to support farmers.

description: Rift Valley fever (RVF) is a zoonotic disease caused by a virus that is transmitted by a wide range of mosquitoes. The disease mainly affects livestock and people. It has been listed by the World Health Organization as one of the nine diseases that has the potential to cause pandemics. Decision makers often face major challenges predicting and responding to outbreaks, and so we have developed this prototype tool for forecasting risk and identifying actions that can be taken to manage the risk. The tool has two components, the first ingests rainfall forecasts from the Global Precipitation Climatology Centre and processes anomalies to identify periods when above normal rainfall is expected. The second component provides actions that need to be taken at various phases of the outbreak ranging from pre-outreak, outbreak, post-outbreak and peacetime periods.
title: A web-based based decision support tool for managing Rift Valley fever outbreaks in Kenya

description: As most agricultural farmers especially women get older, their responsibilities increase and their patience with longs hours of face to face meetings and trainings becomes a problem. Farmers are showing interest in receiving information from the value chain through animations and visual presentations. They prefer listening to an animation of three to five minutes and having a discussion to fill any needed gaps. This way they have more time to attend to other productive or household activities. Also using animation has increased the reach of information and technologies to farmers (where to source seed, varieties to plant, preparation of land, post harvest losses, nutrition and multistakeholder platforms) through social media channels like Whatsapp.

description: We have co-developed and co-designed a dashboard with an interactive map that dynamically displays the global distribution of socio-economic datasets, data, and tools that facilitate bundling in different local, regional, and thematic contexts. Gender and socioeconomic studies from the CGIAR Gender Impact Platform were used to compile the existing STIBs, and more data from learning labs in Kenya, Ethiopia, and India will be added subsequently. Additional socio-economic and gender inventory data has been extracted from FAO’s Agricultural Innovation Systems and the World Bank, but not clustered into different bundles. Out of the 5504 datasets currently housed in the dashboard, 450 have been assessed for their alignment with EMPOWER work package definition of STIBs. The remaining 5054 datasets are inventory data. The inventory data contains 151 from the Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS), 1314 from FAO’s Agricultural Innovation Systems (AIS), and 3589 from the World Bank’s Agriculture Data.

description: Digital innovations are increasingly being utilized in food, land, and water systems. It's crucial that these innovations are inclusive and cause no harm, especially for less developed countries where many people rely on food systems for their livelihoods. However, there is a lack of standard metrics and guidelines for measuring and promoting digital inclusivity. To address this gap, the Multidimensional Digital Inclusivity Index (MDII) has been developed. The MDII offers 22 indicators of digital inclusivity across five dimensions. It can be used to assess and promote the level of digital inclusivity of an innovation, an innovation bundle, an organization, or a country. This index aims to make digital innovations accessible, usable, beneficial, participatory, and safe for socially and economically marginalized groups in food systems.
title: MDII: A multidimensional index designed to promote ethical and socially inclusive digital innovation processes within food, land, and water systems

description: The potato production through zero-tillage with straw mulch (PZTM) is an innovative technique to sustainably intensify agricultural production with potato uses few inputs and residues from the previous crop without disturbing the soil. It has the potential to address issues being exacerbated by climate change like excessive input use leading to detrimental environmental effects, water scarcity, and worsening air quality due to rice straw burning and, as such, significantly contribute to a sustainable agroecological transformation in Bangladesh. Key to this practice is the efficiency principle, by increasing resource-use efficiencies of major inputs. It recycles straw as mulch, creating value for a residue that would have been burned otherwise. As this technique is associated with economic gains as well as women’s empowerment, it improves rural livelihoods and promotes gender equity, and as such adheres to the principle of human and social values.
title: Production of saline tolerant potato variety under zero tillage using rice straws during the fallow winter season for farmers in rice-based ecosystems in Bangladesh

description: Nomadic livestock systems have evolved over millennia in response to seasonal rainfall patterns. In Tunisia, where approximately one-third of the land is semi-arid, arid, or desert, degradation poses a significant challenge. The Gdel resting technique, a low-cost intervention, has been part of the national strategy for rangeland improvement since 1990, and is implemented by developing agencies for rangeland improvement. The pastoralists whose animals would normally graze in these areas are supported through the provision of feed supplements for 3 consecutive years. However, the implementation had its shortfalls. In 2018, unexpectedly high rainfall led to abundant vegetation growth, but the rigid implementation of the resting technique hindered pastoralists from capitalizing on the surplus biomass. In response, ICARDA developed flexible or opportunistic grazing criteria and trained partners to adapt to climate variability. This innovative approach allows pastoralists to optimize resource utilization during favorable years and addressing the shortcomings of previous implementations.
title: Restoring rangelands: the art of flexible livestock grazing to restore soil health, ecosystem function and ecosystem services

description: In Ruzizi plain of DRC, research activities on the integration of Brachiarea into maize-based system to mitigate the the major agricultural constrains in the region (animal feed lack, soil fertility depletion and climate change) are ongoing. So far, the most performing Brachiarea varieties were identified, maize and Brachiarea productivity, carbon incorporation into the soil and soil coverage when Brachiarea is integrated into the system were assessed. The feasibility and productivity of maize resowed in Brachiarea plot established during the last cropping season were evaluated. The feasibility and productivity of replicating Brachiarea suckers to overcome the issue of no seed availability and high cost were assessed and farmers’ impression and opinions on Brachiarea-maize intercropping system were received and integrated in next step of the technology development. During last season, we carried out experiment and identified the best and cost-efficient way to control weeds at early growth stage, in the Brachiarea field.
title: Brachiarea integration into maize-based cropping system for smallholder farmers multi-benefit, resilient and climate smart agriculture

description: The agro-climatic bulletin (ACB) is an agro-advisory tool and system based on a seasonal, monthly, and 10-day weather forecast that aims to provide climate advisory services to local agricultural insitutions, officials, and farmers in Vietnam. It is being co-developed and delivered through the public systems in Vietnam where sub-national offices are integrating the tool on their local agricultural development planning and decision-making. ACBs in Vietnam now has reached more than 200,000 and received funding from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) in 2024 and 2025 to implement and scale its operations in 13 Mekong River Delta provinces.

description: Good quality feed year-round is limiting livestock productivity on-farm and resource use in farms of small to medium size. Feed production can amount to 50 to 70% of livestock production costs. Forages are a means to overcome the feed gap, and resilient forages responding to different abiotic and biotic stresses, including low soil fertility, drought / excess water, pest diseases, are essential, increasing livestock productivity by up to 15%. To scale such technologies, suitable entry points i.e., market-oriented livestock production particularly dairy are required. Enablers are animal generics and health technologies which capitalize on the improved feeding as well as capacity and dissemination channels such as cooperatives and functional seed supply systems. We are using a diversity of advanced forages which have a good availability of seed and/or planting material and demand pull through livestock production in Kenya; at the same time a pipeline for improved forages is being maintained.
title: Novel stress tolerant (abiotic and biotic), highly productive and resource efficient forages to drive livestock production and productivity for market oriented small and medium, size farm operations.

description:
It is important to understand how and why antibiotics are used. Usage of such can be categorized into three key areas:_x000D_
    Knowledge: This involves assessing what veterinarians, farmers, and other stakeholders know about antibiotics and how resistance develops._x000D_
    Attitudes: Understanding the attitudes of individuals within the target population towards antibiotic use._x000D_
    Practices: Examining how antibiotics are prescribed and used in practice._x000D_
Collecting this information can be accomplished through Knowledge, Attitude and Practice surveys. While many studies use the Knowledge, Attitude and Practice surveys, they often fail to collect data comprehensively or use unvalidated instruments. To address these shortcomings, we aim to develop a Knowledge Attitude Practice survey, tailored for small-holder dairy farmers and veterinarians in Kenya. The project also explores the application of Item Response Theory (IRT) modeling in evaluating measurement scales.
title: Development and Application of a Quantitative Tool for Measuring Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Animal Health Professionals

In the status quo, eligible farmers receive an input loan via our implementing partner. Agricultural inputs, however, are not the only inputs required for the production of agricultural products. Labor, land, and other forms of capital must combine with agricultural inputs.

description: The Rice Crop Manager Advisory Service (RCMAS) Climate+ generates climate-adjusted nutrient and crop recommendations to address dynamic weather conditions and potential climate-related risks during the cropping season. It is a link between the RCMAS platform, https://rcm.da.gov.ph/, and the Agro-climatic Advisory Portal (ACAP), https://amia-cis.github.io via applications programming interface (API). The RCMAS uses the 6-month seasonal and 10-day weather forecasts from the ACAP to formulate agro-advisories aiming to reduce crop loss due to climate risks such as floods and drought. RCMAS Climate+ upgrades the existing RCMAS platform with pre-season and mid-season climate-related recommendations, such as adjustments to the date of sowing, fertilizer application timing in response to floods or droughts during the crop growth period and (2) real-time or near-real-time climate information dissemination to farmers, which could enable better decision-making under dynamic climate conditions. The agro-advisories are provided to farmers through the one-page printout and/or SMS.

description: A package combining gender accommodative and transformative approaches to deliver improved chickens, animal services and markets to women farmers by women veterinarians. Gender accommodative approaches were adopted to enhance the business and chicken management skills of the women vets. Gender transformative approaches (in this case social media) were adopted to address gender norms that make women’s involvement in chicken business socially inappropriate. Restrictive gender norms are considered the root cause of gender-based disadvantage; unlike gender accommodative approaches, gender transformative approaches aim to change such restrictive norms for lasting social change.

description: Point of Cow is a disposable chip manufactured by Fluimedix (Denmark).  It is a compact and user-friendly diagnostic tool that serves as a crucial component in antibiotic treatment decision making. The chip is engineered to detect both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria within 4-24hrs,  enabling quick decision-making on whether to use antibiotic treatment for mastitis. Point of Cow is primarily designed for dairy farmers, but can also be used by milk processors and quality control professionals in the dairy industry. It is a valuable tool for anyone involved in milk production and processing.
title: Testing Point of Cow, a penside diagnostic test, for treatment decision making in mastitis

description: CIAT started an interspecific breeding program with Urochloa brizantha (CIAT-6294 cv. Marandú), Urochloa decumbens (CIAT-0606, cv. Basilisk), and Urochloa ruziziensis (BR4X-44-2) in 1987 (Rao et al. 1998; Miles et al. 1995), and since then delivered numerous Urochloa hybrid lines to the private forage seed sector for further selection and commercialization. This has led to the release of the first Urochloa hybrid ever in 2001 in Mexico by Grupo Papalotla and to several subsequent hybrid releases thereafter. Today, 6 different Urochloa hybrids are being commercialized in around 70 countries globally, mainly among cattle farmers, leading to increased animal productivity, livelihood benefits, and positive environmental externalities.

description: The innovation described here is a crowd-sourced information clearinghouse, similar to trustpilot.com or yelp.com, to help smallholders secure quality inputs and services such as improved varieties and agronomic recommendations. Farmers use the clearinghouse to rate agro-input dealers as well as the products and services they offer; these ratings are then used to rank the dealers, with the ranking made available to both farmers and dealers in an appealing and marketable manner. A recent randomized trial of a prototype clearinghouse conducted with 350 dealers and 3500 farmers in 11 districts in Uganda found significant positive impacts on input use, enabling farmers to grow more food on less land, and indirect impacts on climate resilience and the environment. Dealers also received more customers, sold more, and earned higher revenues, although there are gender biases observed in the ratings for women dealers that can remedied through a more gender-intentional design at scale-up.
title: Scaling up an information clearinghouse to accelerate agricultural technology adoption in Uganda

description: Ethiopia hosts over 916,000 refugees and asylum seekers , in addition to over four million IDPs . In many situations, this increases pressure on natural resources due to additional demands for food, water, and other natural resources. description: In Son La province, north-west Vietnam, a tailored training package has been introduced for smallholder farmers and animal health professionals under the Li Chan project (CRP Livestock). In Sustainable Animal Productivity (SAPLING) we've adapted and enhanced these materials to better address the needs of the Son La community.  This innovation emphasizes animal health biosecurity and recent advancements in animal health. For the farmers, the training package includes a detailed training guideline, complemented by training materials, focusing on three key pillars: biosecurity, animal health, and animal welfare. Animal health professional training package is more specialized for those who already have basic knowledge of animal health, which covers biosecurity, animal diseases, vaccines and drugs, and outbreak control. Through this training material, our goal is to strengthen animal health and productivity in the targeted area. The innovation is already being adapted for a Mobile application (app.) in a bilateral project

description: Transforming Agrifood Systems in South Asia (TAFSSA) with the Linkage of Cereal Systems Initiative for South Asia (CSISA)  has started to work on increasing crop diversification by increasing crop intensification and through integrated market systems development. description: The call for establishing the Tropical Poultry Platform (TROP) has emanated from the need to address the critical bottlenecks constraining the efficient and effective operation of poultry value chains in the tropics. SAPLING will identify key actors and catalyse TROP’s creation. Working alongside national, regional, and private sector partners, we will engage and collaborate with partners, exploiting synergies and complementarities and ensuring alignment and harmonization of actions with like-minded institutions. Key private sector players in the poultry industry, investors, farmers’ groups/associations, civil society organizations and non-governmental organizations. TROP will be established as a membership-based organization that would mobilize resources both from within its members as well as from potential outside financiers.

description: In the Northwest Highlands of Vietnam, cattle and pigs are characterized by low productivity and mainly fed with low quality forages, crop residues and food waste. Feed and forage quality is generally of low quality resulting in low livestock output. Assessments conducted in the region have identified the main feed-related challenges including winter feed shortage, poor diets, and low yield of available forages. Farmers also have limited knowledge on suitable forage types and management, feed processing and preservation, which greatly affects livestock productivity. Gender-responsive feed intervention strategies that can address these context-specific challenges, mainly winter feed shortage, can greatly improve livestock productivity and efficiency. Such interventions include capacity building of women and men farmers, extension & vet staff on utilization of locally available feed resources and purchased feeds, feed conservation, diet formulation, and feeding regimes, and promoting improved forage varieties (establishment, management, and utilization), for cattle and pigs.
title: Feeding strategies based on locally available feeds, preferred improved forages and associated farmer-friendly training materials targeting women and men cattle and pig producers

description: PigSMART platform delivers digital extension messages to pig farmers. It covers an integrated content that is delivered to pig farmers based on the stage of growth of the pigs. The messages include best practices in feeding, herd health management, breeding and genetics, manure management and heat stress management. The process of integrating and adapting the content followed key steps: (i) curation of research outputs on feeds, health, genetics, and heat stress, (ii) drawing messages from the research outputs, (iii) validating messages from the researchers and government extension  to ensure integrity of content, (iv) integrating messages premised on the different stages of pig growth, and (v) developing audio skits from integrated content in Luganda. A brochure on the integrated content was developed and disseminated to pig farmers in addition to the audio skits. The messages can be used by extension agents to train farmers on best practices in pig production.

description: Using a farmer field school approach, four model farms were set up by renovating existing housing units through ILRI-farmer co-funding arrangement. The model farms were renovated to showcase integrated technology innovations (herd health package): improved housing, health, welfare, piglet care, biosecurity measures, improved feeds and genetics. This is expected to spur adoption of the integrated innovation elements, which improve health, survival, growth rates and productivity.

description: In Uganda smallholder pig systems, the pig keepers usually do not have access to weigh-scale to obtain accurate pig weights. Knowledge of weight is important for both pig management decisions (such as determining drug dosage) and for determining sale price (which is based on estimated liveweight or carcass weight derived from this). To overcome this, a pig weigh-band was developed. A weigh-band is similar to a tape-measure, however it shows weight estimates of the pigs based on their heart-girth. The equation to predict weight from heart-girth was developed from a study on 764 pigs of different ages, sex, and breed types, from 157 smallholder pig keeping households in Central and Western Uganda (see Marshall et al., 2023). The weigh-bands and an associated training manual have now been produced, and are undergoing a pilot with women and men pig keepers in Uganda.

description: The Farmer Interface App FIA (FIA–niébé) developed to scout for Fall Armyworm (FAW) and cowpea pod bug (Clavigralla tomentosicollis). The FIA–niébé was demonstrated to farmers, extension agents, and researchers during several training sessions in Benin and Mali. Scouting for FAW eggs and neonates is difficult and time consuming. To optimize scouting intervals, it was hypothesizing that the optimum timeframe for the FAW female arriving to lay eggs in sown maize fields could be predicted. This was done by back-calculating from interval censored data of egg and neonates collected in emerging maize seedlings. Early time of ovipositing FAW after sowing was recorded in field experiments. Using temperature based phenological models it was estimated that about 210 accumulated degree days is needed for early detection of neonate larvae in the field. This work is meant to provide new insights on timely pest detection and to guide precise timing of control measures.
title: Farmer Interface Application (FIA) validated and operational for Fall Armyworm and cowpea pod borers and pod sucking bugs

description: Agronomic gain key performance indicators (KPIs) are designed to monitor, evaluate and measure the impact of changes in agronomic practices in the CGIAR Excellence in Agronomy initiative (EiA). description: Self-sovereign identity (SSI) is a digital identity that is fully controlled and owned by the individual it represents. Unlike traditional centralized identity systems, SSI allows individuals to have autonomy over their own identity, what information is shared, with whom, and for what purposes. SSI is a relatively new concept, but we argue it has the potential to revolutionize how we manage identity and privacy in digital ecosystems. To explore the potential of SSI in smallholder farmers' data sharing and management, we partnered with Bluenumber Foundation to develop a data traceability pilot in Mexico for small-scale maize producers to manage their farm management data. We expect SSI can also help producers securely access financial and other services more easily through the certified digital identity.
title: Digital Identities: Enabling farming data traceability using open data sharing protocols with self-sovereign identity in Mexico to allow individuals' control on their identity and shared information

description: Searching for a simple road map to explain Genetic Innovation initiative linkages resulted in the creation of a two-dimensional process-based Theory of Change (2D-ToC). The 2D-ToC distinguishes between the main trust of a program or project, and capabilities that need to be developed or improved to achieve the main trust. In the case of Genetic Innovation, the ontological analysis has become the foundation for practically aligning initiatives and bilateral projects through a Program Management Platform. During 2024, the approach was expanded using business analytical approaches to conceptualize the entire CGIAR portfolio along the two pathways of value creation, impact or benefit generation and development or organizational effectiveness. This was done for both the 2022-2024 portfolio and the 2025-2030 portfolio. It was shown that portfolio analytics can be used to conceptualize the total CGIAR research agenda and identify Key Performance Indicators, that could be utilized across a hugely diverse research agenda.

description: A production hub is a system comprised by different actors in an agri-food chain of an agro-ecological region who work together to promote sustainable agriculture. The FRESH initiative will implement the hub model for testing, validating, and scaling-out proven technologies for a greater impact in each of its focus countries, in more than one geographic location (production zone) in each country. FRESH researchers will develop and cater research products and services to promote efficient use of resources and adoption of safe and sustainable vegetable production practices. Hub implementation involves three stages: (i) establishing physical components (platforms, demonstration and extension areas); (ii) training extension agents, private sector, and farmers; and (iii) creating, promoting and strengthening local innovation systems. Actors contributing to the success operationalization of these hubs include NARES, members of relevant government ministries, farmer cooperatives and small holder farmers, the private sector, and FRESH researchers and research partners.

description: Aphids and pod borers are key yield limiting factors on temperate food legumes like faba bean, lentil and chickpea. Besides direct economic damage, aphids are vectors of devastating plant viruses. Not much progress has been made to develop aphid-resistant crop varieties due to low levels of resistance available in the gene pools. Farmers in North Africa, South Asia and East Africa use synthetic insecticides to mange aphids and pod borers. This increases cost of production to smallholder farmers and also health risk during applications. Laboratory and field trials of essential oils extracted from indigenous plants and entomopathogenic fungi strains showed promising results to control aphids and pod borers. The innovation will be used to develop biorational pest management innovations that will significantly reduce pesticide applications.

description: An advancement in 2024 was a study to understand the challenges in production and supply of early generation seed by evaluating the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of three rapid multiplication techniques: rooted apical cuttings (RAC), aeroponics and sand-hydroponics. Results show significant differences in multiplication rates among cultivars across the three techniques and with no major interaction observed between cultivar maturity type and the multiplication technique used. None of the variations of the multiplication rates among cultivars resulted in a preference of another multiplication technology because of the cultivar. Analysis of the cost of set-up and operation of the multiplication facilities shows aeroponics as the most expensive technique to implement, followed by ARC and sand hydroponics.
title: Apical Rooted Cuttings - cost-effective method for potato seed production in Subsaharan Africa

This innovation aims to map the potential for the introduction of aquaculture in small reservoirs using geospatial analysis in northern Ghana. description: Private (small- and medium-scale) seed potato businesses in Sub-Sahara Africa have challenges in the planning of their production and its related factors (screenhouse capacity, labor, land, cash flow, storage capacity, …) leading to premature sales of seed potato due to lack of suitable land available for further multiplication or unsold stock of starter material, among others. Therefore, this seed potato production planning and business decision tool aims to support them to improve their production planning and its related factors while showing the profitability of their planned production schemes.  The development of a user-friendly online and smartphone application is foreseen. Moreover, this tool shows the business opportunities for small- and medium-scale seed businesses in Uganda and Kenya, but it can be used in other countries as well because the identified challenges cut across many countries.

description: Parasitic weeds are major biotic constraints on food legumes and causing a decline in area and productivity in North and East Africa. The level of resistance in released varieties is low and requires additional management options to effectively reduce the economic impacts parasitic weeds. Hashengie + two sprays of sublethal doses of glyphosate at early flowering stages of the crop. The innovation reduced parasitic weeds population and doubled crop productivity. Hashengie  will be used next season.

description: Maintaining inter-varietal crop diversity, created through evolutionary plant breeding (EPB), on farms is proven to improve farmers productivity, resilience to climate change and enhance dietary diversity. We have tested evolutionary populations created through Evolutionary Plant Breeding in Ethiopia, Bhutan, Iran, Jordan, Nepal and Uganda for four crops: Barley, beans, wheat and rice and identified superior performing populations under different farming systems. Integration of evolutionary plant breeding to Sustainable Intensification of Mixed farming System (SI-MFS) in target countries is important to sustain crop production sector of target farming systems. At least one composite or mixture population is developed for each country targeted by the SI-MFS initiative.
title: Dynamic evolutionary populations of productivity of mixtures of different of barley in Ethiopian Highlands

The initiative and CSISA-MEA worked to boost the same of crucial farm machinery 924 spare parts needed for intensification and diversification. These were mainly for irrigation pumps, threshers, fodder choppers, drive belt wheels, and engine liners and the sales were worth USD18,827. description: Premium quality rice market linkages to specialized millers to enhance profits for smallholder farmers and small businesses in Northern Bangladesh. During the reporting period, Cereal Systems Initiative in South Asia (CSISA) in alignment with Transforming Agrifood Systems in South Asia (TAFSSA) and eight seed companies in Bangladesh produced and sold around 400 tons of Premium Quality Rice (PQR) seeds in the CSISA working areas. Data collected from the Department of Agricultural Extension in 16 districts indicated that PQR varieties were cultivated in 79 of their 107 upazilas and that a total of 934,196 farmers cultivated PQR on 215,145 hectares of land. The research team worked with 12 seed companies in nine districts. 695.35 tons of PQR seed were sold in these nine districts. 115,892 farmers (at an average of five farmers per hectare), and 23,178 hectares of land were involved in these markets.
title: Farmers diversify rice variety production and enter markets with premium quality rice (PRQ) varieties
