description: Work Package 3 (Behavioral Intelligence) is testing two innovations to address behavioral barriers to adopting new varieties across 6 different experiments. One intervention is the provision of free trial packs of seeds, which helps farmers overcome aversion to risky experimentation with new varieties. The trial pack is only meant to cover a portion of a farmer's agricultural land, but large enough for farmers to learn and experiment with how the variety works. The second intervention is a cooking demonstration and free sample of the "end product" (such as flour). This is meant to help farmers overcome risks of experimentation with varieties that they may not want to consume and misperceptions that improved varieties do not taste good.  We also test site-specific interventions, including crop insurance in Kenya and Ethiopia, agricultural advisories in Nigeria and Kenya, leveraging endowment effects and nudging in Uganda, and social distance with champion farmers in India.
title: Demand-side innovations to accelerate varietal turnover (such as seed trial packs, cooking demonstrations, consumer trial packs, crop insurance, agricultural advisories, leveraging endowment effects, nudging, social distance)

description: This comprehensive tilapia biosecurity manual is an integral component of the initiative to establish a robust GIFT breeding population in partnership with the largest tilapia breeder and producer in Nigeria to disseminate fry and fingerlings for hatchery production and grow-out across Nigeria. These manuals provide crucial guidelines and protocols for ensuring the health and biosecurity of tilapia hatchery and grow out operations. It is expected to provide instrumental in guiding fish farmers across Nigeria to protect their stocks from diseases. This, in turn, will enhance yields and ensure the long-term success of their aquaculture endeavors.

description: e-Agrology Central America is a data collection system for agriculture that allows capturing detailed agronomic data from farmers' plots and research trials. It collects approximately 500 variables including agronomic practices, costs, yield, field visits, polygons, postharvest and commercialization. It works both in web and mobile applications and it is ready to be used in the region including specific catalogues of crops, seeds, products, political divisions, ethnic groups and agronomic cycles.  Customizations were also made to the currency configuration and a conversion tool was built-in to convert local to universal units of measure such as cuerdas, squares, tasks, pounds, and quintals. Additionally, it has a Project Management module, specifically developed for AgriLAC which allows to register Innovations, Training and Knowledge products.

description:
A multiplier population of generation 11 (G11) of genetically improved farmed tilapia (GIFT) selected for rapid growth was produced in India in collaboration with the Rajiv Gandhi Center for Aquaculture (RGCA). The full-sibling families of G11 are the progeny of Generation 10 parents selected for rapid growth and genetic diversity. These fish are expected to grow faster than unimproved base-population animals and will help increase fish production in India._x000D_
Genetically superior candidate parents from Generation 11 were selected and mated to produce G12 families in 2024.  G12 fish were grown out in a common garden experiment and measured in Dec 2024.

description: DataScribe enables users to collaboratively create agronomic surveys or upload ODK questionnaires (as xls forms), share them (or particular questions within them), and easily specify variables aligned with data standards (via the tool's semantic engine). Users upload their forms to ODK to collect data. The tool also standardizes surveys by enabling questionnaires to draw from the same global choice lists (over 50 currently available, for such topics as "inorganic N fertilizer"; "weeding" and more). Questionnaire blocks can be saved and shared or reused, saving time and enabling further standardization across surveys. The tool was developed in 2022 but has been improved in 2023 and used by several EiA Use Cases.
title: DataScribe - a tool for creating standards-compliant, shareable agronomic survey questionnaires

description:
In Ghana’s North-East Region, an innovative aquaculture pilot initiative is transforming local communities by creating new livelihood opportunities. The completion of the first cycle of the aquaculture pilot marks a significant milestone for the participating communities.  2024 saw the completion of the harvest for the first cycle of production of fish in the reservoirs of four communities in Northern Ghana(Langbinsi, Nalerigu, Nansoni, and Tombu). The second cycle of production is now on-going and was partly financed from the earnings from the first round._x000D_
The success of the pilot has caught the attention of various stakeholders, including the Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture Development, which is now planning to expand the initiative across all 5 regions of Northern Ghana. _x000D_
The introduction of aquaculture is turning local dams into sources of growth and development. By utilizing aquaculture, the initiative not only boosts economic prospects but also fosters community resilience and pride.

description: Stakeholders in the aquatic food systems make suboptimal decisions due to the lack of quality accessible data and information. Data gaps and needs vary within stakeholder groups, time, and geographies. The current challenge consists in understanding what is the real demand for data for stakeholders in different countries. It is a methodology, based on multi-stakeholder consultation and analysis of data available from different sources, developed to identify data gaps and needs of different stakeholder groups in different countries of interest.
title: Methodology for analyzing data gaps and needs was developed to identify and remove limitations in data and information that hinder the development of aquatic food systems.

description:
The innovation develops common germplasm licensing approaches for use by CGIAR centers under One CGIAR. It is being developed by an inter-initiative work group – including Seed Equal, Genebanks and Accelerated Breeding - for review, discussion and endorsement by Centers and the System Management Board.  _x000D_
_x000D_
At this stage, few centers have systematic germplasm licensing approaches in place, approaches differ between centers, and there is a lack of awareness among public and private sector entities how to access CGIAR Center germplasm for research, breeding or commercial use. The innovation seeks to implement more streamlined approaches and conditions to foster wide and equitable use of Center germplasm by public and private entities under One CGIAR. These approaches need to be aligned with International Treaty obligations, Article 15 commitments, and the CGIAR Principles on the Management of Intellectual Assets._x000D_
_x000D_
In 2024, a new draft version of the licensing strategy for One CGIAR was prepared.

description:
The unreported nature of many small-scale fisheries means they have insufficient data to conduct assessments of fish stock health, a prerequisite for certification as sustainable fisheries. It also often causes them to be automatically characterised as illegal, due to the term "IUU fishing" - Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated fishing.    _x000D_
This innovation is a novel approach to pilot a LBB (Length-based Bayesian Biomass) analysis of important targeted species in Timor-Leste into the fisheries monitoring and automated analytics system workflow.

description: Based on information and services currently available in the region and the requirements expressed by stakeholders such as LIMCOM, we are developing a seasonal forecast of droughts for the Limpopo River basin in Southern Africa. This system is based on state-of-the-art data processing and machine learning tools currently developed by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) for the generation of seasonal temperature and precipitation forecasts at global scales. The innovation seeks to adapt this system for the forecasting of drought events and intensity over the Limpopo River basin using indices selected according to their suitability to describe droughts locally, which is carried out using satellite and climate information. The forecast system will be embedded in the Digital Twin platform developed by CGIAR Research Initiative on Digital Innovation to assess the potential impacts of seasonal climate anomalies on agricultural and hydrological systems.
title: Actionable drought forecasts for the transboundary natural resource management authorities in Southern Africa using satellite-based climate information

description: The increasing capabilities of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-augmented data analytics present significant opportunities for agricultural extension organizations operating in the Global South. In this work, we developed a proof-of-concept audio analytics tool to demonstrate the possibility of automating the process of translating and analyzing farmers' voice message data collected by Farm Radio Rural radio programs. This innovation, Tambaya ("Ask" in Hausa) draws on several cutting-edge AI tools, in particular, the use of unsupervised learning to generate language models, to expand the number of languages available to the user. In the context of NGOs working with African (Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria) radio stations, Tambaya will allow them to quickly analyze farmers' voice messages, understand farmers' needs, and draw insights to deliver targeted extension services.
title: Longa: An Artificial Intelligence-based audio analytics tool for identifying farmers' need and targeting digital extension services

description:
The lack of robust and coherent data on aquatic food systems is a major barrier to realizing their potential for sustainable development and public health. Limited data (or access to it) hinders informed policy and investment decisions, leading to undervaluation and underinvestment in the sector by public and private stakeholders._x000D_
The data-to-action portal addresses this gap by providing a unified platform where researchers, policymakers, investors, and other stakeholders can access data, evidence, and stories of impact related to aquatic foods. It also enables collaborators and scientists to contribute new datasets and insights, fostering a dynamic and evolving resource._x000D_
An AI-driven storytelling model is under development to further enhance the portal’s capabilities. This model will transform research data into compelling narratives, making complex insights accessible and actionable, supporting decision-making, and driving greater engagement across sectors.

description: In 2022, IFPRI and ANAPRI (formerly ReNAPRI) collaborated to establish the Modeling Service Center (MSC) at ANAPRI's Secretariat in Lusaka, Zambia. IFPRI conceptualized the modeling community of practice (MODCOP), which evolved into the MSC, and shaped the Policy Prioritization through Value Chain (PPVC) Analysis II proposal funded by BMGF. The MSC focuses on training researchers in economywide analysis, including food policy modeling and climate impact assessments. In 2023, it conducted four training events for ANAPRI partners, offering tiered programs for ambassadors, affiliates, and fellows. By 2024, the MSC became independently operational and self-funded, with ANAPRI fully embracing the model. IFPRI continues to provide advisory support and capacity building to strengthen MSC activities.

description: This is an update on the draft standards developed to define the novel inclusive process of building Target Product Profiles (TPPs) for crop-breeding to deliver improved varieties more efficiently with higher rates of adoption. This provides an end-to-end description of the process and steps required to develop a gender inclusive target product for each market segment identified at the CGIAR Sub region and NARES level. It also defines the key terms in a TPP and describes the relationship between a seed product market segment and a TPP. The draft standard also explains and defines the membership, roles and key responsibilities of the multi-disciplinary team required to develop a gender inclusive TPP and lastly, list all process owners and key contacts. This is used in the Product Development Team meetings.

description: e-Agrology is a high-frequency monitoring system for agricultural production in the global South. This open-source solution for web and mobile includes a data collection module adapted for any crop and production system (perennials, seasonal, intercrops); a transformation module for automated data cleaning and standardization; and a visualization module for dashboard creation and data download. It allows monitoring of production systems, including detailed data on planting dates, pest and disease management, agronomic practices, costs, yield, input prices, commercialization, and post-harvest. The system has supported CGIAR private sector partners in measuring their sustainability within agri-food systems; also, we have generated site-specific recommendations for farmers based on optimal planting dates, nutrient management, best practices, and yield limiting factors per agroecology. By December 2022, more than 250,000 farmers are registered with 350,000 agronomic seasonal logbooks. Sustainability indicators have been measured for including water-use efficiency, nutrient-use efficiency, CO2 emissions, profitability, yield, and others.

description: The 'GANSO Guarantee' is a voluntary evaluation tool for livestock producers. It was developed by the GANSO (GANadería SOstenible / Sustainable Livestock) organization, co-founded by the Alliance BI-CIAT, created to improve the livestock production systems in the Colombian Eastern Plains, from extensive degraded pastures and soils to productive and sustainable landscapes.  The guarantee has grown and developed as a set of 5 pillars (environment, people, animal welfare, management & meat quality) and 52 practices are independently assessed and categorized in order of their compliance level. This gives the farmers incentives to sell beef at a premium price, supported by the consumers' willingness to pay for environmental-friendly products. These products are currently available in one the largest retail store in Colombia, with 182 stores in 6 cities. Starting in Meta department, now the tool is being implemented in other departments of the Orinoquia region.

description: The Climate Security Observatory (CSO) is an online dashboard targeting policy and decision makers, development and humanitarian practitioners and advisors to help them with targeting, programming and prioritization of investments particularly in areas under climate stress. The CSO uses a mixed method approach to give answers to four lead questions: Where are the most vulnerable areas to climate-related insecurities and risks? Who are the groups vulnerable to climate and security risks that should be targeted? How does climate exacerbate the causes of conflict? What needs to be done to break the vicious cycle between climate and conflict? The CSO brings together robust, localized and contextualized and policy-relevant evidence on the climate-security nexus. It includes a dashboard on climate security programming for climate finance, the climate security sensitivity tool, climate security mapping and an interactive dashboard for climate security dialogues.

description: The Farmer-to-Farmer Scaling Networks is a farmer-led innovation connecting farmers to each other for information exchange and capacity building, and ultimately the scaling of climate adaptation technologies and innovations that have been developed by the farmers themselves. The pioneers of adaptation are farmers who have developed their adaptation practices with their own endogenous innovations beyond piloting stage. We support them in developing a farm-level adapted scaling approach complementary to existing institutions, involving pioneers themselves as the main actors in the scaling process. Together with the pioneers we study their practices, and then progressively include more farmers, farmer groups, cooperatives in a knowledge exchange through participatory field days where pioneers share and discuss the findings of this data collection on their practices. Gradually, we develop a Farmer2Farmer knowledge network that connects pioneers and their learning groups with research, extension, development organisations, and private sector actors.

description: The multidisciplinary working group (MWG) serves as a pivotal and inclusive platform dedicated to advancing the production of climate services, their interpretation into actionable decisions, and widespread dissemination. This is an innovative approach to establsihing multi-stakeholder platforms to enhance the uptake of weather and climate information services. The national MWG comprises key departments and institutions, fostering collaboration and comprehensive representation. At the local level, 32 MWGs, led by district Prefects, address region-specific challenges through decentralized structures to ensure that MWGs are well-connected with local realities and can effectively address region-specific challenges. Regular collaboration is maintained through tri-monthly meetings where members from both national and local MWGs convene. These meetings cover a spectrum of pertinent topics, including meteorology, hydrology, agriculture, livestock, environment, and market dynamics. The collective insights garnered from these discussions are distilled into recommendations, consolidated in a bulletin. To ensure widespread awareness, these recommendations are disseminated through community radios.

description: The water storage diagnostic is an approach to integrating assessments of different storage types, such as aquifers, soil moisture, and dams. The diagnostic framework supports planning and management decisions across these water storage types by identifying and comparing their relative opportunities and risks. Methods for evaluating individual storage options include recession flow analysis and hydrogeological modelling (for aquifers); analysis of earth observation data (for dams); and analysis of in-situ and remotely sensed or modelled data (for soil moisture). Planning and management across (rather than within) storage types enable the identification of complementary roles for alternative storage options and the design of a diversified path to storage development, which brings a suite of benefits including greater WEFE benefits to water-using communities. The results of diagnostics have now been used by River Basin Organizations and basin managers

description:
AGROTUTOR, a decision-making framework for smallholder farmers in Mexico, Peru and Colombia, prioritizes practicality and actionable information. Unlike offering unique recommendations per plot, it provides scenarios, benchmarks, and tools empowering farmers to make informed, tailored choices. Operating on a circular knowledge approach, it collects farmer data and feedback, enhancing advisory services. _x000D_
AGROTUTOR's flexible architecture integrates information from diverse sources, allowing farmers to compare results from different models and data sources. Its strength lies in geo-localized data, using AI models for crop-specific optimization, weather updates, pest identification, and agronomic recommendations. Historical training data spanning a decade helps to identify limiting factors, provide insightful comparisons among soil and climate clusters. The data wallet feature and digital identity ensure farmers' data rights and introduce a compensation model, treating their data as an asset. With modular and online/offline functionality, AGROTUTOR also fosters peer-to-peer knowledge sharing through WhatsApp community groups.
title: User interface of e-Agrology directed to farmers as a one stop shop where farmers can consult localized decision support for the management of their fields

description: The innovation uses the site suitability mapping for implementing the Aquifer Storage and Recovery (ASR) method called Bhungroo Irrigation Technology (BIT) and solar irrigation pumping to smallholder irrigation schemes that use groundwater and surface water in the Inkomanti-Usuthu Catchment Management Area in South Africa. The ASR /BIT uses one borehole to recharge the aquifer during the wet season and abstract water from the same borehole during the dry season. This resulted in increased irrigation water availability and reduced energy use from grid electricity and fuel pumps, thereby increasing farm profit. Energy use for irrigation contributed 50-70% of the total farming expenses. Successful implementation of the BIT and solar irrigation pumping at a site requires the delineation of suitable areas based on scientific, natural parameters and expert judgment.
title: Conjunctive use of groundwater and surface water with solar irrigation pumping to enhance irrigation water availability and productivity, food and water security for smallholder farmers in dry areas

description: Intercropping is a system based on producing two or more crops within the same space. However, such a system is characterized by competition between crops. To curb competition, strip cropping, an innovative way of growing crops using spatial arrangements that reduce competition can be used. Two forms of this system (two-row and four-row) are based on the reduction in the spacing of maize rows to open space for legumes to grow. Under two-row strip cropping, maize is planted into rip-lines opened in double rows (50cm apart) and a gap of 130cm is left in between the maize double rows where legumes will be planted. For four-row strip cropping four rows of maize alternate with four rows of a legume but the inter-row spacing of maize is reduced from the usual 90 cm to 45 cm. This narrowing and reduction in size increases the growing space for four rows of legumes.
title: Strip cropping is an improved intercropping strategy for smallholder farmers that capitalize on a better plant arrangement. Two types of strip cropping are common: Double-row strip cropping and four row strip cropping.

description:
The science-driven accelerator program for climate-smart agribusinesses focuses on scaling climate-smart agricultural innovations and strengthening the commercial capacity of private sector entities in the agricultural ecosystem. Designed with insights from private sector accelerators, the program supports companies with the potential to achieve both impact and commercial success. Operating in Zambia, it aims to expand the reach of climate-smart innovations and enhance the business capabilities of participating agribusinesses._x000D_
 _x000D_
The program concludes with a demo day, connecting agribusinesses to public, concessional, and private investors, as well as potential market partners, facilitating access to finance and market linkages. After two accelerator cohorts and a large-scale bootcamp, the importance of expanding the scientific network across underrepresented countries like Zambia, Zimbabwe, Uganda, and Malawi became clear. Additionally, fostering ongoing networking among founders with complementary value propositions has become a priority, enabling sustained collaboration and shared growth across programs.

description: The policy support program provides governments in East and Southern Africa (ESA) with context-specific recommendations to help improve their enabling environment for climate-resilient agricultural transformation. Specific interests are in sustainable crop intensification and diversification and agribusiness and value chain development, with attention to gender and youth empowerment. The program comprises two pillars: 1) national policy dialogues, which bring together governments, agribusinesses, donors, researchers, and civil society organizations to explore feasible policy and investment interventions, and 2) the ESA Policy Hub, which scales the key takeaways from dialogues to the regional level to tap opportunities arising from trade and regional integration of national economies. Moreover, the program consists of two main innovation bundles: One, the main bundle, is “long-term technical assistance to governments,” garnering results from crosscutting scientific research and national policy dialogues and taking into account climate shocks and stresses to inform policy-making. Two, a “demand-driven technical facility” is available to national actors (government agencies, farmers, and small- and medium-scale enterprises) and connects strategically selected enterprises with a high-impact potential to agribusiness accelerator programs. The program fosters strategic alliances between various innovation partners and works closely with governments to ensure mainstreaming of recommendations into policymaking and implementation.

description: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are increasingly used as one of the tools to build the evidence base on the effectiveness of complex interventions to address food systems. Researchers conducting RCTs of complex interventions face design and analytic challenges that are not fully addressed in existing guidelines. This leads to questions and confusion about how to conduct these trials and interpret their findings. Guidelines, co-authored by a Sustainable Healthy Diets researcher, were published in 2022 to address key topics of confusion including the number of outcomes that can be assessed, the definition and meaning of primary and secondary outcomes and whether to control for multiplicity. The guidance ensures that trials are conducted to the highest scientific standards while maximizing the evidence that can be extracted. In 2024, the teamed continued (but did not complete) efforts to disseminate this innovation and build capacity for use by researchers, funders, policymakers and others.
title: Guidance for conducting randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of complex interventions published to improve RCT design and the interpretation of results

description: The sustainable intensification initiatives of Southern Africa use Gliricidia sepium, a leguminous tree species which is well adapted to the environment for their sustainable intensification practices. The importance of this system is to grow the trees in hedge rows or as dispersed trees so that leaves can be utilized in a “chop and drop” fashion with limited labour needed for transporting the biomass from one plot to the other. The spatial arrangement also aims at keeping the competition as low as possible while reaping the benefits of the agro-forestry species. Maize-Gliricidia hedge-row and Maize-Gliricidia disbursed shading are the two main systems. In the first one, maize-legume rotations are planted at normal plant population, in addition, hedgerows of Gliricidia trees are planted in rows spaced 5 m apart with an in-row spacing of 1 m. In the second, the disbursed shading system aims at developing larger Gliricidia trees that provide shade, less competition and in addition some green leaves that can be applied to the soil after pruning every year. One tree is usually planted every 10 m in rows 5 m apart.
title: Gliricidia intercropping into maize cropping combines trees and crops to increase diversity, productivity, profitability, and environmental management. This is relevant for resource constrained smallholder farmers

description: Multistakeholder platforms were established organized around lead firms as major buyers of beans, linked to bean producers, and supported by other service providers such as finance, credit, information, research and extension, and policy support. PABRA and NARS provided initial facilitation for the establishment of the platforms. An assessment was conducted based on 227 women and 53 youth who actively participated in the bean business platforms across Rwanda, Cameroon, Madagascar, Tanzania, and Burundi between 2017 and 2023. Among the women and youth who participated, an average of 81% indicated that they were satisfied with the business platform indicator. The satisfaction levels were measured by the sampled individuals using a scale of one to five, with five being the highest, and were then converted to a percentage. In 2024, demonstration of the role of multistakeholder platforms in accelerating new variety dissemination and demonstrated the use of improved and certified seeds in Malawi.
title: Multistakeholder Platforms are networks designed to implement program interventions by bringing together critical actors to improve business ecosystems and incentivise actors in bean corridors

description:
As agricultural growth accelerates and food systems gain focus, the need for robust indicators to quantify the scale and composition of agri-food systems has become critical. Addressing this gap, we developed two pioneering indicators: AgGDP+ measures total value added within key agri-food system segments, while AgEMP+ tracks total employment, including informal and self-employment, with gender disaggregation. Utilizing data and statistical imputation, we provide consistent estimates at national, regional, and global levels for 2010–2019._x000D_
_x000D_
To continually improve, we plan to gather the most recent Input-Output Tables (IOTs), Supply Use Tables (SUTs), and other essential data to update and expand measurements to additional years. With new Social Accounting Matrices (SAMs), we aim to extend coverage to more countries. Complemented by an online dashboard offering open access, these indicators provide the foundation for evidence-based policy and analysis of agri-food systems.
title: Novel Indicators for an Agri-Food System Dashboard Empowering Evidence-Based Policy for Sustainable Growth

description: Governments and donors often request modeling analysis to help understand the immediate consequences of, for example, global crises or local shocks, such as droughts/floods, and inform the design of policy and investment responses. The Foresight and Rapid Response Modeling System (FARRMS) streamlines our global and national data and modeling systems so that we can more rapidly respond to these requests and increase the likelihood that policy actions are evidence-based. FARRMS was conceived of during our response to COVID and was substantially developed in response to the fallout from the Russia-Ukraine War. FARRMS was used in mid-2022 to analyze impacts of the global crises on a large number of developing countries, and to advise donor governments in their responses. The country studies were conducted together with local partners, including country-based CGIAR researchers. The country studies were updated/extended in late-2022 to analyze a global economic slowdown during 2023.
title: Foresight and Rapid Response Modeling System (FARRMS) is an on-demand modeling tool to analyze impact of global crises to advise donor government in responses.

description: This innovation revolves around the development of artificial insemination (AI) protocols that are adapted to low-input systems where central AI labs do not exist and where basic commodities are lacking. It aims at democratizing access to improved genetics for small ruminant farmers. The platform is a network of labs supporting the breeding programs in Ethiopia. The innovation resorts to co-investment with partners in low-infrastructure, mobile labs that are operational under remote, rural conditions. AI relies on the use of fully certified sires that are genetically superior. Vaccination against infectious diseases mitigates the risk for these sires to transmit diseases. Inseminated females are synchronized with prostaglandin-based protocols that yield clean estrus, are easy to use, cheaper and are adapted to breeds under inter- tropical and equatorial African condition. The fixed time AI protocol relies on the use of fresh, non-cooled semen that is collected, assessed, processed and subsequently packed and used.
title: Reproductive platform delivering services, such as fixed-time artificial insemination and sires’ certification, in sheep and goat Community-Based Breeding Program sites leading to genetic gain in small and medium-scale livestock systems.

description: The assessment of an experimental vaccine for the control of East Coast fever (ECF). Thelieria parva, the causative agent of ECF, is a killer parasite infecting cattle. The experimental vaccine is based on the use of nanoparticles to present and deliver p67C antigen. In future the vaccine will be developed by an animal health company and used by livestock keepers to significantly reduce morbidity and mortality in their cattle herds, with a focus on cattpe type parasites. The new technology will also validate the nanoparticle platform for the delivery of subunit vaccines for livestock.
title: An experimental vaccine for the control of East Coast Fever, developed in partnership with an animal health company and used by livestock keepers to reduce morbidity and mortality in herds.

description: We will develop improved gender-sensitive business models for beef-cattle artificial insemination (AI) service providers in Vietnam, with a focus on economic performance and social responsibility. This will support the creation of business opportunities for animal health-care workers (offering the AI services), resulting in income generation and diversification. An increased number of AI service providers, offering quality service and semen from farmer-preferred breeds, is also likely to impact positively on adoption rates of AI, in turn-lead leading to increased beef-cattle productivity and profitability of smallholder beef cattle enterprises. To date, participatory business-model studies have been completed, and a key constraint of lack of access to liquid nitrogen identified.  To address this, we are supporting interested AI service providers to formulate a co-operative including shared access to liquid nitrogen.

description: Failure to address constraints to livestock productivity and the growing risks from climate change and other shocks can limit productivity gains while putting sustainability at risk. Increasing yields through climate-smart interventions can, but may not always, contribute to lowering emissions intensities while enhancing livelihoods. It is therefore important to provide information to stakeholders about trade-offs and synergies between productivity, economics, gender & social equity, and environmental factors. So that they can be considered when developing and scaling livestock innovations and during policy making at national or regional level. In response to this challenge, we are developing a toolbox for scenario assessment that describes trade-offs and synergies associated with those scenarios at different scales. This decision-support system (integrating ex-ante modelling tools) helps researchers, development actors, donors, and governments to consider trade-offs between social, economic, and environmental outcomes at different scales during evidence-based planning of investments in livestock production.
title: Decision-support system to help researchers, development actors, donors and governments assess trade-offs between social, economic, and environmental outcomes at different scales, for evidence-based planning of investments in sustainable livestock production.

description: In 2022, common stage gates spanning the whole breeding pipeline and sub-pipeline segments of collaborative breeding networks were defined. They provide a framework to define the connection between teams along the germplasm development process in a systematic manner for more effective handover between breeding teams, including those in partner organizations. The stage gating is the basis for more clearly communicating individual team focus, success, and defining professional development strategies. During 2024 high-level skill sets were defined that drive the product development process in different stages. Insights help in identifying potential gaps, duplications, and reorganization opportunities, given that similar skill sets are repeated across centers, crops and locations. Participants in a crop lead meeting highlighted the need and intent to better leverage capabilities across centers, based on such understanding. Skill sets may also drive gender-differential preferences for professional roles. The approach supports the design of more inclusive career pathways.
title: Aligning standardized breeding pipeline processes and stage gates in Genetic Innovation with skill-sets of diverse teams required to execute vanguard breeding programs

description: Modern breeding organizations drive efficiency gain, opportunity identification, and operational effectiveness through the coordinated engagement of specialized teams and processes. In interaction with the other Genetic Innovation initiatives, this innovation builds upon the extended stage plan established and validated in 2022 and 2023. It comprises ten distinct stages from product concept and market segmentation to product launch. It includes an extended suppliers-inputs-process-outputs-customers (SIPOC) model that provides a high-level overview of the processes, defines the inputs needed, the supplier(s) of each input, the key processes at each stage, the outputs of the processes, and the customers of each output. The approach was socialized and promoted across CGIAR breeding teams and partners. Deep-dive sessions in 2024 show that 53% fully and 41% partially implemented harmonized stage gate terminology. The terminology is also used in interactions with partners. This development entails a significant step change for consistently aligning CGIAR breeding processes.
title: Aligning CGIAR breeding processes to a common, high level organizational structure create clarity of roles and contributions among the individual initiatives and teams to the overall breeding success

description: This institutional innovation seeks to define common, high-level terms and partnership standards for inclusion in standard agreements that outline the benefits and commitments of belonging to a regional crop improvement network. Currently, rules of engagement differ vastly amongst centers and projects, and indeed are often not well described. If successfully adopted, network membership agreements will enhance equitable and transparent partnership approaches and collaboration through: the use of common tools and services; germplasm, information, and data sharing; acknowledging contributions; input and participation in network decision-making; the adoption of a culture of continuous improvement, and others. Draft terms were reviewed in 2023 by the maize, root and tuber, and dryland crops networks. Feedback was used to update the agreement template and make it customizable for individual network needs. In 2024, the African root-tuber-banana networks were the first to endorse the common terms. The agreement was signed by CIP, IITA and 16 NARES.

description: The partnership strategy assesses historically grown partnership models and creates transparency on partner inclusion. In 2023, 55 regional crop improvement networks were defined based on discussions with CGIAR breeding programs. 26 of these networks are based in Africa. A country prioritization tool developed in 2022 that incorporates crop acreage, world bank income status and existing partnerships was deployed in 2023 with 22 crop x region breeding networks in Africa and 11 crop x region breeding networks outside of Africa. Network members were prioritized according to a three-tier system: Level 1, Level 2 and Spill Over. By 2024, more than 90% of all center-by-crops had categorized partner countries accordingly. The partnership strategy provides an objective approach for networks to prioritize their focus and investments in Level 1 and 2 countries, where the impact is likely to be greatest, whilst ensuring other countries have access to international public technologies.
title: Towards a partnership strategy for CGIAR collaborative breeding networks that promotes equitable and mutually beneficial partnership models and is considerate of the diversity of regions, crops and needs

description: The Breeding Portal is an authoritative platform that captures CGIAR-NARES collaborative breeding strategies and makes the data public through the Global Market Intelligence Platform (GloMIP). Users need have distinct levels of permissions to create, edit, or modify data, or change dataset status from Proposed to Active to Archived. Data sets include: Traits used, Target Product Profile pursued, Breeding Pipelines employed, Varieties released, Market Segments targeted, and (since 2024) Partnerships and level of collaboration established. description: Genetic Innovation is a large endeavor, involving 21 crops, a large number of staff, partners, funders and projects. In collaboration with Breeding Resources and Scriptoria Ltd UK, Accelerated Breeding implemented a Project Management Center (PMC), to make workplans transparent across the two initiatives and several non-pooled projects. It became obvious that uploading workplans by project attracts high transaction costs and does not facilitate cross-initiative/project learning, mostly because interventions are framed and clustered differently.  Therefore, a Program Management Platform (PMP) was developed and tested with 20 non-related workplans of a wide range of bilateral projects. It enabled alignment of all (100%) projects to a common results framework that e.g. could be applied to one or several Program or Accelerator Theory(-ies) of Change. The PMP received positive feedback because it makes the agenda transparent, enables cross-project/initiative learning, and reduces transaction costs. It could facilitate Program and Accelerator implementation effective 2025.
title: A Program Management Platform allows to align a programmatic agenda across initiatives and non-pooled projects, enabling Program-wide learning and reducing transaction costs for staff and research leaders

description: The Scaling Hub aspires to support scientists, private and public sectors, and development partners in Eastern and Southern Africa who are designing, funding and/or delivering agricultural innovations for the transformation of food, land, and water systems. Its mission is to contribute to sustainable impacts by providing a range of research, capacity development on responsible scaling, and other engagements to help increase the use of proven agricultural innovations. More specifically, the hub will (i) incubate proven agricultural innovations and accelerate their adoption by end-users through facilitation of public and private partnerships; (ii) Enhance capacities within CGIAR and with strategic partners to enable responsible and inclusive scaling of agricultural innovations; (iii) Generate and share practical and scientific knowledge on the scaling of agricultural innovations; and (iv) Provide data-driven insights on CGIAR innovations in ESA and make it easier for partners to identify collaboration opportunities with CGIAR in East and Southern Africa. (v) Provide practical tools and frameworks on how to implement responsible scaling for transformative impact.

description: Criteria defined for systematic identification of seed product market segments. The tool introduces eight criteria used to define the seed product market segments. The first three criteria (crop, material type and subregion) form the basic building blocks of the segmentation. Twenty-five crops are considered, some of which are specified by germplasm (e.g. spring and durum wheat). Material type distinguishes crops that are hybrid (hybrid maize, sorghum and rice, for example). The 10 subregions were derived from the seven CGIAR recognized regions.

description:
The innovation is a transformative leadership program for professionals working in the water, energy, food and environment (WEFE) sectors. Its aim is to create WEFE nexus champions to advance the uptake and implementation of people-centric WEFE approaches, while contributing to greater equality and social inclusion among professionals in these sectors. The program’s specific objectives are:_x000D_
1.	Develop the technical knowledge and analytical, advocacy, and negotiation skills of WEFE sector professionals on WEFE nexus approaches and their operationalization._x000D_
2.	Develop the transformational leadership capacity of women and men across WEFE sectors to participate meaningfully in nexus discourses, policy processes, decision-making, planning, and implementation._x000D_
3.	Develop strong and collaborative networks for co-developing and implementing WEFE nexus solutions._x000D_
4.	Capitalize on women professionals’ assets and develop a cadre of professionals aware of and able to address structural barriers to gender equality and social inclusion within the WEFE sectors._x000D_
The course is based on adult learning approaches, such as transformation and experiential learning, and including a mentorship element. Participants are professionals (with an emphasis on women) from government, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), civil society organizations (CSOs), natural resources management networks, and the private sector. Developed in Kathmandu, Nepal, the program is designed to be rolled out to the provinces and local levels and other geographies. The innovation was conceptualized and co-developed by GREAT International, Governance Lab, International Water Management Institute (IWMI), and the Alliance of Bioversity and CIAT (ABC).

description: This innovation contributes to the discussion on water-energy-food nexus that has remained at the forefront of development policymaking. Understanding the nexus between water, energy, and food security requires a well-customized model that traces the supply and use of water, energy, and land resources and their spatial allocation. The two-stage production nesting structure in the standard IFPRI Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) model is extended to a seven-stage nesting structure where various types of water (surface and groundwater) and various types of energy (hydro and non-hydro) are explicitly combined with irrigated land such that the close substitutability and complementarity between water, energy, and land are well captured. A disaggregated Social Accounting Matrix (SAM) that represents the agro-ecological specificity of agriculture and resource distribution (irrigation) is generated. The model and data are used to analyze the economywide effects of water and energy interventions in the face of climate change-induced weather variability. In 2024, the model was used to assess how agri-food system investments priorities in Ethiopia could change under climatic and world price risks. To analyze this, additional outcome indicators - including changes in poverty and diet quality – were introduced.
title: A disaggregated water-energy-food systems model to study the economywide effects of water and energy interventions in the face of climate change.

description: Food, land and water (FLW) systems face challenges from a host of interacting megatrends as well as local and regional drivers. These include changes in population, urbanization, income, inequality, migration, diets, technology, biodiversity, and climate. Many of these trends are themselves influenced by changes in FLW systems, interacting in complex ways that have important impacts on nutrition, poverty, equity, climate, and the environment.  To capture these complexities we need  among other things quantitative  tools that help us understand how, where and at what cost these complex  interactions are manifest across the food system at global and regional scales.  This innovation draws on CGIAR’s biophysical and socioeconomic expertise to enhance the IMPACT model by developing and enhancing specific modules to better understand FLW system outcomes under plausible future scenarios.
title: Enhanced biophysical and socioeconomic modeling tools to explore food, land and water system impacts and strategic policy options relevant for low- and middle- income countries

description: In Tanzania policy and legislation provides for the provision of certificates of customary rights of occupancy (CCROs). However commonly these are issued on an individual basis and challenges arise when trying to secure tenure for a group that shares resources. The Livestock and Climate Initiative has been working with the Government of Tanzania to pilot the provision of group CCROs to livestock keeper associations. In 2022 the first CCROs were issued to four villages in a shared grazing land cluster called OLENGAPA securing around 85,000 hectares of grazing land. In late 2024 another group CCRO was issued to the Amei village livestock keepers association to secure 50,588 hectares of shared grazing land benefiting 15,407 livestock keepers predominantly pastoralists. Amei is part of the four village cluster of villages making up the ALOLLE shared grazing land.

description: The Small Ruminant Tools for Rapid Assessment of Pastoral Systems (STRAPS) initiative supports sustainable sheep and goat production in pastoral systems by integrating traditional knowledge, modern breeding techniques and sustainable practices. Developed by the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), RECONCILE and the Baringo County Livestock Department, STRAPS provides four e-tools to assess three groups of actors in the value chain: pastoral communities, individual producers, service providers and market agents. Using the Open Data Kit platform, STRAPS generates actionable data to improve productivity, strengthen market links and address systemic challenges. By fostering an entrepreneurial ecosystem, the initiative enhances pastoralist livelihoods, boosts climate resilience and supports sustainable livestock systems in semi-arid regions.

description: Controlling banana aphids (Pentalonia nigronervosa) is key to mitigating the banana bunchy top virus (BBTV) spread, responsible for the lethal banana bunchy to disease of Musa spp. Assessing the aphid life cycle (nymphs to adult stage) on Musa cultivars helps determine genotype suitability and the influence of environmental conditions on the aphid life cycle, but studying this under field conditions is challenging. To address this, an in vitro protocol was developed using banana pseudostem and agar media in small plastic boxes under laboratory conditions. The protocol was validated for the aphid life cycle on four banana cultivars: Agbagba, Cavendish-Williams (CW), Grand-Naine (GN), and Bluggoe. Mean development times from nymph to adult were 8, 10.5, 12, and 13 days, respectively. Agbagba supported the highest aphid growth, while Bluggoe was the least suitable. This demonstrates the potential of the protocol to determine aphid life table under controlled conditions crucial for phenology modelling.
title: An in vitro protocol for the estimation of banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa) life cycle on Musa genotypes

description: The objective of this study was to assess the efficacy of seed treatments for eradicating bacteria from rice seed. We evaluated 2 synthetic (Team and Fluidioxinol) and two biological products (ANT FM 30P, RB-99TM or Antinfek 30P) using seed plating technique. Our findings show that Teams is still more efficacious, followed by Fluidioxonil, which corroborates the results obtained by Germplasm Health Unit at IITA. ANT FM 30P, RB-99TM were effective in eliminating bacteria but were not effective against seed-borne fungi. There is need to conduct further testing on additional fungicides to identify those that are deemed acceptable, considering that "Team chemical" has been banned in the European Union and other countries.
title: Validation of four novel chemicals for rice seed treatment

description: A major concern in the exchange of rice germplasm is the potential contamination of seeds with bacterial species. This contamination could have an effect not just on rice crops but also on other crops that are economically important. The integration of heat treatment with the use of fungicide is a viable and economical option that potentially targets both bacterial and fungal pathogens. In 2024, we carried on with heat treatment experiments, exposing seeds to temperatures between 50 and 70˚C  over different durations ranging from 3 to 20 days. Our study demonstrated that heat treatment at 60°C for three days effectively eliminated between 80 and 90% of the bacteria, offering a viable alternative to the use of bactericides, particularly when paired with fungicide (Teams) treatment.
title: Validation of heat treatment in combination with chemicals protocol for bacterial elimination in rice seed

description: Due to weather variability, chickpea pod borer on chickpea and green pea aphids are economically important insect pests.  Besides their economic damage, aphids play a role as virus vectors on food legumes. This study aimed to validate eco-friendly entomopathogenic fungi and essential oils (EOs) formulated with Chitosan+Tween against aphid under controlled and field conditions. Two entomopathogenic fungi (Beauveria bassiana- strain- SGSK and Verticillium lecanii- Strain-SPT-2-271) were tested under controlled and field conditions. The formulated EOs and entomopathogenic fungi were effective against green pea aphids on lentil and chickpea pod borer, respectively.  Entomopathogenic fungi and formulated EOs can be integrated in the management of pod borers and aphids as eco-friendly alternative pest management options in Morocco. The ecofriendly biopesticides will be demonstrated on large plots under farmer condition in 2024/25 cropping season.
title: Development and evaluation of eco-friendly biopesticides against aphids and pod borer of food legumes in Morocco

description: On farm- and on-station trials explore diverse forage types useful for strengthening crop livestock integration, diversification and intensification of smallholder farming systems in Malawi. Sensitization and improvement of quality roughages, can improve both biomass yield and quality, providing better nutrition for animals. Some forages, such as Brachiaria, are adapted to low rainfall and offer additional environmental benefits like  controlling soil erosion, reducing nitrogen loss, and sequestering carbon. Mucuna pruriens, another forage, serves as a cover crop but also has potential as livestock feed. Forage legumes, like Crotalaria, also fix nitrogen in the soil, enhancing soil fertility. Dual purpose maize and groundnut varieties can increase biomass yields and quality on croplands without compromising grain yield. Private sector interest in forages like Brachiaria and Crotalaria is growing, increasing seed availability. Mucuna pruriens is produced locally, further supporting sustainable livestock feed.
title: Improved Forage for Livestock Nutrition, Soil Fertility, and Sustainable Crop-Livestock Integration for smallholder farmers in Malaw

description: Climate change requires a more urgent approach to innovation and scaling, especially in food systems that are vulnerable to extremes weather events. Much of the critical work required to address these extremes through crop improvement is associated with high costs and risks, especially for private sector innovators and investors. In situations like this – where commercial incentives for innovation trail behind social value – there is scope for novel "pull" mechanisms to spur innovation. One such instrument is an Advance Market Commitment (AMC) for crop improvement. This convening explores the application of AMCs to design, develop, and deliver new varieties to farmers' fields in low-income countries. The convening explores the economics of AMCs for climate-resilience traits, responses from breeding programs, and the enabling policy environment required for AMCs to succeed.
title: Advance market commitments for climate-resilient traits in food crops for low-income countries: An expert convening

description: ACRE Africa, a Kenya-based crop insurance company, utilizes smartphone pictures of insured crops sent in by farmers to evaluate an insurance claim and determine appropriate compensation. Evaluating images for thousands of insured smallholder farmers to verify insurance claims is time-consuming, and this often slows down claims settlement. To this end, CGIAR Initiative on Digital Innovation launched a competitive data science challenge program to crowdsource machine learning models to automate claims settlement. Total of 833 data scientists participated in the 3-month challenge program hosted at the Zindi platform, and the best performing model, developed by Mohamed Abdelrazik from Egypt, was selected in December 2023.
title: "Eyes on the Ground Challenge": A competitive online crowdsourcing program for developing machine learning models to analyze smartphone crop images for enhanced crop insurance solutions

description: In Nigeria, processing cassava for food and industry yields around 15 million tons of wet peels annually. These peels are usually dumped near processing centres to rot or dry enough to be burned. Rotting heaps release methane into the air and a stinking effluent that pollutes nearby streams and underground water, while burning produces clouds of acrid smoke. However, when properly dried, peels can be an ingredient in animal feed. Previous attempts over two decades to use peels in animal feed failed to yield profitable options for drying wet peels at commercial scale, but recent research suggests that cassava peels can be processed into high-quality cassava peel (HQCP) products to be used as nutritious, low-cost animal feed ingredients by livestock feed suppliers and their customers (livestock-keepers)
title: Cassava peel as a nutritious animal feed for livestock feed suppliers and livestock-keepers

description:
The Initiative on Asian Mega Deltas (AMD) together with the Indian Council for Agricultural Research (ICAR) and local partners have developed land-shaping technologies by transforming the lowland rice landscape to overcome certain climatic hazards and improve land productivity. It also aims to provide rice farmers opportunities to improve their livelihoods during the dry season where water is scarce thereby enhancing livelihood security. Inland shaping, the surface of farmland is modified primarily for harvesting rainwater to create a source for irrigation especially during the dry season, reducing salinity and drainage congestion, and practicing integrated farming around the year. _x000D_
_x000D_
Currently, the land shaping technology is now being introduced in a small scale utilizing rice fields of 2 farmers for tirals. The trials are conducted to establish proof of concept and for further refining the design of the technology to ensure effectiveness and suitability to local and farmers' conditions.
title: Introduction of land shaping to farmers to harvest rainwater that can be used by rice farmers during the dry seasons in India

description: The Climate Security Sensitivity Tool is a 2-step user friendly tool to assess the peace potential of climate adaptation interventions. Peacekeeping and climate adaptation are rarely integrated in adaptation initiatives. The Climate Security Sensitivity Tool tries to close this gap by assessing whether climate action programs and their implementation are appropriate for the context in which they are carried out and recommending solutions to improve their appropriateness. It is aimed at practitioners, policymakers, and international organizations interested in diagnostic research for peace-responsive climate action in agricultural and rural development.

description: The use of the Human-Centered Design (HCD) approach improved the Agro-Climatic Bulletin (ACB), providing better quality, and consistency of advisories, and accessibility to farmers. This process focused on farmers for their practical use, and the Technical Working Groups from the district and provincial government for their development and dissemination of the ACB. The improvements include (1) an enhanced ACB template, in which practice cards are based on historical data, with expert inputs replacing manual recommendations; (2) a user-friendly design featuring icons, pictures, and a more engaging design and color scheme; and (3) supplementary training materials with new videos and guides integrated as QR codes within the ACB practice cards. By using separate practice cards, advisories can be tracked over time and across different locations, providing opportunities for further analysis, and improvement, and as a step towards ACB digitalisation.
title: Improving the the Agro-Climatic Bulletin (ACB) provided to farmers using human-centered design methods in the Vietnam Mekong Delta

description:
The Crop Decision Tree (CDT) is a supplementary tool for systematically developing seasonal Agro-Climatic Bulletins, which are based on forecasted rainfall scenarios for the entire growing season. As part of the Asia-Mega Initiative (AMD), the Alliance of Bioversity International & CIAT collaborated with the Department of Crop Production (DCP) and sub-DCPs across seven Mekong River Delta (MRD) provinces to develop CDTs for rice at regional and provincial levels. The provinces involved include Tien Giang, Hau Giang, Kien Giang, An Giang, Can Tho, Tra Vinh, and Soc Trang._x000D_
_x000D_
The development of CDTs was informed by historical seasonal Agro-Climatic Bulletins and the technical expertise of national and provincial agricultural experts. The CDTs consist of:_x000D_
•        A crop calendar detailing crop growth stages and associated climate risks._x000D_
•        Farming recommendations aligned with crop growth stages based on seasonal rainfall scenarios (above, normal, or below average)._x000D_
•        Farming advisories tailored to crop growth stages under extreme weather conditions.
title: Crop Decision Tree (CDT) for development of seasonal Agro-Climatic Bulletin (ACBs) for rice farmers in Mekong River Delta (MRD), Vietnam.

description: In the context of AMD-WP1 and aligning with the ongoing work on Agro-climatic Bulletin (ACB) development under AMD-WP3 in Vietnam, the project team from the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, in collaboration with the Dragon Institute at Can Tho University and the Department of Crop Production, developed online training materials for rice farmers in the Mekong River Delta. The goal is to provide high-quality, user-friendly e-learning materials. These will be disseminated through the Zalo messaging app, along with climate/practice advisory cards of the ACBs. To ensure the materials meet farmers' needs, six gender-segregated focus group discussions (FGDs) were conducted across three communes in Hau Giang and Soc Trang. These discussions identified the top ten agricultural practices that farmers find important yet challenging. The team reviewed existing training materials and created ten new technical resources, including blogs with images and videos, to offer practical guidance.

description:
The Climate Clever Check (CCC) tool, developed by Agriterra and the Alliance, is designed to integrate climate considerations into cooperative assessments. It provides an accessible, user-friendly way to evaluate climate impacts without the need for specialized knowledge. Unlike more complex tools, the CCC allows for quick, objective assessments by users without special technical expertise. The tool covers the key areas of Food and Agriculture Organizations (FAO)'s climate smart agricultural practices and helps cooperatives prioritize climate issues, identify risks, and design effective response strategies to protect both production and income_x000D_
_x000D_
Tested in four cooperatives in Mekong River Delta (MRD), the tool offers comprehensive climate assessments. While it works well for agricultural cooperatives, it needs improvements to be fully effective for fisheries and livestock cooperatives. Key upgrades include adding a universal climate risk index, adjusting the weighting of questions, and ensuring an even distribution of questions across categories to avoid bias.
title: Cooperative Climate Cleverness Check: Improvement and testing of tool to assess current farming practice of cooperatives and opportunities for climate smart agriculture

description: This CGIAR Initiative on Aquatic Foods: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) Strategy is intended for CGIAR scientists and development practitioners, project managers and Work Package (WP) leads working in the initiative. Other CGIAR initiatives will be encouraged to use the strategy to promote GESI in Aquatic Foods research and project cycle management, and in their engagements with policymakers. The goal is for the Strategy to help guide the work of collaborating partners and other stakeholders who engage with CGIAR, and other research and development organizations working to empower Aquatic foods smallholders. The purpose is to ensure that women, youth and marginalized people, and their families and communities, live better lives and engage in sustainable livelihoods through aquatic foods. Effective strategies for scaling gender equality and social inclusion will be developed through close partnerships with governments, research and development partners.

description: Fertilizer scarcity and high price coupled with climate change impact have necessitated the need for alternative fertilizers that are developed from locally available raw materials with less or no impact on the environment. Additionally, prolonged and recurrent draught also require a need to build a draught resistant soil. This innovation will therefore look at using of different organic waste materials to develop a fertilizer that would address the above challenges. In 2024, screening of organic materials and experiments were conducted to determine their suitability for fertilizer formulation—based on degradability, temperature resistance, and moisture retention.
title: Development of water storing fertilizer from agro-waste

description: Yam mosaic virus (YMV) transmitted by aphid vectors is the most important production constraint to seed and ware yam production in West Africa. Due to the lack of host resistance, protecting clean seed yams from YMV reinfection by aphids is crucial to prevent yield losses and seed degeneration. Trials were organized to identify methods to avoid YMV infection using two Dioscorea rotundata varieties. Approaches used include: (i) use of tall growing cereal as a barrier to interfere with aphid movement, and (ii) 3% (v/v) mineral (paraffin) oil sprays to prevent aphid feeding. The second-year trials in 2024 continued this model but only using insect-proof net instead of tall growing cereal as a barrier as mineral oil sprays were ineffective. YMV incidence increased from the first month after planting, with the highest incidence of 70% in control after three months. There is a delay in infection in protected plots.
title: Strategies for the management of seed yam reinfection and seed degeneration in seed yam production plots

description: This innovation entails the development of a salinity forecasting system for the 34/2p Khulna polder in the Ganges Delta, utilizing machine learning and deep learning techniques. The system will leverage readily available historical temporal datasets, including information on rainfall, groundwater level, groundwater quality, river salinity, river discharge, tidal height, land use/catchment characteristics, and water extraction patterns within the polder. These data, along with other pertinent co-variates, will serve as proxies to predict salinity levels. This predictive model aims to provide valuable insights to farmers, guiding them on the optimal timing to initiate their agricultural activities.
title: Creation of the Salinity Forecasting System: A Framework for Advancing Water Resource Sustainability and Climate Resilience through Local-scale Hydrological Modeling in the Ganges Delta

description: This innovation comprises a methodology that will enable seed producers of vegetatively propagated crop to self-declare the quality of their seed. The protocol will initially be tested with a group of 20 quality declared seed (QDS) producers of cassava in Tanzania. Seed producers will make use of digitial tools, including Seed Tracker and PlantVillage Nuru to help them to self-assess, and results will be sent electronically in real-time to the regulatory authority - the Tanzania Official Seed Certification Institute (TOSCI). Gender balance will be taken into account when selecting seed producers to participate in the experiment and gender will also be considered in the analysis of results.
title: Protocol for the Inspection and Certification of Quality Declared Seed (QDS) to be used by QDS producers themselves to self-declare the quality of their seed

description: Although potentially profitable, adopting an agroecologically upgraded business model is likely to impose restrictions to resource-poor entrepreneurs, especially small-scale producers and their organizations. Innovative and inclusive financial tools are essential to fill the funding gaps for the adoption of technological and institutional innovations that hamper the transitions to sustainable agrifood systems that go beyond the farm scale. Our innovation includes examples of the design and/or implementation of different innovative financial mechanisms that aim at increasing the access of small-scale producers and their organizations to funds for the adoption and scaling of agroecological practices and innovations.

description: IRRI genebank staff with private sector partners, have imaged thousands of rice seeds and panicles and generated data to train AI tool to discern seed morphological characteristics and identify rice accessions. The AI tool has been trained on 100,000 accessions and successfully identifying accessions with morphological distinctions. The tool is improving the efficiency in managing 130K rice collections and can also contribute to high-throughput phenotyping approaches. As a result of the AI tool development, the IRRI genebank won an award from Google in 2023 to refine the tool and use it to carry out a large-scale evaluation for tolerance to flooding, salinity and drought. Using the tool, over 60k IRG accessions were screened for abiotic stresses (drought, submergence, salinity).  Best accessions for these traits identified. By the end of 2024, >125,000 accessions imaged will be used for retraining the model to select the next batch of accessions for  abiotic screening.
title: Artificial intelligence tool developed to identify rice accessions in genebanks

description: The evidence synthesis collates evidence on how gender norms facilitate or hamper women’s abilities to achieve women's economic resilience in agrifood systems, specifically in the context of climate change.  In the synthesis, fifteen overarching gender norms which play out at individual, household and / or institutional levels that affect women’s economic resilience, are identified, and described. The synthesis covers the production domain of the agrifood system as well as the consumption domain.  Better understanding on how gender norms affect women’s ability to build economic resilience opens up opportunities for targeted gender-transformative development interventions. The evidence synthesis proposes an Economic Resilience Pathways Conceptual Framework that could be used to structure further research into women’s economic resilience in the face of climate change. As such this innovation might act as a guide for policymakers, practitioners, and stakeholders that are seeking to strengthen women's economic resilience in agrifood systems.
title: Pathways towards improved economic resilience for women in agrifood systems

description:
The NATURE+ Initiative aims to establish circular economy innovation hubs in target countries to create an ecosystem for innovation and entrepreneurship in circular economy. In Colombia, partnering strategically with Servicio Nacional de Aprendizaje (SENA), which operates 118 training centers nationwide, a decision was made to form a collaborative network (Recicle +) instead of creating a new center. This network includes SENA, circular economy businesses, and other key players, forming a supportive ecosystem. With the involvement of universities, research centers, incubators, accelerators, and private sector entities, the network aims to broaden its impact. This diverse collaboration seeks to cultivate a supportive environment, encouraging knowledge exchange, training, coaching, and the promotion of circular economy entrepreneurship._x000D_
In 2024, a number of activities have been organized such as innovation challenges, student hackathons, hands-on workshops have strengthened capacities in students, farmers, and local communities, encouraging sustainable practices.

description:
Water resource management in any basin, like the Limpopo River Basin with its intermittent supplies, is complex due to factors like rainfall, water allocation, quality, ecosystems, and risk to citizens. Balancing these factors often exceeds most managers' capabilities, despite the existence of numerous data sets. _x000D_
This project aims to develop a Digital Twin, a real-time, data-backed digital replica of the ground situation. Enhanced with machine learning and AI, it will integrate available data and models, providing easy and intuitive access to information. Grounded in real data, its outputs will be of tangible value, making it indispensable to water resource managers once fully developed.
title: Development of a Digital Twin for water resources management in the Limpopo River Basin in southern Africa

description: Labor scarcity, rising wage rate, drudgery are major problems in the Mixed Farming Systems in Bangladesh. Mechanization of agricultural production system is very limited. The increased mechanization of crop-livestock system is crucial to increase productivity, profitability, and sustainability of the Mixed Farming Systems. Given the dominance of smallholder farmers, small farm machines have huge scope in the Mixed Farming Systems of Bangladesh. The Initiative is testing small farm machines (fodder chopper, mini tiller, PTOS, reaper, mini rice mill, and oil extractor) as mechanization service provision by women and youth. In the model villages women and youth entrepreneurs have been supported with different types of small-scale agri-machinery. description: Most coffee and banana shade trees are slow growing – taking multiple years to provide needed shade levels. We are evaluating a novel tree – yellow jacaranda as a potential source of shade for coffee and possibly banana to improve the adaption to climate chnage. The tree is fast growing, nitrogen fixing and will thus improve nutrient recycling while offering shade for the crops. Its fast-growing nature [up to 5 meters in the first year] could allow for the needed shade levels for coffee to be obtained in a shorter time duration. The trees can produce branches at heights of over 10 meters if not pruned. Studies will also focus on their management [pruning and spacing] for attainment of the optimal branches and shade levels. As a global good, the tree will also improve carbon sequestration of the coffee-banana systems.

description: The Analysis tool for Economics of Land Degradation (ATELD) is an innovation that involves three separate but complementary modules each with specific function. The first module enables researchers and experts to estimate the quantities and monetary values of ecosystem services (ESS) lost due to inaction to combat land degradation (LD). If a package of suitable policy, institutional, and technological innovations for combating LD have been identified, the second module enables to estimate the benefits (in terms of the quantities and monetary values of ESS that can be prevented from being lost) due to the interventions. The third module estimates the cost of implementing the package of innovations,  total discounted benefits of action over the entire planning period, and ultimately provides estimates of the returns on investment that are provided in the form of benefit:cost ratios – i.e., the monetary values of the returns on every dollar invested in combating LD.

description:
This video was prepared by Travelling Tripod  in collaboration with the International Food Policy Research Institute to inspire rural women in Odisha State, India to publicly share with leaders their ideas for assets that might be constructed under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee (MGNREGA) program. The MGNREGA Act envisions a participatory, bottom-up process of choosing which asset will be built by allowing MGNREGA job card holders to recommend assets that would be useful to them at community meetings. Increasing women’s participation in the program is an important development goal for IFPRI and their partners in Odisha._x000D_
_x000D_
--_x000D_
This video was created to inspire women to participate in the Mahatma Ghandi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) program in Odisha, India. MGNREGA is the largest workfare program in the world and is both an employment guarantee scheme and a program by which communities propose and build assets to help improve their livelihoods. This video tells the stories of women who have successfully received assets and encourages women to request assets themselves._x000D_
_x000D_
The video is unique in that it tells detailed stories of women who have been successful in requesting and receiving assets under the MGNREGA program. It showcases women that are easy to relate to and provides specific advice and encouragement to women. Given the size of the scheme, the video can inspire women to improve their lives and livelihoods._x000D_
_x000D_
The video will be easy to scale. It is only 15 minutes long, and is accompanied by a discussion guide for implementers on what to discuss with women at various points during the video to spur engagement and discussions. It is inexpensive to show and it can be implemented by almost anyone within a community. Both the government and NGOs may find it useful as a resource. We also developed a 6-min version in 2024 based on feedback from stakeholders.
