description: The Enviro-Champs are the unsung young heroes of South Africa, bridging the crucial gap between nature and communities. Originating from the Mpophomeni township in KwaZulu-Natal, this initiative, under the Duzi-uMngeni Conservation Trust (DUCT), began by empowering local youth to monitor environmental issues like sewage leaks and illegal dumping. Their efforts quickly extended to tackling water leaks, improving waste management, and enhancing flood preparedness, addressing vital needs within the socio-ecological landscape of South Africa. Technological tools such as group text messaging and Excel for data management have bolstered their activities. Today, approximately 1,000 Enviro-Champs contribute significantly to environmental monitoring, ecological restoration, and food security efforts in KwaZulu-Natal. Their success in various regions showcases the initiative's potential for national expansion. Supported by UNICEF's youth upliftment initiative, YOMA, the Enviro-Champs program is poised for broader national and possibly international growth, demonstrating the power of youth engagement in environmental conservation.

description: Using Farmer Field School (FFS) model, the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) has successfully disseminated agricultural technologies across Bangladesh. But there is no significant adoption of improved technologies in 1.2 million hectares polder zone mainly because of prevailing hydrology that the FFS did not consider as the determinant in scaling innovations. The project identified water stagnation and waterlogging are the primary agronomic constraints, and that community coordination and cropping system synchronization is needed for wide-scale adoption of improved production systems. The “Cluster Farmer Field School (CFFS)” model was developed integrating water management groups with FFS to scale agronomic innovations managing hydrology of the coastal Bangladesh. This innovation was employed to strategically operate the sluice gates for water intake and drainage, aligning with high and low tides of the peripheral rivers of polder ecosystems during key intercultural operations in wet and dry seasons to 14 Learning Hubs in 2023 and 2024.
title: Cluster Farmer Field School (CFFS) Model for scaling agronomic innovations via strategic operation of sluice gates of polder systems in coastal Bangladesh

description: This innovation aims to support agrifood companies, Voluntary Sustainability Systems (VSS), and other actors involved in downstream nodes or supportive functions of agrifood supply chains and markets (e.g., in trade, research, policy and programming) to enhance gender equality and social inclusion in their supply chains. description: A systems perspective is crucial to understanding behavior change processes in agri-food systems transformations. Drawing from three existing frameworks, we developed a conceptual framework of agency and behavior change for agri-food system transformations. It is meant to go beyond the “technology transfer” paradigm in agri-food system research for development, to guide researchers and practitioners in a systems approach that improves understanding of what is enabling or impeding individual and group agency and behavior change in agri-food systems. The Agency and Behavior Change in Transforming agri-food systems (ACT) framework also enables a systematic approach to identifying and addressing gender, social inclusion and and power asymmetries. We expect that along with the use of this framework, more formative research will be conducted to understand food system actor experiences, constraints, and opportunity spaces. We expect the impact of this approach to research and action will be to more effectively achieve agency and behavior change targets, and resulting agri-food system transformations.

description: The vulnerability assessment (VA) framework is an approach used in mapping hotspot agricultural livelihoods of selected crops in the Asian Mega Deltas region. The framework was developed based on existing literature to identify the strengths and limitations of various VA approaches. Based on the developed framework, vulnerability is a function of three components: exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. Each of the three components is represented by a set of diverse indicators which is spatially aggregated into a shapefile to define a location-specific resolution as the unit of analysis. It is now currently being used by CG researchers to conduct their studies in uncontrolled environments and in designing their research projects. The framework is now integrated for adaptive capacity mapping innovation.

description: Tailored capacity building on circular bioeconomy models is provided to women and young individuals residing in urban and peri-urban areas. Specifically, women engaged in informal recycling activities such as biomass briquette production and sales receive hands-on training to improve their product quality. Moreover, they are trained on governance and group dynamics, co-creating and launching a sustainable business model that aligns with the local context. This innovation is being tested in Kenya, involving a cohort of 30 women who were informally and individually producing biomass briquettes in Kisumu's informal settlements. The aim is to empower women by enhancing their ability to produce high-quality briquettes, collaboratively develop a viable business model, and organize the group to produce and sell briquettes on a small and commercially viable scale. Post-training, the group is registered as a cooperative called Tich En Tich Makwangla Women's Group.

description:
Using the principles of Site-Specific Nutrient Management (SSNM), the International Rice Research Institute developed the Rice Crop Manager (RCM), an application that provides farmers with crop management recommendations tailored to their fields and rice growing conditions through the internet and text messages. In addition to nutrients, RCM also addresses other constraints that limit rice yield and farmers’ profit. These constraints can vary across areas, growing conditions, varieties and climate scenarios. _x000D_
_x000D_
For West Bengal, RCM will be developed for the rice growing farmers using secondary data on soil crop managemen characteristics to generate recommendations. To develop RCM algorithms, a yield-gain approach will be used to calculate nutrient rate to achieve a target yield, as a direct function of the estimated yield gain with added nutrient. The results nutrient omission plot technique (NOPT) trials will be used to customize and develop RCM with special focus on salinity management.

description: Farmer groups are core for improved farmers' access to input and output markets, as well as being a forum for capacity development and co-create of solutions to issues pertaining to pig and cattle keeping. However, the existing farmer groups engaged in cattle and pig production in the Mai Son district are not functioning well (regarding economic and financial sustainability, service offers, market connection, and trading capacity). description: The Decision support tool, using a multi-criteria decision method, is designed to assist decision-makers in selecting appropriate business models for Nature-Positive solutions in the context of circular bioeconomy. This tool makes a holistic assessment of interconnected objectives and the evaluation of alternatives while explicitly considering the priorities of various decision makers and stakeholders. It enables decision-makers and practitioners involved in the planning, implementing, and advocating circular economy initiatives to select appropriate circular economy business models that result in positive social, economic, and environmental outcomes. It uses a user-friendly interface where users can modify inputs and test scenarios and an interactive data visualization dashboard for result analysis.

description: Fecundity gene introgression has become an economical method to improve sheep prolificacy in developing countries. The innovation aims to increase the number of effective carriers of the mutation by the introgression of fecundity mutation into non-carrier conventional flocks based on a marker-assisted breeding program. The genotyping was carried out to follow up on the segregation of prolificacy mutation. The conventional, non-prolific ewes, were inseminated by carrier rams and yielded 100% carriers females at heterozygous state. These females were inseminated with conventional rams and produced carriers’ lambs with 66.7% males and 33.3% females. The prolific males are to be kept in breeding centers to disseminate the fecundity mutation in commercial flocks. The innovation was developed and tested in Tunisia and within Sustainable Animal Productivity (SAPLING) countries. It has the potential to be applied in Ethiopia, particularly in Bonga sheep, where a mutation linked to higher prolificacy has already been identified.

description: This innovation involves the establishment of the DTREO - Digital Genetic Data Base for Small Ruminants in Ethiopia, which has now expanded to other countries (East Africa and, Middle East and Northern Africa countries). The DTREO database is designed to be flexible and allows for the capture of reproduction details and performance data using smartphones or tablets operated by enumerators. It has the capability to function offline, enabling data to be saved locally and then synchronized with the cloud when connectivity is available. The data stored in the cloud is subsequently analyzed to rank animals based on their Estimated Breeding Value (EBV), and the feedback is shared with the community. Furthermore, the DTREO database serves to generate input data for genetic analysis. Presently, the DTREO database contains information on 134 thousand animals from 69 Community-based Breeding Program villages.

description:
Community conversations aim to advance equitable participation and decision‑making in locally-led adaptationprocesses to strengthen resilience. The approach draws upon concepts from locally led adaptation and practical insights from gender transformative approaches and was adapted to bolster equitable adaptation _x000D_
in Baringo County, Kenya. Four community conversations were held and were based upon priorities set by the community. Priorities included building capacities in diversification activities such as drought tolerant crop production, goat and chicken production, and group formation. Behavioral change was communicated through engaging media such as a co-developed drama and radio program, a photo gallery and interactive and participatory sessions. Reach per each conversation ranged from 254-339 individuals and women often comprised the majority. Baseline and a preliminary analysis of a midline show perception changes surrounding women's mobility. Men leaders' discussions and a gender dialogue enhance the potential of social change in household and communities to bolster resilience.

description: The Mungbean Interactive Voice Response (IVR) is a system that provides harvest alerts to mungbean farmers in Bangladesh. A business model for this digital application is required for sustaining it in longer term. In 2023, new business models for the system is supported. First model explored the Mungbean value chain to check if value chain actors like exporters are interested to cover the costs of their  farmers supplying mungbean to the exporter firm.  The second model is with microfinance that provides loans to farmers and developing a bundled model that provides the harvest warning as an add-on service to the loans for mungbean farmers. In 2024, microfinance institutions and private company agree to integrate the IVR in the provision of loans to farmers.

description: The use of improved forage seed in Tanzania remains a major challenge for developing of a strong and steady animal feed resource base and access to quality forages backed by a forage sector  and supply chain that assures availability of quality seeds/planting materials. This innovation aims to strangthen the regulatory framework to promote steady supply of certified forage seeds in Tanzania. To do this we are exploring use of trade Block approach i.e., East Africa where Tanzania and Kenyas are members.Two Brachiaira hybrids  (Cobra & Cayman) data had been procured from Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service and presented to Tanzania Official Seed Certification Institute (TOSCI) entity in Tanzania and will only need one season of growth to register them in Tanzania. If the route works, it will be shorter than the conventional National Performance Trials. Data available about the two varieties in Tanzania has also been presented to TOSCI.
title: Evidence based recommendations for policy makers and investors for a supportive regulatory framework for service providers including formalization of forage seed supplies in Tanzania.

description:
"Agvisely" is an agrometerological advisory tool that was developed and released in 2019 jointly by the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) and the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD). Currently, it provide advisories to farmers planting crops including rice, maize, and mungbean through an interactive website that can be access by extension agents to provide information to farmers in Bangladesh as a whole. The advisories are based on a automated 5-day weather forecasts using biological threshhold and forecast data. The tool aims to help the farmers to increase fertilizer use efficiency, irrigation management, and pest management leading to increase in yield and income. _x000D_

description:
The carbon footprint calculator tool for the rice value chain embeds product-scale emission information into a Quick Response (QR) code that can be displayed on the rice package for transparent tracking and tracing. _x000D_
_x000D_
The interface guides users through each step of the field management activities and post-harvest processing that are relevant for measuring the carbon footprint. A selection of default values have been provided based on empirical measurements from scientific experiments or sourced from scientific literature. It allows users the flexibility to enter their own measured values or values from literature that have not been included by default._x000D_
The output provides the carbon footprint from the individual stages of the value chain and allows for comparison across different management options for use as a decision tool.

description: This CGIAR innovation provides a comprehensive framework and set of tools for conceptualizing and measuring women's empowerment in governance, focusing on individual and collective agency beyond the household. Grounded in Kabeer’s empowerment framework, it highlights the interplay of resources, agency, and achievements at both individual and group levels. The toolkit operationalizes key concepts such as collective efficacy, action, and achievements, integrating tangible and intangible resources like social capital. Case studies from India, Guatemala, Uganda, and Nigeria illustrate its application, providing nuanced insights into how group dynamics, organizational structures, and decision-making processes shape empowerment outcomes. The innovation bridges gaps in understanding collective agency, offering participatory and mixed-method tools for analyzing women's roles in climate-related governance and other domains. By advancing measurement and application, this toolkit empowers practitioners, researchers, and policymakers to foster gender-equitable governance systems that enhance women's voice, agency, and community impact.

description: Cowpea is a among key legume crops grown in northern Ghana and it plays an important role in integrating crop-livestock farming system through provision of protein food for human consumption, fodder for livestock feed and biological nitrogen fixing for soil fertility improvement. Despite the contribution of cowpea fodder to livestock feed, national breeding program of cowpea in Ghana does not consider fodder quality as part of criteria for the release of improved cowpea varieties. Hence this innovation assesses the fodder quality in addition to grain production of improved cowpea varieties to determine the suitability of the improved cowpea varieties for crop-livestock farming system in northern Ghana.

description: Gender transformative approaches (GTAs) represent a powerful tool for addressing the root causes of women's disempowerment and gender inequality. GTAs facilitate critical reflection on gender and social norms, fostering transformative changes in harmful masculinities and societal norms, leading to better lives and livelihoods for women and youths, ownership of assets, and participation in decision-making. To maximize effectiveness, GTAs necessitate integration with technical innovations, offering solutions to both technical and social constraints. GTAs involve the use of experimental learning and capacity building, collective action and multistakeholder dialogue, and a blended learning approach. GTAs-related activities may include conducting comprehensive structural and intersectional gender analyses to comprehend the complex context and the multiple dimensions and layers of inequality and power. They may also involve engaging and enhancing the capacities of various stakeholders, including local actors, men, boys, women, community members, local organizations, traditional leaders, and policymakers, to drive and sustain the change process.

description: The African Asian Dairy Genetic Gain (AADGG) platform is an International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI)-led investment by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) that has been developed and tested in Ethiopia and Tanzania and scaled to Kenya, Uganda, Nepal, Nigeria, Zambia, Burundi and Rwanda. The platform uses on-farm performance information and basic genomic data to identify and promote wide use of appropriate superior purebred and cross-bred bulls for artificial insemination (AI) delivery and planned natural mating for smallholder farmers in Africa. The platform has different components: online and offline data capture system, data storage, analytics and genomic evaluation and selection of top ranked bulls and dams. The platform provides summary to enable informed decision and monitoring of progress. The platform has recently been revamped and a new digital application for capturing farm data in both cattle and buffalo developed and launched.

description: An internal Migration Propensity Index (i-MPI) was developed in 2023 for Guatemala and Honduras, aimed at predicting permanent domestic migration at the household level, following the methodology of the e-MPI (to predict cross-border migration) and adapting it to challenges specific to internal migration. The index relies on a concise set of simple, non invasive questions that are easy to collect and that combined best predict the probability that at least one individual from a household permanently migrates to a different community within the same country over the next 12-24 months. During 2024, the tool was validated completely out of sample (in a new panel household sample) and found to be both predictive of migration and outperform other indicators potentially related to migration. Such a tool can be used for both monitoring and targeting purposes to improve livelihoods at the local level and avoid the need to migrate.

description: Agribusinesses provide important linkages within value chains – linking farmers to product buyers and suppliers of productivity enhancing technologies, inputs, and services. Improving their performance, especially with respect to services they offer to farmers, therefore present significant opportunities. This is more so in a country like Tanzania where the private sector involvement in key commodity value chains remains weak despite the enormous potential of the value chains to improve smallholder access to inputs and services, incomes, food and nutrition security and create jobs. Some of the major current limitations to private sector growth include lack of knowledge and coordination among actors. Successful business training and coordination among actors have been shown to significantly increase the probability of success for both start-ups and established businesses. The “one network ecosystem" proposed here enables both.

description: The ODK-based surveillance tool was developed for the banana bunchy top virus (BBTV) surveillance to enable early detection, map the geographic spread of the virus, and deploy control measures. The tool also streamlines the minimum data set necessary for decision support and provides real-time access to data for the users and decision-makers. The tool was used to delimit surveys in Tanzania from 2022 to 23. The same was scaled in 2024 for use in Uganda and Zambia, and its use is continued in Tanzania and Nigeria to assess the BBTV status in over 300 locations in these four countries. Separate models were developed in Uganda and Zambia, and partners (Zambian Agricultural Research Institute - ZARI in Zambia and the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries - MAIFF in Uganda) were trained in the application. The tool is now being used independently by partners after one training session with users.

description: Cutting dipping in Mandiplus and application of neem oils significantly reduced adult whitefly numbers 45 – 74% compared to control. Mandiplus alone was the most effective at 74% followed by Mandiplus + neem oil (61%), TopNeem Ultra oil (50%) and crude neem oil in ethanol (45%). TopNeem Ultra and neem in ethanol had yield increases of 18 – 19% though these were not significantly different from the control.

description: This research aimed to determine if there are distinct features between virus-contaminated and normal seeds that could be used as a proxy marker for detecting virus-contaminated seed lots. Experiments were performed using a seed-transmissible virus species, bean common mosaic virus (BCMV), in 12 cowpea genotypes. The harvested seeds were sorted using the Videometer that provides precise measurements of seed color, shape, and size, including (i) normal size and seed coat color, (ii) normal size with seed coat discoloration, (iii) small size with no discoloration, and (iv) small size with discoloration. According to the categorization of seed features, 68.3% of BCMV seed transmission occurred through normal seeds. In contrast, 17.5%, 3.2%, and 11.1% of seed transmission rates were attributed to normal-sized discolored seeds, small-sized seeds without discoloration, and small-sized discolored seeds, respectively. Work is ongoing to validate more data parameters generated using Videometer to differentiate contaminated seeds.
title: Development of a non-invasive seed health testing protocols: standardization of Videometer multispectral Imaging for seed characterization

description: National Agricultural Research Institutes (NARIs) face challenges in correctly estimating the required amount of sweetpotato early generation seed (EGS) every season due to lack of information on adoption of improved seed and varieties by farmers and the negative effect of farmers’ use of planting materials of unknown health status. This makes it difficult for NARIs to fully sustain their EGS business. Therefore, a user-friendly tool to estimate the requirements for EGS was developed and automated using Excel & web based. description: The digital advisory is an online and SMS service system that effectively delivers early warning and real time information on production stressors and advises small-scale farmers accordingly. Spatially explicit and multi-scale satellite data and climate and pests/weeds data are uniquely combined in a digital platform, and accurate advisory information is then channeled to end users. For instance, farmers could be advised to plant less cereal crops this season because of anticipated Fall Armyworm infestation for a specific location. Reliable information about abiotic/biotic production constraints will prove critical in managing sustainable cropland productivity. In due time, cropping systems information such as fields are under mono- or mixed-cropping or if fields are irrigated/rainfed will be added in order to improve pest and climate risk forecasting. description: On-station studies conducted in eastern DR Congo, have shown cover crops including Mucuna to offer multiple services such as erosion control, soil health regeneration, weed management, soil moisture and temperature moderation within banana and coffee fields. These practices improve overall biomass production and crop yields and offer opportunities for livestock integration. These innovations have been tested and are currently being scaled. This will identify the best way to multiply the seed and is supporting validation trials and ongoing scaling efforts. Strategies will be explored for a more sustainable production of seed to support farmers.

description: Mercy Corps is collaborating with the Excellence in Agronomy initiative to develop agronomic advisory solutions aimed at benefiting over 300,000 smallholder farmers. This initiative focuses on creating gender- and youth-responsive agronomic solutions, covering soil health, crop productivity, climate change adaptation, and precision cropping system management. The collaboration involves digitizing specific value chain agronomic content for Nigeria, which will be disseminated through the MercyCorps Sprout platform. This digital content is designed to reach farmers via organizations and various communication channels. The first year of the project was dedicated to establishing partnerships, developing the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) tool, and outlining data and tool requirements along with prototype development. The second year focuses on validating and piloting the MVP to ensure its effectiveness and impact. This innovative approach seeks to sustain agricultural productivity and ecosystem services, adapt to climate change, and refine cropping system management solutions for smallholder farmers.

description: Index-based drought risk financing and insurance (IBDRFI) instruments have been designed to protect pastoralists in the face of drought. In all Index-based livestock insurance (IBLI) products,Normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) time series are elaborated to obtain an area-aggregated index of relative seasonal forage availability. When the index falls below a pre-defined threshold, payouts are triggered and increase proportionally to the severity of estimated forage scarcity. This assumes that, when forage is scarce, grazing resources are depleted quickly, leading to deteriorating livestock conditions and increased livestock mortality. Pastoralists could use the payouts to make production decisions that reduce their herd losses during the drought including, purchasing animal fodder, water or veterinary services. IBDRFI initiatives have been so far implemented in Africa with different modalities, including retail microinsurance products, macrolevel insurance schemes for social livelihood protection, or scalability mechanisms of social safety net programs.

description: The sustainable rangeland management (SRM) toolkit advocates for a holistic and participatory multi-stakeholder approach that emphasizes the important role played by governance of rangelands using bottom-up landscape restoration. It emphasizes the need to ensure that decisions are based on both indigenous knowledge and modern science to address site-specific challenges. The goal of the toolkit is to assist and prepare practitioners working closely with local communities perform proper diagnostic, plan, and implement specific interventions and continuously monitor and evaluate rehabilitation or restoration efforts. Users have access to a collection of validated SRM practices aimed at achieving a neutral level of degradation (LDN) and offering a strong potential to rehabilitate and restore degraded rangeland ecosystems. The case studies demonstrate step by step how the toolkit is used to identify practical solutions that are integrated and socially accepted leading towards more resilient livestock and pastoral systems.

description: Breeding programs in developing countries still cannot afford the new genotyping technologies, hindering their research. For it we have assembled an Association Mapping panel to serve as CGIAR Barley Breeding Toolbox (CBBT), especially for the Developing World. The germplasm set was designed to be representative of the varieties grown in the Developing World, with high genetic variability and of public domain. The CBBT preserves good balance between row-types and good representation of both phenology allelic combinations and subpopulations of a larger World collection. The CBBT lines and its 50K SNP genotypic data is available to researchers worldwide as a collaborative tool to underpin the genetic mechanisms of traits of interest for barley cultivation.

description: Participatory land use planning (PLUP) for pastoral areas overcomes many of the challenges of conventional land use planning including creating hard boundaries around villages or other administrative units, breaking up and limiting or preventing access to shared grazing lands and water points. PLUP for pastoral areas aims to keep rangelands and particularly grazing lands intact working across administrative boundaries through joint PLUP agreements strengthening reciprocal relations, collective tenure and good governance and resolving and preventing conflicts between land users. Pastoral communities traditionally marginalized from village PLUP process benefit particularly from the approach due to it being more inclusive of all land users in the planning and decision-making processes. The PLUP process includes the collection of data for assessing land potential most relevant for pastoral systems.

description: A framework(s) for improving large-scale land use change decision making processes in pastoral areas, particularly those related to commercial sector agricultural investments. Currently the frameworks used for such decision making do not take into account the full costs and benefits of the land use change from rangeland to e.g., crop farming including the full value of rangelands and their contribution to such as ecosystem services. This framework will endeavor to do this ensure a broader range of costs and benefits are included. The framework will be developed through a consultative process, tested with beneficiaries, decision makers, researchers and investors, to support the development of short- and long-term scenarios, the prioritization of interventions, and the design of supporting strategies, and policies. It is anticipated that the framework will be used by governments and other decision-makers concerned with land use planning and land investment decisions.

description: Milk production in developing countries is dominated by smallholder dairy farmers, each keeping 1-3 dairy cows. Majority of these farmers are not extracting optimum benefits, because herd and cow production and productivity levels are low. Small holder dairy farming is constrained by lack of sustainable breeding program that delivers adaptable high yielding dairy animals that suits the different production system, inadequate access to various services and inputs, and limited access to information or farmer education. The problem was addressed through innovative application of ICT and genomic technology.  The data generated is used to define more robust breeding objectives, develop realistic selection indices, and the information is ultimately used to select top ranking bulls and cows for breeding under local production conditions. The African Dairy Genetic Gains project has established a pipeline that harness performance data captured that incorporates genomic data for genomic prediction for milk yield and efficiency.
title: Genomic selection-based breeding programs for dairy cattle, based on performance records provided by farmers, linked to natural sire and artificial insemination-based delivery systems

description: The GeoAgro-MiSR system represents a powerful digital transformation that serves the national extension system, farmers, youth, and women, providing them with site-specific agronomic recommendations generated from farm analytics. EiA envisions a bottom-up and top-down synergy approach to agricultural transformation by leveraging digital tools and engaging stakeholders at different scales. At the grassroots level, the GeoAgro-MiSR smartphone application offers tailor-made agronomic advisories and services to smallholder farmers. It also facilitates citizen science by allowing users to contribute data to a centralized database. The GeoAgro-MiSR system comprises a centralized server hosted at ICARDA and two user interfaces: the GeoAgro-MiSR app and the GeoAgro-MiSR administrative dashboard. Communication between users and experts is via real-time interaction, including the "ask an expert" module and P2P chatting. The system also provides weather forecasts, remote sensing analytics for biophysical variability, and crop-specific agronomic practices.
title: GeoAgro-MiSR: A comprehensive digital solution that enables Egyptian small holder farmers achieve climate smartness, sustainable intensification and economic optimization under climate change and economic volatility

description: The WEAI ado file is a Stata user-written program that can calculate all versions of the Women's Empowerment in Agricultural Index (WEAI) depending on the options specified by the user. WEAI is a standardized, survey-based tool that has been widely used to track gender equality and measure empowerment, agency, and women's inclusion in the agricultural sector (Alkire et al. 2013). Since the WEAI's release in 2012, an abbreviated version of the WEAI (referred to as A-WEAI) and a project-level version of the WEAI (referred to as pro-WEAI) have been developed (Malapit et al. 2017; Malapit et al. 2019). The tool allows users to specify the binary adequacy indicators, empowerment cutoff, and indicator weights. WEAI provides a decomposition by indicator and, when specified, by sub-groups. Note that because the WEAI requires data from women and men, users are required to specify a variable (and values) identifying the sex of respondents.
title: Stata command file that simplifies the calculation of all versions of the Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (WEAI)

description: The IRRI-NARES Breeding Network is managed by a steering team comprising platform leaders, IRRI research unit leads, regional and modernization leads, and NARES coordinators. Their combined expertise helps shape strategies for implementing the network across different regions, ensuring alignment with breeding goals and agricultural priorities. Once the strategy and trial plans for NARES locations are established, IRRI’s network management team collaborates closely with breeding pipelines to oversee trial execution. This involves breeding pipeline leads, physiologists, pathologists, NARES coordinators, breeding and modernization leads, and seed systems experts working together to ensure efficient trial management and data-driven decision-making. This collaborative framework strengthens institutional governance, fosters knowledge exchange, builds capacity within NARES, and enhances relationship management. By leveraging expertise and shared resources, the network facilitates effective breeding strategies, broadens engagement, and drives agricultural innovation, ultimately contributing to more resilient and productive cropping systems in the region.

description: The methodology provides a framework for establishing field trials to assess the adaptability, productivity, and nutritional quality of commercial grasses under the climatic and soil conditions of Izabal, Guatemala. A pilot field trial was conducted in collaboration with a local livestock association and academia in the Izabal department, Guatemala. Experimental plots were established on both well-drained and poorly drained soils, testing eight commercial grasses, including hybrids of Urochloa and Megathyrsus maximus. Each treatment was replicated and included both technical and participatory evaluations by local livestock farmers. The results can provide key information for designing forage management strategies adapted to the climate and local conditions, to strengthen livestock productivity in the region.

description: This innovation offers a sustainable solution to the energy and nutritional challenges of cooking beans. Traditional methods require up to 2.6 kg of firewood for 1 kg of dry beans, contributing to deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions (Kajumba et al., 2022). Beans also take 3-4 hours to cook, limiting their use (Munthali et al., 2022). By boiling beans and using steam or pressure cooking, this innovation preserves nutrients like protein, fiber, and essential micronutrients while reducing anti-nutritional factors. After cooking, beans are dehydrated to extend shelf life, reduce food waste, and improve food security. The precooked and dehydrated beans cut cooking time and energy use, benefiting households by saving time and reducing the burden on women and youth. This cost-effective solution supports SMEs, improves nutrition, saves resources, and mitigates environmental impacts, with potential for wide-scale adoption in urban areas, contributing to food security and sustainability.
title: Empowering small-medium enterprises (SMEs) and Communities through Precooked and Dehydrated Bean Products: Enhancing Nutrition, Gender Equality, and Climate-Smart Solutions for Sustainable Growth and Social Impact

description: Sustainable food systems transformation requires multi-stakeholder processes. The current resources for the actors involved focus more on what needs to be done rather than how it can be done effectively. This qualitative methodology fills that gap and provides practical recommendations for supporting effective multi-stakeholder processes. It builds upon published frameworks and the building blocks assessment guide developed by the United Nations (UN), starting with five best practice principles for multi-stakeholder processes. It then assesses the compliance of the particular process to the principles based on a set of identified indicators, relying on a combination of desk review and interviews. The research team from Sustainable Healthy Diets applied the methodology to three recent food systems transformation processes in Honduras - creation of a national food systems profile, the 2021 dialogues to prepare for the UN Food System Summit, and the development of the Tegucigalpa Urban Food Policy Pact.
title: Methodology to assess the effective contribution of multi-stakeholder processes to food systems transformation applied in Honduras

description: Access to nutritious, affordable food can be challenging in emergency contexts. Traditional crisis responses often focus on staple crops to meet immediate needs, overlooking the nutrition and income opportunities offered by vegetable production. This toolkit seeks to fill that gap by providing practitioners with a variety of resources and tools to develop resilient irrigated vegetable projects in crisis settings. Vegetable irrigation is vital for nutrition and resilience, particularly as climate change and crises disrupt food systems. Designing and implementing efficient irrigation technologies and climate-smart practices reduces crop stress, boosts productivity, and strengthens resilience in the face of climate change. Investing in local irrigation solutions and supporting vegetable production helps vulnerable populations cope with humanitarian crises, sustaining their food, livelihood and nutrition security.

description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development designated Dong Thap and Son La provinces as pioneering provinces for subnational implementation of Viet Nam's National Action Plan for Food Systems Transformation (NAP-FST). To start, the provincial governments needed to create implementation plans with prioritized activities for their provinces. Sustainable Healthy Diets was invited to provide technical and coordination support to the provinces to meet this goal. An engagement process, comprised of several activities including capacity building, prioritization, and multi-stakeholder consultations, was designed and implemented in 2024. Recognizing the benefits of documenting the process for use in other provinces or even by other countries embarking on subnational implementation of their national action plans, Sustainable Healthy Diets has drafted a toolkit of resources for actors facilitating engagement activities that support subnational implementation of national/federal-level food systems transformation political processes. The toolkit will be further refined for dissemination in 2025.
title: Toolkit developed and piloted to support actors facilitating subnational implementation of the national action plan for food systems transformation in two provinces in Viet Nam

To start, the provincial governments needed to create implementation plans with prioritized activities for their provinces. Sustainable Healthy Diets was invited to provide technical and coordination support to the provinces to meet this goal. An engagement process, comprised of several activities including capacity building, prioritization, and multi-stakeholder consultations, was designed and implemented in 2024. Recognizing the benefits of documenting the process for use in other provinces or even by other countries embarking on subnational implementation of their national action plans, Sustainable Healthy Diets has drafted a toolkit of resources for actors facilitating engagement activities that support subnational implementation of national/federal-level food systems transformation political processes. The toolkit will be further refined for dissemination in 2025. Toolkit developed and piloted to support actors facilitating subnational implementation of the national action plan for food systems transformation in two provinces in Viet Nam

description: After launching an e-course on Food Systems Governance in 2022, key government partners of Sustainable Healthy Diets identified a need for follow-up trainings held face-to-face. A team from this Initiative and representatives from two government ministries agreed that the best way forward would be to jointly develop a new Training of Trainers (ToT) program on food systems. The ToT program will increase the pool of in-country experts that can facilitate learning processes on using food systems approaches. At the same time, the ToT program will complement the national policy processes for food systems transformation, like the Plan of Action that will be finalized in 2025, by filling identified gaps in awareness of how sustainable healthy diets can be achieved through food systems transformation and how to apply food systems approaches in these specific, and more general, policy processes.

description: This innovation development integrates seed fairs, field days, and farmer field schools into a dynamic framework promoting sustainable agriculture. Seed fairs celebrate agricultural heritage, offering farmers access to diverse seeds while fostering community engagement and partnerships. Field days demonstrate agroecological practices, providing hands-on learning and exposure to tools, techniques, and technologies in real-world settings. Farmer field schools equip stakeholders with skills in soil health, ecosystem restoration, and climate adaptation, fostering collaboration for resilient landscapes. Together, these activities create interactive platforms for knowledge exchange, innovation, and sustainable farming, emphasizing agroecology's role in economic and social development. The bundle strengthens local seed systems, highlights sustainable practices, and encourages partnerships among farmers, agribusinesses, and organizations, driving agroecological transitions, enhancing food security, and building climate-resilient landscapes.

description: The On-Farm Feed Advisor (OFA) App, originally developed on the Ionic framework, faced significant upgrade challenges due to deprecated libraries. To resolve this, the app was successfully migrated to React Native, incorporating enhancements to improve functionality and user experience. Additionally, a robust web application was developed, providing a comprehensive dashboard for seamless data management and parameter tracking. This effort was a collaborative achievement of the Digital Innovation (DI) and SAPLING Initiatives. The revamped mobile app and web dashboard are now fully operational and reintroduced to users with advanced features. The mobile app is available on both Google Play Store and iOS App Store, ensuring broader accessibility. Updated links to the app have been added under the evidence section.

description: The qZn5 Quantitative Trail Locus (QTL) was previously reported as contributing to grain zinc in rice, however validation was lacking and no elite material appeared to contain the gene. Deployment of this QTL into an elite background was completed, to a purity of >99.3% recovery of the elite genomic background.  Evaluation of the near-isogenic elite deployment products showed that qZn5 indeed does produce about 4ppm increase in grain zinc, which represents approximately a 40% improvement over the baseline level in the elite recurrent parent. The increase in grain zinc was apparent in milled, polished grain, so this represents zinc that would be available in rice consumed. Evaluation of the elite lines also showed no further penalty for yield (which was seen in early-generation products), so there are no penalties for breeders to use this QTL. The QTL interval was reduced by 90% to just 300kb/1.5cM.

description:
Diversity for Restoration (D4R) is a decision-support tool for the identification of appropriate tree species and seed sources for tree-based restoration or other tree planting activities. The tool has been adapted to support the integration of native tree species in production systems and land restoration in Northern Mountainous Region of Vietnam, to help enhance ecosystem service provision and rural livelihoods. The tool includes information on the distributions, uses and functional traits of over 80 local tree species from Northern Vietnam._x000D_
The tool is based on user inputs, allowing tailored recommendations for local land use objectives and site contexts. It provides recommendations of appropriate tree species that match the growth conditions on site, land use objectives, site-specific land degradation characteristics, and climate change predictions to help improve the resilience of production systems. _x000D_
The easy-to-use tool can be used by extension agents, other government agencies or development projects supporting farmers in nature-positive production.

description: A significant block to utilization of major genes in mainstream breeding is not only availability in one elite background, but in a diversity of elite backgrounds.  To enable easier use of genes conferring broad-spectrum blast resistance, a pyramid of 3 genes was backcrossed to 40 elite backgrounds nominated by the IRRI breeding programs.  In addition to selection for the main target genes, BC1F1, BC1F2 and BC1F3 materials were secondarily selected based on breeding value.  Resulting fixed lines consistently ranked in the top 50% of the current breeding cohort based on breeding value, and many were >1 standard deviation above the mean.
title: Pyramid of 3 blast genes conferring extremely broad-spectrum resistance has been introduced into 40 elite backgrounds from IRRI and AfricaRice breeding programs

description: The goal of food system dashboards is to offer users the opportunity to monitor or assess national food systems. One challenge is how to strike an acceptable balance between the complexity, specificity, and multi-sectoral nature of food systems while also ensuring that the information remains accessible and usable for decisionmakers. Rarely are these dashboards co-constructed with local stakeholders. This case study from Sustainable Healthy Diets describes how a replicable yet rigorous methodology for co-creating food system dashboards was applied in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, and Honduras. The three pilots demonstrate that it's feasible to integrate comprehensive and multi-sectoral inputs from national stakeholders into dashboards that are functional, evidence-based, and reflective of the country’s specific features. The methodology has the potential to progressively build capacities of decisionmakers to make more informed and evidence-based decisions to curb negative outcomes of food systems, like the triple burden of malnutrition.
title: Methodology for building participatory national food system monitoring dashboards tested with stakeholders in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, and Honduras

description: Currently there is no feasible indicator that assesses the diversity of foods that retailers offer to consumers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Researchers from Sustainable Healthy Diets have developed and validated a simple, cost-efficient, tool that can fill this methodological gap in food environment research. The Retail Diversity Index (RDI) measures the diversity of the retail food environments at two levels: at the food group level and at the outlet level. It also captures basic information regarding the level of processing of the food items available in these food outlets. To date, the tool has been validated across 374 food vendors in one urban and one peri-urban site in Viet Nam.
title: Retail Diversity Index: a tool to characterize the diversity of foods that retailers offer to consumers in urban and peri-urban food environments in Viet Nam

description: The affordability of sustainable nutritious food for all is an important dimension of food security. Timely, high-frequency indicators of food affordability are rarely collected in any systematic fashion despite the reality that food price volatility is a driver of food insecurity. Furthermore, even though development agencies have made investments in expanding food price monitoring, they have paid insufficient attention to monitoring wages and to measuring real food wages as a food security indicator. This innovation demonstrates how tracking wages of unskilled workers can be a timely, accurate, and cost-effective income proxy for monitoring food affordability for critical populations. The research team, including members of Sustainable Healthy Diets and Fruits and Vegetables for Sustainable Healthy Diets, apply the method using data from well-known food price crises in Ethiopia (2008, 2011 and 2022), Sri Lanka (2022) and Myanmar (2022).
title: Timely, accurate, and cost-effective means for high-frequency monitoring of both food affordability and security applied in Ethiopia, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka

description: Line augmentation aims to create a critical mass of elite material containing valuable new genes to enable simple and easy scaling through mainstream breeding. Augmentation workflows have been implemented in rice. At IRRI, a pyramid of 3 blast resistance genes (Pi9+Pi35+Pikh) has been completed into 40 elite backgrounds nominated by breeding programs. At AfricaRice augmentation has been initiated into 15 elite breeding lines for blast and rice yellow mottle virus resistance. Evaluation of breeding value of completed lines shows these match or exceed the original recipient breeding value.

description: Using Striga tolerant maize hybrids and a popular benchmark Striga-susceptible variety, we tested three options for Striga management in western Kenya through on-farm trials. The options were maize sole crop, maize intercropped with soybean and maize intercropped with Desmodium. Farms with heavy Striga infestation were chosen to host the trials. Eight farms were selected in three counties in western Kenya to host the trials. The trials were farmer-managed with researchers only collecting data at the critical stages. Data were collected on the number of Striga plants that had germinated in the plots and harvested field weight.  The differences in performance between the Striga tolerant hybrids and the commercial hybrid were very clear for both grain yield and Striga germination. A farmer field day was hosted at one of the sites and a flyer on Striga management were distributed to farmers.

After validation with stakeholders, a user-friendly online web-based interface will be developed to disseminate the innovation to its end-users. description: Supplemental irrigation is the practice of providing additional water to crops to support their survival, especially during periods of drought. Wheat cropping systems in Morocco and across much of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) are predominantly rainfed and vulnerable to poor crop yields or total failure with increasing rainfall variability and high-temperature extremes. Crop yield reduction or total loss can cause economic, social, agricultural, and food security challenges. In situations where supplemental irrigation is possible, irrigation scheduling is done through the in-situ measurement of soil moisture content at a depth of 90 cm. Irrigation water is applied through drippers when the available soil moisture content in the soil profile drops to 60 %. In drought years, the precise application of 28-166 mm supplemental irrigation (depending on drought severity) has been found to increase wheat productivity by 2-3 t ha-1 when compared to rainfed conditions.
title: Supplemental irrigation of wheat to mitigate productivity loss when the soil moisture content drops to 60% during periods of drought in rainfed cropping systems in Morocco and across MENA

description: The Reference Diet Deprivation (ReDD) index is estimated from household consumption survey data and measures the incidence, breadth, and depth of diet deprivation (the voluntary or involuntary shortfall in consumption) across multiple food groups. It can be used to compare diet quality across households or populations or track changes in diet quality over time. The advantage of the ReDD index is that it can be integrated into an economic model to examine changes in diet quality under different food and agriculture policy scenarios or external shocks. More recently, the ReDD index has been used as part of the underlying data for the Food Security Simulator, a tool for assessing the potential short-term impacts of food price or household income shocks on food security and people’s diets. It is showing to be a useful tool for researchers and decisionmakers to assess diet quality and examine the drivers of dietary change.
title: Reference Diet Deprivation (ReDD) index: a tool to measure diet quality and explore how policies are driving dietary change

description: A conducive enabling environment for agribusinesses is fundamental for African economies to grow rapidly. The unit for enabling environment technical assistance supports agribusinesses identified by agribusinesses acceleration programs to practice inclusive and sustainable agriculture, investment, value chain development, and trade, with a high impact potential: benefitting and creating employment for the disadvantaged and marginalized groups, including women, youth, and migrants, and fostering climate-resilient agriculture, climate adaptation, and sustainable natural resource management. This unit assists agribusinesses in three general clusters: (1) mapping, (2) networking, and (3) advocacy. The first two are “low-hanging fruits,” providing agribusinesses with research-based evidence on the policy, market, and regulatory environments to increase awareness and connect them with public and private actors for market expansion and overcoming bureaucratic bottlenecks. The advocacy cluster, a “high-hanging fruit,” seeks to drive regulatory change through collaboration with national governments, a long-term process, and links businesses with industry associations toward this goal.

description: This retail-level innovation was developed to address barriers in the affordability and acceptability of fruits and vegetables among low-income women in urban and peri-urban areas of Nigeria and Viet Nam. The intervention included a variety of strategies designed to improve: (1) the affordability through a coupon system; (2) the acceptability through a promotional campaign about the importance of eating fruits and vegetables every day; and (3) a combination of both through a loyalty card system and improvements in point of sales, product display, marketing, delivery of nutritional information to consumers, food safety, and customer service practices. The bundled intervention was implemented over twelve months and led to a marginal increase in the proportion of females consuming fruits and vegetables during the intervention period in both countries.

description: Various fish-based products have been introduced in communities in several countries in Africa and Asia by WorldFish and partners. In particular, dried fish powder that utilizes nutrient-dense small fish can contribute to making healthy, affordable, and sustainable diets more accessible for vulnerable communities in low- and middle-income countries. In Zambia, nutrient-enhanced complementary foods for Africa and dried fish powder (ComFA+Fish) products and recipes for enhanced nutrition, particularly for mothers and infants in vulnerable households, have been developed and tested with mothers, caregivers, small-scale fishers, fish processors, fish traders, the private sector, and government representatives. These include fortified chibwaba fisashi, kapenta chutney, fortified maize porridge, fortified bean-vegetable soup, fortified cassava bites, and fortified nutri-biscuits. The ComFA+Fish products have been widely accepted in the communities around Lake Kariba in Zambia and were recommended for scaling in communities where malnutrition is high.

description: Malnutrition is one the important cause of morbibity and mortality in the world and highest malnutrion levels are still found in Africa. School-age children are at high risk of nutrition deficiency. Here we develop and test a scalable model for integrating poultry product consumption (eggs) in school feeding programs in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Tanzania. By feeding an egg/day/child through a multi-sectorial collaboration approach we will improve school-age children’s nutrition outcomes. The effect of one egg/child/day will be assessed.  The project will establish a poultry farm in each of the selected schools compounds that will hold about 1200 layers and part of the eggs produced from this farm will be supplied to the existing school feeding program, while the remaining will be sold to the local community to cover production costs.
title: School-based model poultry farms for school-feeding programs to increase consumption of animal source foods (eggs) in primary schools.

description: The integrated Future Estimator for Emissions and Diets (iFEED) is an inclusive integrated assessment framework that combines climate-food-emissions modelling with land use dynamics, trade and nutrition analysis as well as expert judgement to develop policy recommendations towards a climate-resilient and nutrition-secure future. iFEED assesses both climate-smart agriculture and food and nutrient supplies under different climate change and policy scenarios. iFEED has been used in Malawi, South Africa, Tanzania, and Zambia. Through ClimBeR, iFEED is continuing to be developed in Zambia and is expanding to Kenya. iFEED is led by the University of Leeds (lead of ClimBeR Work Package 3) in collaboration with several partners, including the Food, Agriculture, and Natural Resources Policy Analysis Network, UK Met Office and other partners. A technical working group consisting of policymakers, researchers, and other stakeholders is engaged at every stage of the development process to ensure results are policy relevant.

description: The informed demand-led approach for the improvement of food safety comprises three key activities. First, reliable data on the level of food safety hazards or relevant production processes is collected across a set of foods within a category (for example, the level of aflatoxin in different types of grain or whole meal vs. refined flour; the hygiene practices of different vendors of fresh foods; the level of lead in different types of cookware). Second, this information is provided to consumers, who are expected to utilize the information to make safer choices. Third, additional rounds of information are collected at regular intervals (and again provided to consumers) to allow producers or markets with significant problems to benefit from corrective action. This approach aims to harness consumer demand for safer food to be translated into action, thus steering markets to provide safer food.

description: The innovation aims to identify which factors in the rural food environment or food markets influence access to and purchase of nutritious food for consumers living in poverty. The innovation revolves around the idea of spatial mapping and market surveys of the food environment. It involves geospatial mapping of different types of markets and retail food shops, conducting a market census and survey of the market and retail food environment, and finding the food availability and price of food in local markets. Building on the evidence, we explore if an improvement in the food environment (e.g. diversity of food, placement of food etc.) leads to improved access to nutritious food by consumers living in poverty.

description: A positive perception was observed among farmers growing vitamin A-rich bananas (pVABs) due to their early maturity, high provitamin A content, and long storage life. Adoption rates among initial beneficiaries were 45% in Gitega and 12% in Cibitoke. These rates were influenced by COVID-19 outbreak that hampered complementary innovations. Nevertheless, the willingness to adopt the pVABs was high (86-90%) across the sites. The adopters had expanded their areas under the pVABs. Diffusion from them to other farmers was also high e.g., two farmers reported sharing over 200 suckers with over 70 farmers in Gitega. Alternative uses including beer making had been invented by farmers. Scaling efforts have focused on establishing a robust seed system, engaging local leaders as influencers, and enhancing community awareness of the pVABs for reducing the high prevalence of vitamin A deficiency. Partnerships are being explored to leverage additional support for the promotion of adoption and use.

description: CGIAR researchers from Sustainable Healthy Diets with other academic partners developed a series of experiments to improve the quality of household food consumption data collected through surveys. The first experiment studied telescoping. Telescoping errors occur when respondents recall an event but their memory of the date of the event is inaccurate. In food consumption surveys, this means a respondent may report that their family ate eggs last week, but it might have been that they last ate eggs nine days ago (outside of the seven-day reference period). A second experiment studied whether food consumption data can be reliably collected over the phone. The experiments found that (1) telescoping leads to substantial overstatement of the consumption of high-nutrient foods and (2) survey data collection via phone leads to understatement of consumption. This innovation can be a valuable resource for researchers and policymakers keen to accurately measure sustainable healthy diets.
title: Results from survey experiments published to improve the quality of household food consumption data collected in Ethiopia

description: The innovation is end-to-end integrated system that combines citizen engagement for data curation with modern agile analytics to provide real-time and actionable insights about dietary patterns and food system dynamics. The system is made up of three components: citizen-powered high-frequency data collection, user-centered dashboard analytics, and demand-driven reflexive modeling of intervention options. The innovation stands out by leveraging crowdsourced data collection methods that are both cost-efficient and easily deployable, enabling more frequent and accurate insights compared to traditional in-person methods on diets, markets, and transport infrastructure. It aims to serve as scalable platform to engage, inform, and empower individuals and decision-makers; support data-driven and informed decision-making; and provide robust data to inform policies and interventions, direct capital investments to improve food system resilience, and increase preparedness/planning for potential and direct risk. It is already under development with diet quality, food flows, and transport network being mapped in Rwanda and Kenya.

description: Maize monocropping usually leads to soil nutrient mining, the prevalence of pests and diseases, and undiversified household nutrition. Diversification through either intercropping or crop rotation is a method that can be used to reverse these negatives. However, crop rotations are usually not feasible for farmers with small landholding sizes. For such farmers, intercropping is a viable solution. Intercropping is the practice of growing two or more crops in the same area, at the same time. In general, intercropping is better suited to farmers with small landholdings whereas crop rotation is more suitable for farmers with larger landholdings. However, other factors such as household needs and farm economics determine the choice of these two practices. The land equivalent ratio (LER) is often used to measure the benefits of intercropping compared to planting a single crop (sole cropping).
title: In maize-legume intercropping, two or more crops are grown simultaneously by smallholders in the same cropping season sharing the same piece of land. This practice reduces the risk of total crop failure and improves nutritional yields.

description: Conservation Agriculture (CA) is based on three key principles: minimum soil disturbance, provision of permanent soil cover and the use of rotations or associations amongst other good agriculture practices. These CA principles are applicable to a wide range of crop production systems from low-yielding, rainfed conditions to high-yielding, irrigated conditions. However, the techniques used may vary from place to place depending on farm power, system management conditions and farmer circumstances. Recent work conducted in Zambia showed that CA-based systems are capable of increasing economic and nutritional returns. The social and economic benefits gained from combining production and protecting the environment under CA are greater than those from production alone. CA in maize-legume systems addresses major production challenges in farming areas of Eastern and Southern Africa where both cereals and legumes are commonly grown.

description: Mbili Mbili intercropping system has been promoted as a crop diversification and intensification approach. Mbili-Mbili exploits plant spatial configurations to increase light penetration to the legumes, otherwise often shaded by cereals. The main aim is to increase legume productivity, while maintaining the same productivity of the cereal and taking advantage and complementarity of the different growth habits and durations of the combined crops. Mbili Mbili enables a farmer to grow both legumes and cereals on the same land and thus harvest at different times. In event of a loss, one crop serves as an insurance. This makes the system climate smart. Mbili Mbili system has been reported to have a higher returns (upto 37% more) compared to the standard farmer intercropping practices. The technology has been tested, and widely promoted in maize growing areas in Kenya and other countries in east and southern Africa.
title: Mbili Mbili is an innovative cropping system to ensure crop diversification and resilience in smallholder farming systems

description: Maize-legume rotations in Conservation Agriculture systems are an innovative method of reducing the build-up of pests and diseases and improve soil fertility and nutrition. Cereal-legume rotations are agriculture practices which are common and targeted to all farmers globally. Maize-legume rotations are traditonally practiced in areas where pest pressure is high and where soil fertility is limiting. Instead of growing just one crop (such as maize) in monoculture, the cereals are rotated with leguminous (cowpea, groundnuts, soybeans, common beans) or non leguminous crops (sunflower, cotton etc.) on an annual basis. As a good agriculture practice, this is essential for all farming, particularly in Conservation Agriculture systems.

description: Achieving food security and good nutrition requires coordinated action between multiple sectors, including agricultural production, food processing and marketing, health and hygiene, and cultural work to improve equity and knowledge. Food systems research, and the food environment concept, aim to make sense of this. It can be difficult to develop a comprehensive picture of a food system, and to identify the most influential leverage points. The framework, first is for the structuring of information regarding a local food system; second a participatory process in which stakeholders to develop a shared understanding and prioritisation of challenges within the food system; and third a searchable database of potential food security interventions which may be matched to the needs of a specific food system. The objective of the framework is to help sub-national decision makers operationalise food systems concepts, in order to tackle inadequate nutrition and food insecurity.
title: Food Security, Environments and Nutrition Framework: A decision support framework to identify and prioritise barriers and solutions for improved food security for use by decision makers at lower jurisdictional levels.

The objective of the framework is to help sub-national decision makers operationalise food systems concepts, in order to tackle inadequate nutrition and food insecurity. description: The digital advisory is an online and SMS service system that effectively delivers early warning and real time information on production stressors and advises small-scale farmers accordingly. Spatially explicit and multi-scale satellite data and climate and pests/weeds data are uniquely combined in a digital platform, and accurate advisory information is then channeled to end users. For instance, farmers could be advised to plant less cereal crops this season because of anticipated Fall Armyworm infestation for a specific location. Reliable information about abiotic/biotic production constraints will prove critical in managing sustainable cropland productivity. In due time, cropping systems information such as fields are under mono- or mixed-cropping or if fields are irrigated/rainfed will be added in order to improve pest and climate risk forecasting. The production constraints information over time can also be used to guide the scale out of climate and pest-smart agriculture, such conservation agriculture or the “push-pull” system.

description:
Dormancy-breaking treatments play a crucial role in enhancing seed germination and promoting seedling growth in Macroptilium and Clitoria species. In the case of Macroptilium species, it was observed that applying dry heat for a duration of 15 to 20 minutes significantly improved the germination percentage of seeds. Conversely, treatments involving concentrated sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) and hot water resulted in a notable increase in seed mortality. _x000D_
For Clitoria species, two effective scarification methods were identified: using sandpaper and soaking seeds in hot water for 4 minutes. These treatments helped to disrupt the seed coat, enhancing water penetration and promoting germination._x000D_
 In contrast, treating Clitoria seeds with H₂SO₄ for 10 minutes led to seed damage, even though it reduced the hardness of the seed coat. Untreated seeds in both species exhibited poor germination, remaining hard at the final evaluation highlighting the need to break dormancy for germination.
title: Breaking dormancy in Macroptilium and Clitoria species for routine viability monitoring of genebank collections

description: The ILRI Genebank houses a vast forage genetic pool that can be leveraged to address feed shortages and enhance farmers' resilience to climate change. However, traditional methods of forage characterization and screening have been expensive and time-consuming. To overcome this challenge, we have developed and applied genomic tools to accelerate the selection of optimal forage accessions and expedite the deployment of genebank materials for use by farmers. By utilizing DNA markers, we have identified core collections of forage species, including cowpea, lablab, Sesbania sesban, Rhodes grass, oats, Urochloa spp., buffel grass, and Napier grass. Consequently, candidate best-bet varieties were identified and prepared for national variety verification trials. The Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR) is evaluating the performance of the promising subsets to submit applications for the registration of new forage varieties in Ethiopia. This milestone provides livestock keepers with new forage options, improving feed supply, livestock productivity, and livelihoods.
title: Genomic tools for selecting and deploying best-bet forages for farmers use

description: The Water-Energy-Food Nexus Decision Support System (WEF Nexus DSS) is an advanced framework for addressing challenges in the WEF nexus, designed for policymakers, development practitioners, researchers, and other stakeholders involved in sustainable resource management. It integrates modelling, data analytics, and scenario-based assessments to support decision-making. Key innovations include surface and groundwater management integration, district-level typological mapping for irrigation planning (e.g., Ganges District Typologies), and tools like the WEF Trade-off Index (WEFTI) to assess sectoral trade-offs and synergies. The framework emphasizes policy convergence to enhance coherence, balance trade-offs, and maximize synergies. This approach enables national and local authorities, institutions, and researchers to make informed decisions, promoting resilience and sustainability in interconnected systems.

description: The agronomic and economic performances of an integrated rice-fish system were evaluated using a 1200 m² block subdivided into six plots of 120 m² each: a. a fish pond in the middle of the rice plot, b. rice monoculture with no fertilizer application, c. cultivating rice in the middle of the plot and raising fish around the rice, d. rice monoculture with the application of the recommended doses of fertilizers (NKP and urea). The fifth and sixth plots were in symbiotic association i.e., rice and fish were grown in two separate plots, and the water from the fishpond was used to fertilize the rice plot. The association of fish with rice significantly reduced the production cost by approximately 30-67% and enhanced both the profit (by 3-164%) and the producer’s income over rice monoculture.
title: Enhancing Productivity and Profitability: The Agronomic and Economic Benefits of Integrated Rice-Fish Farming Systems

description: School feeding programs reach approximately 368 million children globally and serve as a multifaceted intervention benefiting education, health, and nutrition. Despite these investments, there is limited data on diets and nutritional status of school-age children, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). For many reasons, monitoring the quality of school meal programs in LMICs remains challenging. This innovation builds on a collaboration that began in 2020 with CGIAR and the listed national partners from Viet Nam. (Its application in Ghana has been reported by Resilient Cities.) The collaboration developed the PlantVillage Food Recognition Assistance and Nudging Insights (FRANI) app, which offers a cost-effective solution for recognizing foods, providing consumption statistics, and estimating nutrient intakes in children and youth with accuracy comparable to professional dieticians but at a lower cost. In 2024, Sustainable Healthy Diets began a feasibility study to test how this innovation works in primary schools.
title: Feasibility of using an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted dietary assessment mobile app to characterize the quality of school meals and their contribution to children’s diets validated in Viet Nam

description: Diet quality is a major component of food and nutrition security across agrifood systems. Current priorities for sustainable development include the need for nutrition-sensitive agrifood systems, linking production with consumption and health outcomes for evidence-based impact of interventions and investments. Therefore, it is important to consistently assess diet quality over time and at varying geographic levels. To respond to this need, IITA and The Alliance Bioversity & CIAT have conducted a pilot study in 2024 to implement an innovative lean data system for monitoring dietary diversity in Nigeria, providing insights that can inform policy actions to improve nutrition and health outcomes in Nasarawa State. Specifically, the study aims to: (i) Develop a rapid data collection system for diet quality monitoring by incorporating lessons learned from previous efforts and ensuring alignment with the national context and (ii) Analyze diet quality trends across Nasarawa State over the data collection period.

description: As part of the TAFS-WCA initiative, Work Package 2 (Digital Agriculture) is piloting the Remote Sensing-based Information and Insurance for Crops in Emerging Economies (RIICE) tool (www.riice.org) for Bouake region in Cote d'Ivoire. This tool aims to support the government's endeavors to achieve rice self-sufficiency, through monitoring rice production at national scale. The preliminary activities have been conducted during the wet season 2023 over Bouake region using RIICE technology, in collaboration with IRRI, sarmap, AfricaRice, the Alliance of Bioversity - CIAT, and local partners.  The pilot activities were conducted to generate rice areas, Start-of-Season, Leaf Area Index (LAI), and end-of-season yield maps for the wet season 2023. In 2024 the plot continued with objectives to (i) generate Rice Baseline and Ecosystem Map, (ii) Generate Rice area-yield estimates for the main rice wet season 2023, (iii) conduct fields experiment, and to (iv) Validate the rice area-yield estimations.
