description: The Agroecology Initiative Kenya Work Package 1 team developed personalized soil data reports in an effort to provide actionable data feedback to the farmers who participated in the co-design cycle. Prior to establishing the first trials, the team took soil samples. Rather than only using the scientific insights to advise on appropriate soil health measures, the team developed a generic report format for each trial participant that allowed sharing the main information back with each farmer. The report is structured in four sections: (1) general introduction about the project, (2) farmers’ personal data including name, farmer group, ALL, trial focus area, and trial practice, (3) individual soil data report with individual results for 15 soil elements that are relevant for agricultural production, including pH, Soil Organic Carbon (%), Total Nitrogen (%), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K) – alongside interpretation guidance ranges, and related personalized interpretations (high; medium; low), and (4) a generic soil data interpretation and recommendations guidance section. The personalized reports were shared with each trial participant during a technical training and a general data feedback workshop session.
title: Personalized soil report for farmers in the Kiambu and Makueni County Agroecological Living Landscapes (ALLs) in Kenya

description: Brown rice hopper (BRH), a key insect pest to rice, is known can change its longevity and fecundity due to rising temperatures. Here we modeled the response of BRH population growth to temperature using an age-structured population growth model, based on reported responses of BRH development time, survival, and fecundity to temperature. We applied this model to predict the historical level of BRH population growth in the Mekong River Delta (MRD) and compared the predictions with historically observed percentages of rice fields infested by BRH. The model was able to capture the seasonal variation in BRH infestation and the optimal temperature for BRH activities (app. 26.5 degrees C). These results highlighted the importance of temperature in regulating BRH population growth. The model, with further improvements as discussed, could be used for projecting BRH activity under rising temperatures or predicting BRH outbreaks due to seasonal temperature anomalies

description: The research investigated methods to improve the germination of Cytisus proliferus seeds, a perennial legume with significant potential for livestock feed. Different scarification techniques were examined to effectively overcome seed dormancy. These methods included the use of sulfuric acid, to chemically break down the seed coat; boiling water, a thermal method to soften the outer layer; potassium nitrate solutions, to facilitate germination by penetrating the seed; and the excision of embryos, a physical approach to remove the embryo from the seed. Each of these techniques was assessed for its efficacy in promoting germination and improving seed viability.  Excised embryos and boiling water at 80 oC for 15-25 minutes were most effective at increasing germination percentages compared to other scarification methods. The study concludes by recommending optimized germination protocols for genebank viability monitoring of this species, prioritizing practical, less labor-intensive methods for broader application.
title: Optimization of the germination test protocol for viability monitoring of Cytisus proliferus seeds in genebank collections

description: The effect of cold acclimation on in vitro yacon plants prior to cryopreservation was assessed using a set of 28 accessions. Shoot tips excised from in vitro yacon plants, which were incubated for one week at 20 °C followed by two weeks at 7 °C (cold acclimation), showed a significantly higher full-plant recovery rate (67.5%) after thawing from liquid nitrogen (+LN) compared to shoot tips from in vitro plants grown for three weeks at 20 °C. It was decided that the assessed yacon protocol could immediately be applied for routine cryopreservation once the virus elimination process is complete.
title: Cryopreservation protocol for yacon developed and ready for implementation (average recovery rate >65%) once the accessions are tested to be disease free

description: The Local Technical Agroclimatic Committees (MTAs) were first developed in Colombia in 2014 to deliver tailored climate information to farmers, supporting them to adapt to climate variability and enhance resilience. The implementation emphasizes gender and social inclusion, ensuring equitable access to resources and information. This model represents a transformative approach to integrating localized climate services into rural development, driving resilience and sustainable agricultural practices in vulnerable communities.

description: A drying curve for pearl millet under the ICRISAT drying room conditions (150C and 15% RH) was developed to understand the drying pattern of pearl millet seeds. The purpose was to determine the time required for the seeds to reach the optimal moisture content for storage in Medium Term Storage (MTS) and Long Term Storage (LTS). It was found that pearl millet seeds take approximately two weeks to reach the target moisture content of 6-8% for MTS conservation, and about three weeks to achieve the target moisture content of less than 6% for LTS. This data will be re-validated in 2025 before being incorporated into the final conservation Standard Operating Procedure.
title: Improved protocol for drying pearl millet seed for long-term conservation

description: The forum theatre play titled "She Inherits, She Sells" was developed to engage entire communities in exploring, analysing, and solving the challenges faced by members of rural women's cooperatives in Morocco, rooted in societal gender norms. Using the 'Theatre of the Oppressed' format, the play begins with actors portraying  a scenario of oppression where the oppressed character(s) fail to overcome the challenges. The play then restarts, inviting audience members to participate as active 'spect-actors.' These participants can step into the roles of the oppressed character(s), attempting new strategies to overcome the oppression, and other characters met along the way whose responses may either support or resist these interventions. The format of the play brings to light the challenges individuals face due to societal norms and provides a platform for collective analysis, exploration, and practice of possible pathways towards liberation.

description: Unsafe food creates a cycle of disease and malnutrition, affecting infants, young children, elderly and the sick. Fresh foods, particularly, fruits, vegetables, and animal source foods, are both more nutritious and riskier from a food safety perspective. Researchers from Sustainable Healthy Diets and Resilient Cities are developing a scale to assess food safety experiences and concerns. The focus is not to objectively assess or quantify food safety risks or how nutritionally adequate diets are. Rather, this measure will capture the subjective food safety experiences and concerns of consumers and how consumers respond to these concerns in choosing their diets. By the end of 2024, the team completed the background research in three countries and identified an initial set of candidate scale items. The next phases of the project will refine the scale and field test it in surveys around the world.
title: Scale to assess food safety experiences and concerns of consumers in low- and middle-income countries in development to diagnose constraints to consumption of sustainable nutritious foods

description: The study evaluated the impact of hydropriming on the germination of five pigeonpea wild species: Cajanus cajanifolius, C. scarabaeoides, C. reticulatus, C. sericeus, and C. acutifolius. Seeds were scarified and soaked in four treatments: no soaking (T1), 12 hours (T2), 16 hours (T3), and 24 hours (T4), then sown in a glasshouse using a Completely Randomized Design. ANOVA showed significant effects of species, treatments, and their interactions. Among the species, C. sericeus showed the highest reduction in days to emergence (60%), while C. acutifolius showed the lowest (26.66%). The 16-hour soaking treatment (T3) was the most effective for improving germination. These results offer valuable insights for optimizing germination and using wild pigeonpea species in improvement programs.
title: Improved protocol for the germination of pigeonpea wild species

description:
Dietary assessment provides crucial data for understanding dietary patterns as a key driver of nutritional status and associated health outcomes in individuals and populations. Currently, little is known about the consumption patterns of aquatic Foods (AF) in Timor-Leste, particularly during the first 1000 days of life. Accurate dietary assessment of AFs is particularly challenging given the high diversity of fish, seaweed and marine invertebrate species consumed throughout the country’s coastal areas._x000D_
Together, WorldFish and CSIRO, with the support of the Directorate General of Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Resources of the Timor-Leste government, have developed a quantitative food frequency questionnaire FFQ designed specifically to capture aquatic food consumption in Timor-Leste in the first 1000 days of life. The approach includes a survey module and two visual aids to help participants accurately recall both the type and quantity of AF consumed: (1) a species identification tool and (2) a portion size estimation tool.
title: Measuring aquatic food consumption in the first 1000 days of life: An approach to estimating portion sizes in Timor-Leste

description: PCR (polymerase chain reaction) based methods are proven to be faster, cheaper and still highly effective methods for the detection of presence of bacteria in seeds compared to the traditional methods. In spite of the cons, such as the need of highly specific equipment and technical competence or the higher rate of false-positive results, these methods provide reliable and fast results allowing  the streamlining of end-to-end transboundary movement of seeds, with a lead time of 3-5 days as compared to 10-12 weeks. To attain the validation and verification of these highly specific methods, protocols require thorough evaluation under strict standards. The implementation of such methods and their cross validation with the national plant protection organization, will allow the Seed Health laboratory at IRRI to offer this service to researchers, partners and  external customers in the Philippines to enhance their capacity to import and export rice seeds.

description: The innovation aims to develop a digital crop map and forecasting map of vulnerable areas affected by salinity risks (Tien Giang province as pilots). description: The main contributor to anthropogenic nitrous oxide emissions is the utilization of agricultural nitrogen, with as much as half of the nitrogen applied through fertilizers being released into the atmosphere. To address this issue, the establishment of a monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) system is crucial for devising effective mitigation strategies. In response to this need, a practical MRV framework for monitoring nitrogen emissions from fertilizers is proposed, which can be readily adopted by farmers and local policymakers. Additionally, recommendations are provided for the implementation of a coordinated network to enhance the efficiency of such monitoring and mitigation efforts.

description: Quantifying GHG emissions and mitigation potential is important for all sectors of the economy including food systems for achieving the 2°C target outlined by the Paris Agreement. However, actions to reduce emissions from food systems have lagged behind other sectors. Investment and mitigation actions in the food sector have been constrained by the lack of policy-relevant and science-based methods for estimating GHG emissions and mitigation potential that contribute to decision-making. Most developing countries set their NDC (nationally Determined Contributions) targets through top-down aggregated estimates of national technical mitigation potentials, rather than the bottom-up information needed to inform implementation planning.

description: The One Health Unit (OHU) serves as a collaboration and coordination platform for frontline service providers and community-based actors to deliver integrated services to improve the health of humans, animals and the environment. In mobile OHUs, frontline service providers move along pastoralist/livestock routes, according to a monthly schedule, changing sites every day and responding to the needs of the population in a certain site/location. In static OHUs, frontline service providers work side by side in a common facility (e.g., human/animal health post, water point or other village gathering site). The OHU is generally staffed by government employees from different sectors who are released from their regular duties to deliver integrated services through the OHU. The services are targeted towards pastoralist and agropastoralist communities, their livestock, and the rangelands which they access, with a particular focus on vulnerable and hard-to-reach communities.

description: Leaf blast, neck blast and bacterial blight are the most important rice diseases. Simulation modelling will facilitate the identification of  risk factors, develop  management recommendations, and reduce yield losses under different climate change scenarios. Simulation models for leaf blast and bacterial blight were improved and neck blast was developed based on EPIRICE, a generic model for rice diseases. Infection rates were mainly driven by relative humidity, temperature, rainfall, and crop age. The values of parameters were based on field experiments, pest surveys and published literature. The coupling point for the leaf blast and neck blast models was a linear regression on the effect of leaf blast severity on neck blast incidence. Simulated levels of leaf blast severity, neck blast incidence and bacterial blight incidence were generally higher in the wet season than in the dry season. Additional research activities are necessary to improve the performance of the models.

description: A cluster-randomised proof-of-concept trial  in Dagoretti, Nairobi to evaluate the potential for a locally designed intervention to improve the food hygiene behaviours of caregivers living in a peri-urban, low-income area of Nairobi, Kenya. Fifty community health volunteers (CHVs) were selected and assigned, randomly, to intervention or control arm (1:1). 101 households (one caregiver/household) under the CHV’s catchment (2-3 per CHV), with at least one child aged 6-24 months, were selected for participation. Caregivers in the intervention group (n=50) received a CHV-delivered food hygiene intervention and those in the control group (n-51) received no intervention. Blinding was not possible. Follow-up was four weeks post intervention delivery. Our primary outcome was the proportion of caregivers observed to practice five pre-specified food hygiene behaviours. Secondary outcomes assessed these five observed behaviours individually as well as a sixth behaviour - the proportion of caregivers who report always boiling the child’s drinking water.
title: Urban Infant Foodscape Intervention designed to improve food hygiene behaviours among caregivers of young children living in low-income areas of Nairobi, Kenya

description: Vegetable adaptation trials are crucial for evaluating different varieties under specific growing conditions, aiding farmers in identifying the most suitable options for their region. In Tanzania, where peppers are an important income generating crop, FRESH core partner World Vegetable Center is conducting adaptation trials on 18 locally adapted pepper varieties - 6 chili peppers, 6 habanero peppers, and 6 sweet pepper varieties . These varieties were selected based on traits like yield, perceived disease resistance, and physical characteristics that may impact marketability. The adaptation trials have successfully identified promising pepper breeding lines outperforming the currently materials at three locations in Tanzania. The top-performing pepper varieties will progress to the World Vegetable Center's variety development process, contributing to the enhancement of crop productivity and quality in the region. The release of the habanero, bell pepper and chili varieties will be the first ever publicly released pepper varieties in Tanzania.

description: The sweetpotato whitefly, Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) MEAM1, is a globally distributed pest with a significant economic impact due to its ability to transmit numerous plant viruses. Understanding the temperature-dependent population growth is crucial for managing this pest effectively. Studies were conducted on B. tabaci MEAM1's development, mortality, and reproduction across seven constant temperatures (12° to 35°C). The Insect Life Cycle Modeling (ILCYM) software was employed to create a phenology model, predicting life-table parameters based on temperature. The model successfully predicted population development between 13.9 °C and 33.4°C, with the highest finite rate of increase observed at 26.4°C. Validated with field data, this model provides valuable insights into the species' potential distribution based on temperature, aiding in the design of pest management strategies globally.

description: Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) is an integral component of a decentralized, farmer-led seed system that aims to empower farmer groups with the collective authority to validate the standards of truthfully labeled seeds (TLS). Mainstream seed certification procedures require a licensed seed officer to verify the quality in accordance with the Indian Minimum Seed Standards and provide certification. Smallholder and women seed producers might not be able to adhere to or afford the stringent requirements of formal certification procedures. PGS transfers the responsibility of quality assurance and certification from government to Seed Growers’ Associations, that  facilitate the procurement of seed and provide their members advice on processes and practices. They certify the seeds produced by member farmers based on assessment of seed sources and production processes through regular inspection and record keeping. While promoting equity and diversity within the seed chain, the PGS also ensures that seed quality is preserved.

description: Access to seed of improved varieties holds the potential to transform the lives of farmers who use them. Efforts such as The African Seed Access Index (TASAI) are dedicated to mapping bottlenecks in the seed industry value chain.  However, to date these efforts have paid limited attention capturing data on access to quality seed by women and other unreached farmers. To fill this evidence gap, we have developed a set of 20 indicators that may be used by private sector, public sector, research and extension agencies, community seed banks to capture data on access to quality seeds of improved seeds by women and other vulnerable farmers. Survey questionnaires have been developed to capture the data and have been piloted in Uganda. These can now be used by other actors in other places with context-specific adaptations.
title: Indicators to measure access to seed by women and other vulnerable socio-economic farmer groups that can be used by seed producing and distributing agencies and researchers

description: In Colombia, the sector that contributes the most to national emissions is Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use (AFOLU), where the loss of natural forests for conversion to other land uses has a significant impact. Monitoring non-deforestation associated with agricultural and livestock supply chains at the farm level is a challenge. Therefore, one of the main challenges faced by the public-private initiative of the Zero Deforestation Agreements is to develop agile, cost-effective, and transparent tools and protocols to monitor compliance with non-deforestation commitments in these supply chains. The protocol developed serves as an implementation tool for the Zero Deforestation Agreements (ZDA) and can serve as a reference for other sectors and stakeholders, including the financial sector. The document provides a guide for information collection and the processes of MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification) of non-deforestation resulting from agricultural activities, thus contributing activity data to national inventories.
title: Measuring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) framework for monitoring deforestation emissions from Colombia

description: Farm to Market Alliance (FtMA) offers a platform to provide last mile service delivery to farmers in rural Tanzania via Farmer Service Centres. To realize this, the project seeks to establish a robust network of  farmer service centers scattered across six regions of Tanzania. Farmer service centers are grouped in three main categorizes; 1) Agricultural Marketing Cooperative Society (AMCOS), 2) Micro, Small and Medium Enterprize (MSME) led (comprising of agro-dealers, aggregators, processors etc.) and 3) Individual entrepreneurs (comprising of Village Based Agricultural Advisors/agents (VBAAs), lead farmers). Through the Farmer service centers and applying a demand led approach, farmer services that enhance smallholder productivity on farm can be accessed through facilitating linkages with input companies. These services include agricultural inputs, mechanization services, advisory, finance to mention but a few. The farmer service centers also double as aggregation hubs and link farmers to markets.

description: The highlands of North Shoa in Amhara region are dominated by cereals  followed by food legumes. The productivity of cereals and food legumes is low due to biotic and abiotic factors as well as insufficient input supplies like certified seed, inoculants and other inputs. Because of diseases and insect pests, acidity and water logging problems, farmers are reducing areas of food legumes and growing more cereals leading to low crop diversity, reduced soil fertility, incomes and food diversity. Several cereals, food legume and potato  varieties are released by many centers did not reach farmers due to limited demonstration to create awareness and demand and shortage of quality early generation seed. Moreover, popular varieties certified seed production is hampered due to shortage of breeder and pre-basic seeds of new and popular varieties from research centers. The poor access to quality seed contributes to low crop productivity and crop diversity.

The approach combines an integrated modeling approach on surface and groundwater interaction modeling with hydrochemical modeling to understand the factors influencing water and salinity dynamics. This comprehensive assessment will shed light on the area's unique environmental and hydrological conditions to gain insights into the factors that impact water and salinity dynamics within the specified polders. _x000D_

Governments, local agriculture and water authorities, and researchers are expected to benefit from the results and recommended strategies.

description: Clean seed movement (MCMV disease-free) from endemic countries is very critical for containing and preventing the spread of MLN.  A seed treatment protocol using TSP (10%) for removing MLN (especially MCMV) virus contamination from the seed is developed. A new seed treatment prototype with the capacity of 700 pouches (each with 200 kernels) has been designed. Over 7000 germplasm entries were decontaminated using the protocol, with less than 1% of treated samples showing positive for MCMV. The protocol was validated using a different set of MLN-contaminated grain samples. The protocol is being further refined in collaboration with KEPHIS, KALRO and Kenya Seed Company. A prototype with larger seed treatment capacity (0.5 ton) has been fabricated and will be further tested in 2025.

description: One of the important components for the sustainable and efficient management of MLN is to implement a digital tool/app for efficient data management with several partners. description: Using a custom-trained YOLO-v8 deep learning model, we expanded detection capabilities to include video analysis, enabling real-time disease identification. We successfully surveyed banana fields via drones, identifying healthy and Fusarium-infected plants. While further validation is needed, the most groundbreaking aspect is the establishment of a real-time disease detection pipeline using drones. Over 8,000 drone images from Fusarium-infected fields in Vietnam and Peru were analyzed. In 2024, we trained a YOLO-v9 model to differentiate between Banana Xanthomonas Wilt (BXW), Fusarium wilt, and healthy plants, using datasets from the Democratic Republic of Congo for Banana Xanthomonas Wilt and Vietnam for Fusarium wilt. The model achieved a mean average precision (mAP) between 68-80% across all categories foe YOLO-v9, with Faster R-CNN slightly outperforming YOLO-v9 for Fusarium detection.

National partner Agrosavia, La Selva branch, now hosts a partial safety duplicate of part of the cassava collection managed by CIAT. CIAT has purchased and maintains incubators at Agrosavia, which currently safeguards 4,280 accessions in nano culture, a technique developed at CIAT. In 2024, CIAT have been adjusting lightening conditions and long-distance monitoring of environmental conditions in the growth chamber with the in vitro nano cultures to optimize cultures longevity. CIAT will continue using this safety duplicate platform as part of routine operations going forward._x000D_
Nano-culture is a plant tissue culture technique in which cassava in vitro plantlets are cultivated under sterile, controlled conditions—regulated light, temperature, and photoperiod—within small containers (2 ml) at a slow growth rate. This technology enables the preservation of a large number of accessions in a minimal space. Additionally, it is a highly efficient method that requires less plant tissue as source material, reduces propagation time, and minimizes culture medium consumption due to the small container size.

description:
This activity examines product advancement processes across seven CGIAR centers and their national partners. The study assessed how agricultural products progress from breeding to market launch through interviews, standardized questionnaires, and observations of product advancement meetings. The evaluation covered diverse crop programs: CIP's potato breeding, IITA's soybean development, rice improvement at both IRRI and AfricaRice, CIMMYT's sorghum program, ICRISAT's groundnut breeding, and common bean advancement at the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT._x000D_
_x000D_
Key findings revealed varying adoption levels of the One CGIAR stage-gate process, highlighting the importance of partnerships, market segmentation, and Target Product Profiles. Challenges in licensing, seed production, and commercialization planning were identified. Recommendations focus on defining core activities, clarifying partner roles, implementing market-segment-focused breeding, and formalizing product advancement meetings to enhance efficiency across the CGIAR system.

description:
In Tunisia, some of the major constraints in crop-livestock production systems are monoculture of cereals leading to poor soil health and lack of nutrient rich forages for the key small ruminant activity. Forage seeds were insufficient, and no national seed company had been engaged in forage seed production as this wasn't considered beneficial to them._x000D_
In 2019, ICARDA and the National Institute of Agronomic Research of Tunisia – INRAT started a facilitation process for a Public-private partnerships through cooperation and engaging with COTUGRAIN, a private seed production and commercialization company. The partnership is set around the commercialization of some forage crop seeds, in addition to some forage mixtures (Vetch-Oat, Vetch-Triticale, Vetch-Oat - Triticale), pre-defined and advised by the research team composed of INRAT. Different formula for forage seed mixture were tested, recommendations were provided to the private company COTUGRAIN, to tailor its seed mixtures products for commercialization. _x000D_
Recently, Cotugrain acknowledged the integration of the co-design methodology into their projects, which has made it possible to create seed solutions adapted to new agroecological conditions. Cooperation with partners such as ICARDA has made it possible to increase the area cultivated with vetch and mixture seeds (ID 26 it doubles each year for mixture seeds it has gone from 10T to 30T to 80T), particularly for adaptation to changing climatic conditions. The enterprise has also strengthened its interactions with research institutions (INRAT, ICARDA) and has set up a tripartite agreement for the dissemination of adapted seeds and the application of agroecological practices on a larger scale"

description: A new soil leaching technique for use by farmers was trialled in newly reclaimed agricultural land in the Sinai Peninsula, Egypt, to improve water drainage and salt removal from the soil via leaching. By the end of the 90-day experiment, the creation across levelled fields of a structured network of (i) internal canals connecting from the external canal into the fields and (ii) parallel internal drains connecting from the fields into the external drain resulted in an 84% decrease in soil salinity and a 96% decrease in internal drain water salinity. These results indicate that this innovative soil leaching technique allows the water to infiltrate and flow more evenly through the soil, laterally and vertically, thereby efficiently removing salt deposits that have built up in the soil.
title: A new soil leaching technique of a network of internal canals and drains across levelled fields to reduce soil salinity in newly reclaimed lands in Egypt

description: The workflow outlines the processes and step-by step guide to manage and analyze data for yield gap decomposition by data scientists and analysts. It also includes concepts and definitions of yield levels, yield gap and yield gap decomposition and describes the analytical models for yield gap decomposition. Three main data-driven methods have been used for yield gap decomposition in agronomy research: (a) boundary line analysis, (b) stochastic frontier analysis, and (c) machine learning methods. The material documents how to implement these three methods in R are provided with reproducible examples. The R workflows have been used in analyzing data from surveys done by Use Cases in the Excellence in Agronomy to understand the factors causing yield gaps and to prioritize the development of agronomy solutions to close the yield gaps.

description: Despite women’s significant contributions to agri-food systems, positive stories about women’s roles are scarce in AFS discussions and media coverage. Dominating narratives often cast women as victims and patronize or misrepresent their roles and contributions. In this way, the currently dominant narratives about women’s role in AFS can be perceived as counterproductive, standing in the way of progress towards inclusive, equitable AFS. Therefore, there is a pressing need to collect, produce and share ‘better’ stories about women in AFS and agricultural solutions that work for women. In 2023 and 2024, the CGIAR GENDER Impact Platform organized three training programs, for science communicators from CGIAR and partners (as well as journalists) from around the world on how to prepare and publish stories on agricultural technologies that work for rural women. This training resource guide was developed as part of this series. Several stories are published in mainstream media outlets.

Through discussion-based stakeholder consultations, facilitated by trained researchers, the tool provides a structured approach to characterize and explore potential adaption solutions for specific crop production regions. As a first step, characterization data_x000D_
for climate challenges and production system characteristics should be aggregated; this helps ensure that discussions are focused on topics that require the wisdom of groups. It is also important to aggregate experimental evidence of the value of different technologies and management approaches to respond to the climate challenge. Following the workshop, areas of uncertainty and evidence gaps should be addressed to enhance initial results. Thereafter, a provisional set of priorities should be shared with a broader set of stakeholders to cross-validate results. As a last step, it is envisioned that results from the PAiCE tool will provide a strong foundation for climate change adaptation by steering investment and helping to coordinate the efforts of partners through action roadmap.
